therefore, where symptoms causing death arise in a patient during surgery, it may be possible to presume that such symptoms were caused by medical negligence by proving indirect facts from which it is difficult to see that there was any cause other than medical negligence for the occurrence of such symptoms (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on July 7, 2000, 99DA66328), but even in such a case, it cannot be allowed to vaguely presume, from circumstances that do not secure the degree of probability sufficient to infer the occurrence of a result caused by a physician’s negligence, a physician’s negligence and a causal relation therefrom based on a serious result, thereby effectively imposing on the physician the burden of proving absence of negligence (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on October 28, 2004, 2002DA45185).\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the court below, after comprehensively considering the admitted evidence and finding the facts as stated in its holding, determined that acute pancreatitis after an Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangio-Pancreatography (Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangio-Pancreatography, ERCP) examination can occur in about 5% of examination cases and can arise even in the absence of any special pathological condition, that no circumstances suggesting a problem were found during the ERCP examination course for the deceased Non-Party (hereinafter referred to as “the deceased”), and that, in light of the deceased’s condition at the time, it could not be said that the mechanism of acute pancreatitis was wholly absent in the deceased; accordingly, it was reasonable for the court below to conclude that, merely on the basis that acute pancreatitis occurred in the deceased after the ERCP examination, it was difficult to find negligence such as alleged by the Plaintiff on the part of the medical staff of the Defendant hospital in the course of that examination, and there is no illegality such as violation of the rules governing the assessment of evidence or erroneous understanding of the legal principles concerning the presumption of negligence in medical litigation, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. Concerning the Plaintiff’s second and fourth grounds of appeal\\n\\nA physician, in rendering medical treatment, has a considerable scope of discretion to select the method of treatment deemed appropriate according to the patient’s condition, the medical standards at the time, and the physician’s own knowledge and experience, and, so long as it does not exceed a reasonable scope, it cannot be said, merely by looking at the result of the treatment, that only one of the available methods was proper and that taking a different measure constituted negligence (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on May 12, 1992, 91DA23707).\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles, reviewing the record, although it is somewhat inappropriate that the court below, while rejecting the Plaintiffs’ contentions, referred to the possibility of impairment of kidney function, the court below’s determination that it is difficult to find negligence in the action of the medical staff who selected internal medical treatment for the deceased on the ground that the deceased was in a considerably serious condition at the time, showing multiple organ failure and being urgently transferred to the intensive care unit to begin emergency treatment, is reasonable, and there is no illegality such as factual error due to violation of the rules governing the assessment of evidence, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Concerning the Plaintiff’s third ground of appeal and the Defendant’s first and second grounds of appeal\\n\\na. Generally, where a physician performs a medical act involving invasion such as surgery on a patient and, in the process thereof and thereafter, performs a medical act with a likelihood of causing adverse results, or where a physician performs a medical act for which a serious result such as death is foreseeable, unless it is an emergency patient or there are other special circumstances, as a prerequisite under the treatment contract or for obtaining consent to the invasion, the physician has a duty to explain to the patient concerned or the patient’s legal representative matters that are deemed reasonable in light of the medical standards at the time, regarding the symptoms of the disease, the content and necessity of the treatment method, and the risks expected to arise, so that the patient may sufficiently compare the necessity and risks and choose whether to receive the medical act; and the physician’s duty to explain cannot be exempted merely because the likelihood of risks such as sequelae or side effects arising from the medical act is remote, and if such sequelae or side effects are typical risks inherent in the treatment act or are serious and irreversible, they are subject to explanation notwithstanding the remoteness of their occurrence (see Supreme Court Decisions rendered on January 20, 1995, 94DA3421, and on October 25, 2002, 2002DA48443, inter alia).\\n\\nMeanwhile, the duty to explain is a procedural measure necessarily required of a physician in the course of proceeding to invasive medical acts; in light of the seriousness of that duty, it appears that a physician has, at minimum, a necessity in the performance of duties to document and preserve the contents explained to the patient; moreover, under Article 9 of the Emergency Medical Services Act, Article 3 of the Enforcement Rule of the same Act, and [Form] 1, even in the case of emergency medical care, which requires more urgency than ordinary medical practice, the legal duty is imposed on medical personnel to explain the necessity of the medical act, the content of the medical act, the risks of the medical act, and to obtain consent in writing documenting such matters; in light of the fact that it is very easy for a physician to prove performance of the duty to explain by means of such a document, whereas it is, by its nature, extremely difficult for the patient side to prove that the duty to explain was not performed, it should be interpreted, absent special circumstances, that the physician side bears the burden of proving performance of the duty to explain, as this accords with the ideal of the damages compensation system, whose guiding principle is the equitable and reasonable allocation of losses, and with the requirement of uniform interpretation of the legal system.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles, reviewing the record, in this case where there is no evidence to establish that the medical staff of the Defendant hospital explained to the deceased the content of ERCP and the risks expected to arise, the court below, after admitting from the evidence cited the facts that, at the time, the Defendant hospital was in a situation where residents were on strike over the issue of separation of prescribing and dispensing of medicines, and that the nursing record concerning the deceased stated, “10/17 decided to perform ERCP without consent,” determined that the medical staff of the Defendant hospital had violated the duty to explain owed to the deceased; although there are somewhat inappropriate aspects in the reasoning, the conclusion is reasonable, and there is no illegality such as violation of the rules governing the assessment of evidence as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nb. Where a physician, in violation of the duty to explain, performs surgery or the like and a serious result such as death occurs to the patient, if the patient side claims only solatium for having lost the opportunity to choose and being unable to exercise the right of self-determination, it is sufficient to prove only that the opportunity to choose was lost due to the physician’s lack or insufficiency of explanation, and it is not necessary to prove the relation that, had an explanation been given, the result such as death would not have occurred; however, where the claim is for all damages resulting from that result, there must be an adequate causal relation between the serious result and the physician’s violation of the duty to explain or the fault in the process of obtaining consent, and the physician’s violation of the duty to explain in such case must be of such a degree as to be equated with a physician’s breach of the Duty of Care required in the concrete treatment process concerning the patient’s life and body, in light of the point that it is intended to protect the patient’s right of self-determination and the opportunity to choose medical treatment (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on April 15, 1994, 93DA60953).\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles, reviewing the record, in this case where it is recognized, as stated above, that the deceased lost the opportunity to choose due to the medical staff of the Defendant hospital’s violation of the duty to explain, the court below, after comprehensively considering the admitted evidence and finding the facts as stated in its holding, determined that the performance of the ERCP examination by the medical staff of the Defendant hospital, having judged that the deceased was in a condition requiring the ERCP examination, was reasonable in light of the deceased’s specific symptoms and the medical standards at the time; that there was no medical negligence on the part of the medical staff of the Defendant hospital in the course of the above examination or in the measures taken after acute pancreatitis occurred; that acute pancreatitis is a typical side effect accompanying the ERCP examination but its incidence is not high; and that the deceased had been hospitalized at the Defendant hospital for a planned two-week stay in order to determine the exact cause of jaundice; and on that basis, the court below concluded that it cannot be said that the deceased would necessarily have refused the above examination even if the medical staff of the Defendant hospital had fulfilled the duty to explain to the deceased before the ERCP examination at issue, and therefore limited the scope of the Defendant’s liability for damages to solatium for violation of the duty to explain rather than all damages resulting from the deceased’s death; this disposition is reasonable, and there is no basis to conclude that the amount of solatium recognized by the court below compensates not only for damage from infringement of the right of self-determination but also for mental suffering resulting from the deceased’s death; accordingly, there is no illegality such as violation of the rules governing the assessment of evidence, erroneous understanding of the legal principles concerning damages arising from violation of the duty to explain, or erroneous understanding of the legal principles concerning the calculation of solatium, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by each losing party. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the Disposition."}

{"[2020DA218925]": "We determine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Outline of the case\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below and the record, the following facts may be found.\\n\\na. Plaintiff 1 (then 11 years and 7 months old) visited Defendant Seoul National University Hospital (hereinafter referred to as the \"Defendant Hospital\") on 2016. 6. 17. for treatment of Moyamoya disease, and Plaintiff 2, the mother of Plaintiff 1, was informed by the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital that cerebral angiography (hereinafter referred to as \"the angiography in this case\") had to be performed as a preoperative examination before indirect bypass surgery for the treatment of Moyamoya disease.\\n\\nb. Plaintiff 1 was hospitalized in the Defendant Hospital on 2016. 6. 30. and, after undergoing the angiography in this case from around 09:00 to around 10:20 on 2016. 7. 1., was moved to the hospital room around 10:37.\\n\\nc. Plaintiff 1 began to show convulsive symptoms intermittently, pursing his/her lips, from around 12:02 on 2016. 7. 1.; the convulsions appeared to subside around 16:01, but convulsive symptoms appeared again around 16:20. Accordingly, a brain MRI examination was conducted around 17:26, and as a result, findings of acute cerebral infarction in the left middle cerebral artery were observed, so Plaintiff 1 was moved to the intensive care unit around 18:52 and received intensive treatment.\\n\\nd. Plaintiff 1 underwent indirect bypass surgery on 2016. 7. 13. and was discharged from the Defendant Hospital on 2016. 7. 20., but permanent right hemiplegia and deterioration of language function remained as residual disability.\\n\\n2. Determination on the Plaintiffs' grounds of appeal\\n\\nFor the reasons stated in its judgment, the court below determined that the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital had taken appropriate measures in the course of selecting and performing, or after performing, the angiography in this case, and thus found that there was no breach of the duty of care by the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital in relation to the occurrence of Plaintiff 1's cerebral infarction and residual disability, and therefore did not accept the Plaintiffs' claim for damages based on the medical staff's breach of the duty of care. It also did not accept Plaintiff 2's claim for damages based on breach of the duty to explain.\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the relevant legal principles and the record, the above determination by the court below is proper, and there is no error, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, in that it failed to fully examine the necessary matters, thereby exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in violation of the rules of logic and experience, or misapprehended the legal principles concerning the duty of care and the duty to explain in medical practice, thereby affecting the judgment.\\n\\n3. Determination on the Defendant's grounds of appeal\\n\\na. For the reasons stated in its judgment, the court below determined that, because the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital did not specifically explain to Plaintiff 1 the risks that could arise during or after the performance of the angiography in this case, they infringed Plaintiff 1's right to self-determination, and therefore held that consolation money should be paid therefor.\\n\\nb. However, the court below's determination is difficult to accept.\\n\\n1) Unless in the case of an emergency patient or other special circumstances, when a physician performs medical acts such as surgery that pose risks to the human body, the physician has the duty, as a prerequisite to obtaining consent thereto, to specifically explain to the patient matters that are considered important for decision-making in light of the medical standards at the time, concerning the symptoms of the disease, the content and necessity of the treatment method, and the expected risks and side effects to life and body, so as to give the patient an opportunity to decide on his or her own whether to undergo the medical act such as surgery (see Supreme Court Decision rendered on 1994. 4. 15., 93DA60953, Supreme Court Decision rendered on 2022. 1. 27., 2021DA265010, etc.).\\n\\n2) Article 24-2(1) and (2) of the Medical Service Act provides that, where a physician, dentist, or Korean medicine doctor performs surgery, transfusion, or general anesthesia that is likely to cause serious harm to a person's life or body, the physician, dentist, or Korean medicine doctor must explain to the patient, or to the patient's legal representative if the patient lacks decision-making capacity, the sequelae or side effects that are typically expected to arise from the surgery, etc., and obtain written consent thereto. In addition, Article 9(1) and (2) of the Emergency Medical Service Act provides that, where an emergency medical practitioner is required to provide emergency medical care to an emergency patient lacking decision-making capacity, if the emergency patient's legal representative accompanies the patient, the emergency medical practitioner must explain the emergency medical care to the legal representative and obtain consent; if the legal representative does not accompany the patient, the emergency medical practitioner must provide first aid after explaining it to the accompanying person. Furthermore, Article 16(1) and (2) of the Bioethics and Safety Act provides that, in conducting research involving human subjects, the researcher must obtain written consent from the research subject; in the case of research in which a child under 18 years of age under Article 3(1)18 of the Child Welfare Act, who lacks or has incomplete capacity to consent, participates, written consent from the legal representative, etc. must be obtained, and in such case the consent of the legal representative, etc. must not contravene the will of the research subject.\\n\\n3) a) In light of the purpose of the Medical Service Act and the related statutes, even if a patient is a minor, so long as the patient has decision-making capacity, the patient may have the right to self-determination regarding medical acts that pose risks to his or her body, and thus, in principle, a physician bears the duty to explain the medical act to a minor patient.\\n\\nb) However, a minor patient will often visit a hospital under the protection of a person with parental authority or a legal representative, hear the physician's explanation, and choose and consent to the medical act. In such a case, the physician's explanation is made to the person with parental authority or the legal representative, and it is common for the minor patient, while being present during the explanation, to hear its content or to accept the medical act by having the details of the medical act explained by the person with parental authority or the legal representative. For a minor who is not yet mentally or physically mature, it may be more desirable for the minor's welfare that the explanation be conveyed through a person with parental authority or a legal representative with whom the minor has a close relationship, rather than for the physician to always directly explain the medical act and have the minor make the choice. Therefore, if the physician has explained the medical act to the person with parental authority or legal representative of the minor patient, it may be deemed that the physician has fulfilled the duty to explain to the minor patient, insofar as such explanation is conveyed to the minor patient through the person with parental authority or legal representative.\\n\\nc) However, even if an explanation is given to the person with parental authority or legal representative, if it is clear that the explanation will not be conveyed to the minor and the minor's will will be excluded from the decision and performance of the medical act, or if there are special circumstances in which the physician needs to directly explain the medical act to the minor patient and obtain consent, such as where the minor patient actively expresses opposition to the medical act, it cannot be said that the physician has fulfilled the duty to explain merely by explaining to the person with parental authority or legal representative, and the physician must directly explain the medical act to the minor patient.\\n\\nd) Thus, where a physician bears the duty to directly explain to a minor patient, the physician must make the explanation in accordance with the minor patient's age and the degree of understanding the minor patient has regarding his or her disease.\\n\\n4) Examining the reasons of the judgment of the court below in light of the above legal principles and the record, the court below acknowledged that the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital explained the angiography in this case to Plaintiff 2 on 2016. 6. 30., and that Plaintiff 2 signed the consent form for the angiography in this case as the patient's proxy or guardian. If so, Plaintiff 1 was likely to have accepted the performance of the angiography in this case after hearing from Plaintiff 2 the explanation given by the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital, and may even have heard the explanation by the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital together with Plaintiff 2 at the time. If the circumstances are such, then, unless there are special circumstances, it may be deemed that the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital fulfilled the duty to explain to Plaintiff 1.\\n\\nc. In order for the court below to determine that the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital infringed Plaintiff 1's right to self-determination on the ground that they failed to fulfill the duty to explain regarding the angiography in this case, it should first have examined whether Plaintiff 1 had decision-making capacity to understand the meaning of the medical act and to choose and consent thereto; and if Plaintiff 1 was found to have such capacity, it should have examined whether there were special circumstances requiring direct explanation to Plaintiff 1 even though an explanation regarding the angiography in this case had been given to Plaintiff 2. Nevertheless, the court below, without conducting such examination, determined that the medical staff of the Defendant Hospital infringed Plaintiff 1's right to self-determination solely on the ground that there was no circumstance showing that the medical staff had directly explained it to Plaintiff 1. This determination by the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning a physician's duty to explain to a minor patient and by failing to fully examine the necessary matters.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal of the Defendant, we reverse the portion of the judgment of the court below that was unfavorable to the Defendant and remand this case to the court below for further trial and determination on that portion, and dismiss all of the Plaintiffs' appeals. It is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

question: Among the explanations concerning defective declarations of intent, which is correct? (Each statement is independent, and in case of dispute, according to case law)
A: In a non-genuine declaration of intent, “true intention” means the matter that the declarant genuinely wishes in his or her mind; therefore, if, at the time the declarant made a declaration of intent to make a gift under duress, the declarant’s true thought was latent in his or her mind that property would be forcibly taken away, then the gift declaration of intent lacks the internal intent to produce the effect of a gift and thus constitutes a non-genuine declaration of intent.
B: Where an act of contribution by written instrument is made for the establishment of a foundation juristic person, even if the juristic person is established and the contributed property becomes basic property, the act of contribution may be rescinded on the ground that it is a declaration of intent based on mistake.
C: In a real estate sale contract, if both the parties, A and B, intended land A to be the object of the contract, but made a mistake as to the lot number, etc. of that object and indicated the object as land B in the contract, then under normative interpretation the sale contract should first be regarded as having been concluded with respect to land B; however, seller A may rescind the above sale contract on the ground of mistake.
D: After A assigned to C a claim for return of lease deposit against B, creditor D of C obtained an order of seizure and collection with respect to the above claim for return of lease deposit, and if the assignment contract for the claim for return of lease deposit is a collusive false declaration of intent and therefore void, then because D is merely a person who acquired the collection right concerning the above claim for return of lease deposit, B may assert against D that the above assignment contract is a collusive false declaration of intent and therefore void, regardless of whether D acted in good faith with respect to the collusive false declaration of intent.
E: If, under the mistaken belief that, if a restitution lawsuit is brought, the real property would have to be returned without receiving any compensation, one enters into a sale contract to sell it, this is merely a mistake as to motive; therefore, only if there is an agreement to make that motive part of the contents of the declaration of intent may the seller rescind the above sale contract on the ground of mistake.
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[2013DA59753]": "The grounds of appeal (the matters stated in the supplemental statement of grounds of appeal submitted after the period for filing the petition of appeal has expired, only to the extent that they supplement the grounds of appeal) are examined.\\n\\nAs a principle, a false manifestation of intention made in collusion with the other party is void, and anyone may assert its invalidity; however, as against a bona fide third party who, other than the parties to the false manifestation and their universal successors, has entered into a new legal relationship in substance on the basis of the legal relationship outwardly formed by the false manifestation, neither the parties to the false manifestation nor anyone else may assert the invalidity of the false manifestation. The purpose of preventing a false manifestation from being asserted against a bona fide third party is to protect a person who, on that basis, has entered into a legal relationship and acquired a proprietary legal interest under a separate legal cause; the scope of the third party should not be determined formally only on the basis of the rights relationship, but should be determined substantively according to whether the person entered into a new legal relationship in substance on the basis of the act of false manifestation (see Supreme Court Decision 99DA51258, decided July 6, 2000). Accordingly, where, after a claim for return of a lease deposit has been assigned, a creditor of the assignee obtained an order of attachment and collection with respect to the claim for return of the lease deposit, and the assignment contract of the claim for return of the lease deposit is void as a false manifestation, that creditor must be deemed to fall within a third party who has entered into a new legal relationship in substance on the basis of the legal relationship outwardly formed thereby.\\n\\nAccording to the reasoning of the lower court judgment, the lower court determined that the Plaintiff, merely being the general creditor of Nonparty 1, the sham assignee of the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue, and a person who acquired the right of collection by obtaining an order of attachment and collection with respect to the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue from the sham assignee for the collection of its fee claim, does not fall within the third party under Article 108(2) of the Civil Act.\\n\\nHowever, the lower court’s determination is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nAccording to the reasoning of the lower court judgment and the record, it can be seen that the Defendant leased the building at issue to Nonparty 2 on February 4, 2008, setting the lease deposit at KRW 65,000,000, etc.; that Nonparty 2 and Nonparty 1 agreed to execute a contract formally assigning the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue to Nonparty 1 without any actual intent to assign it, and notified the Defendant of the assignment on December 10, 2008; and that the Plaintiff, on January 7, 2011, obtained an order of attachment and collection with respect to the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue assigned by Nonparty 1, based on the authenticated copy of the judgment in the fee case against Nonparty 1, and that the order was served on the Defendant on May 18, 2011.\\n\\nIf the factual relationship is as above, then in light of the foregoing legal principles, the Plaintiff, under the assignment contract of the claim for return of the lease deposit at issue made by a collusive false manifestation, has come to have a new legal interest in substance on the basis of the legal relationship outwardly formed, and thus must be deemed to fall within the third party under Article 108(2) of the Civil Act.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower court, without examining or determining whether the Plaintiff acted in good faith with respect to the collusive false manifestation, determined for the above reasons that the Plaintiff does not fall within the bona fide third party prescribed in Article 108(2) of the Civil Act; in so doing, it erred by misapprehending the legal principles concerning third parties in cases of collusive false manifestation and by failing to conduct a complete examination, and such error affected the judgment. The ground of appeal pointing this out is well taken.\\n\\nTherefore, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, the lower court judgment is reversed and the case is remanded to the lower court for further trial and determination; it is so adjudged as per the disposition, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}
{"[88DAKA31507]": "The appeal is dismissed.\\nThe costs of appeal shall be borne by the Plaintiff."}

{"[98DA9045]": "We determine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. As to Points 1, 2, and 3\\n\\nCivil Act Article 555, which is applied mutatis mutandis under Civil Act Article 47(1) when a foundation is established by an inter vivos disposition, provides that, “If the intention to make a gift is not expressed in writing, either party may rescind it,” thereby limiting rescission of a gift (contribution) made in writing. However, since such rescission differs from avoidance under the general provisions of the Civil Act in terms of requirements and effect, even where the contribution is made in writing, the contributor may avoid the expression of intent to contribute on the ground that it was made by mistake pursuant to the general provisions of the Civil Act, and it is not to be viewed differently merely because it is an act of contribution to a foundation, which is a unilateral juristic act without a counterparty.\\n\\nAccording to the record, the court below correctly held, to the effect that Defendant 1’s avoidance of the expression of intent to contribute in this case on the ground of mistake was lawful.\\n\\nThere is no error in the court below’s above findings and determination in failing to conduct a sufficient examination, omitting to decide, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the expression of intent regarding the contributed property, rescission, nullity, or avoidance of a juristic act, a gift without a counterparty, or changes in contributed property prior to the establishment of a foundation.\\n\\nFurther, even though, in the relationship between a contributor to a foundation and the corporation, once the corporation is established on the basis of the act of contribution, the contributed property shall, pursuant to Civil Act Article 48, belong to the corporation at the time of incorporation and become the corporation’s property, and even in the case where the contributed property is real estate, as between the two parties above no registration is required apart from the incorporation of the corporation (see Supreme Court Decision 93DA8054, rendered September 14, 1993; en banc Decision 78DA481, 482, rendered December 11, 1979; inter alia), in this case, where avoidance was sought on the ground of mistake, Defendant 1, as the contributor, may avoid the expression of intent to contribute regardless of whether the Plaintiff corporation was established or whether the contributed property was basic property; accordingly, the court below’s judgment is also free from error of law in its interpretation of the contribution of property to a foundation and Civil Act Article 48(1).\\n\\nThe arguments in the grounds of appeal on this point cannot be accepted.\\n\\n2. As to Point 4\\n\\nIn order to seek delivery or surrender on the ground of unlawful possession, the claim must be brought against the person who is actually in possession of the object in question, and even if a person is an unlawful possessor, unless that person has delivered the property to another and is not actually in possession thereof, a claim for delivery or surrender against that person is improper (see Supreme Court Decisions 81DA187, rendered May 10, 1983; 70DA1508, rendered September 29, 1970; 68DA1594, rendered February 4, 1969; inter alia).\\n\\nThe court below determined that the contents of Exhibit A No. 9 and Exhibit B No. 1, together with the respective testimonies of the non-party witness at the trial court and the court below, were insufficient to establish that Defendant 1 was in possession of the donated building in this case, and that there was otherwise no evidence to establish that Defendant 1 was in possession of the donated building in this case or had agreed to deliver it to the Plaintiff corporation.\\n\\nIn light of the record and the legal principles stated above, the court below’s factual findings and determination are proper, and there is no error of law concerning Civil Act Article 48(1), nor any factual error arising from a failure to conduct a sufficient examination or a violation of the rules of evidence, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe argument in the grounds of appeal on this point cannot be accepted.\\n\\n3. As to Point 5\\n\\nThe court below determined that the respective partial testimonies of the non-party witness at the trial court and the court below, which appeared to support the fact that the buildings listed as items A, B, C, D, and E in Attached List 2 to the lower court judgment were donated (contributed) by Defendant 1 to the Plaintiff corporation, were not credible; that the contents of Exhibit A No. 10 (the same as Exhibit A No. 12-3) were insufficient by themselves to establish such fact; and that there was otherwise no evidence to establish it.\\n\\nThe court below’s foregoing findings and determination are supportable as proper on the record, and there is no error of law arising from a failure to conduct a sufficient examination or a factual error resulting from a violation of the rules of evidence, as argued in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe argument in the grounds of appeal on this point likewise cannot be accepted.\\n\\nTherefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the Plaintiff, and it is so adjudged as stated in the disposition by the unanimous concurrence of the Justices who participated."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning an order for registration of a leasehold right are correct? (In case of dispute, according to case law) (a) A tenant who has registered a leasehold right pursuant to an order for registration of a leasehold right, where such leasehold right registration was completed before the registration of the first order to commence auction, falls within the class of creditors entitled to distribution even if he or she does not separately file a demand for distribution. (b) Under the Housing Lease Protection Act, the landlord’s obligation to return the lease deposit is an obligation that must be performed before the tenant’s obligation to cancel the leasehold right registration. (c) Since the Housing Lease Protection Act partially applies mutatis mutandis the procedural provisions concerning provisional seizure under the Civil Execution Act to judicial proceedings on an application for an order for registration of a leasehold right and to the enforcement, etc. of an order for registration of a leasehold right, leasehold right registration pursuant to an order for registration of a leasehold right prescribed by the Housing Lease Protection Act has the effect of interrupting the statute of limitations equivalent to seizure, provisional seizure, or provisional disposition, which are grounds for interruption of the statute of limitations.
label: C
supporting_precedents: {"[2005DA33039]": "According to the reasons of the judgment below, the court below found, based on the evidence it adopted, that the Plaintiff leased 15 pyeong of the subject house on December 12, 1996, for a lease deposit of 7,000,000 won, and moved into the subject house on December 21, 1996; that on July 27, 1999, the Plaintiff obtained a certified date on the lease agreement and filed a report of change of address to that address on the same day; that the Defendant, on August 31, 1999, obtained registration of the creation of a mortgage on the subject house with a maximum secured amount of 11,700,000 won, debtor Non-party 1, and mortgagee the Defendant; that thereafter, on October 26, 1999, the Plaintiff obtained from the Gwangju District Court an order for registration of a housing leasehold right with respect to the subject house stating that “lease agreement date: December 12, 1996, lease deposit: 7,000,000 won, resident registration date: July 27, 1999, scope of lease: 15 pyeong of the subject house, commencement date of possession: December 21, 1996, certified date: July 27, 1999,” and completed the said leasehold registration on November 11, 1999; that the Defendant, based on the said mortgage, filed with the said court an application for auction by sale of real property, Case No. 2002TAGYEONG35117, with respect to the subject house, and the said court rendered a decision to commence auction on October 15, 2002, and the registration entry thereof was completed on October 17, 2002; that the said court conducted the said auction proceedings and, on the distribution date of March 2, 2004, prepared a distribution schedule allocating, out of 13,025,728 won as the amount to be distributed after deducting execution costs from the successful bid price, etc., 6,512,864 won, being one-half of the amount to be distributed, to Non-party 2, who had leased part of the subject house for 10,000,000 won, and 6,512,864 won, being the remainder of the amount to be distributed, to the Defendant, who was both the petitioning creditor and the mortgagee; that the Plaintiff, at the said distribution date, stated an objection to 3,743,568 won out of the above distribution amount to the Defendant under the above distribution schedule, and filed the action for objection to distribution in this case with the said court within 7 days thereafter; and that the Plaintiff had not made a demand for distribution by the deadline for demands for distribution in the said auction proceedings; and, after recognizing these facts, the court below, on the ground that a person who has completed leasehold registration pursuant to an order for registration of a leasehold right is deemed to have made a demand for distribution even without separately making a demand for distribution in auction proceedings, and thus is also entitled to distribution, held that, because the Plaintiff had the right to receive repayment of the said lease deposit in preference to the Defendant, who was a junior right holder, the amount to be distributed to the Defendant under the above distribution schedule should be corrected from the original distribution amount of 6,512,864 won to 2,769,296 won, which is obtained by deducting 3,743,568 won, the amount to which the Plaintiff stated an objection at the said distribution date, and the amount to be distributed to the Plaintiff should be corrected to 3,743,568 won.\\n\\nArticle 3-3(5) of the Housing Lease Protection Act provides, “When leasehold registration is completed by execution of an order for registration of a leasehold right, the tenant acquires the opposability under Article 3(1) and the preferential right to repayment under Article 3-2(2). Provided, however, that if the tenant had already acquired opposability or the preferential right to repayment before the leasehold registration, such opposability or preferential right to repayment shall remain in effect as is, and after the leasehold registration, even if the tenant loses the requirements for opposability under Article 3(1), the tenant shall not lose the opposability or preferential right to repayment already acquired.” Article 3-5 of the same Act provides, “A leasehold right shall be extinguished by the sale of the leased house through auction under the Civil Execution Act when auction is conducted with respect to the leased house. Provided, however, that this shall not apply to a leasehold right with opposability for which the deposit has not been fully repaid.” As a tenant who has completed leasehold registration pursuant to an order for registration of a leasehold right has the right to preferential repayment, and the above leasehold registration primarily serves a security function of enabling the tenant to maintain any existing opposability or preferential right to repayment (see Supreme Court Decision 2005DA4529, decided June 9, 2005), if the above leasehold registration was recorded before the registration of the first decision to commence auction, then, by analogy to the “creditor holding a mortgage, leasehold right, or other right to claim preferential repayment that was registered before the registration of the first decision to commence auction and is extinguished by sale” under Article 148(4) of the Civil Execution Act, which governs the scope of creditors entitled to receive distribution, the tenant should be deemed to belong to the creditors entitled to distribution even without making a separate demand for distribution.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the above determination by the court below, as noted above, is proper and can be affirmed, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality, such as an erroneous understanding of the legal principles concerning the scope of persons who may participate in distribution with or without a demand for distribution, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[2005DA4529]": "Although a tenant who, after the termination of a residential lease, has not received back the lease deposit needs to move his or her residence or to transfer the resident registration because of a change in place of work, etc., in order to enable such tenant to move freely from the leased house or to transfer the resident registration without losing the opposability and preferential right of repayment prescribed by the Housing Lease Protection Act, Article 3-3 of the Housing Lease Protection Act, in response to such need, provides that a tenant who has not received back the deposit after the termination of the lease may apply to a court for an order for the registration of leasehold right, and that when the leasehold right registration by execution of the order for the registration of leasehold right is completed, the tenant acquires the opposability and preferential right of repayment under the same Act, and, if the tenant has already acquired the opposability or preferential right of repayment before the leasehold right registration, such opposability or preferential right of repayment remains as it is, and after the leasehold right registration, even if the requirements for opposability under Article 3(1) of the same Act are lost, the already acquired opposability or preferential right of repayment is not lost. Therefore, since the leasehold right registration under the above provision is completed while the landlord does not return the deposit even though the lease agreement has already been terminated, it is not to be interpreted that the landlord’s obligation to return the lease deposit, which has already fallen into actual default, and the tenant’s duty to cancel the newly completed leasehold right registration in order to preserve the corresponding rights of the tenant, are in a concurrent performance relationship; rather, especially in view of the fact that the above leasehold right registration is mainly intended to serve only the security function of enabling the tenant to maintain the existing opposability or preferential right of repayment, the landlord’s obligation to return the lease deposit should be deemed to be an obligation that must be performed prior to the tenant’s duty to cancel the leasehold right registration.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below, based on the evidence it admitted, recognized the facts as stated in its holding, including that the Nonparty leased the building at issue for a deposit of 28,000,000 won and filed a resident registration move-in report on November 16, 1994; that the Nonparty, after the lease agreement terminated, applied for registration of leasehold right pursuant to Article 3-3 of the Housing Lease Protection Act, and the leasehold right registration was completed on October 13, 1999, and around that time delivered possession of the building at issue to the owner while demanding return of the lease deposit; that the Plaintiff entered into a housing lease credit insurance contract with the Nonparty, and when the owner of the housing at issue failed to pay the lease deposit as above, the Plaintiff paid the above 28,000,000 won to the Nonparty pursuant to the insurance contract; that a voluntary auction was conducted on the building at issue, the Defendant purchased it at the auction, and in the distribution proceedings only 3,535,264 won was distributed to the Nonparty; and, after recognizing such facts, determined that the Defendant, who succeeded to the status of the former landlord pursuant to Article 3(2) of the Housing Lease Protection Act, was obligated to pay to the Plaintiff, who acquired by subrogation the rights of the Nonparty tenant maintaining opposability by having completed leasehold right registration with respect to the building at issue pursuant to the proviso to Article 3-5 and Article 3-3(5) of the Housing Lease Protection Act, the unpaid lease deposit, and rejected the Defendant’s defense of concurrent performance to the effect that the lease deposit could not be paid until the leasehold right registration of the building at issue was cancelled, on the ground that the landlord’s obligation to return the lease deposit is an obligation to be performed prior to the duty to cancel the above leasehold right registration, and further, as stated in its holding, after sequentially appropriating the above distribution amount and the amount already paid by the Defendant to the Plaintiff under the name of return of the lease deposit to delay damages and the lease deposit, ordered the Defendant to pay to the Plaintiff the balance of the deposit not yet paid; and, in light of the legal principles examined above and the record, the above fact-finding and determination by the court below are just and reasonable, and there is no illegality such as misapprehension of the law regarding the duty to cancel leasehold right registration or misapprehension of facts, as alleged in the ground of appeal.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal are assessed against the losing party, and it is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices as stated in the dispositive part."}
{"[2017DA226629]": "All appeals are dismissed. The costs of appeal, including the portion arising from the auxiliary intervention, shall be borne by the Plaintiff."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning simultaneous performance is correct? (Where there is a dispute, according to case law)
A: In a contract for work, where the contractor’s failure to properly perform the obligations under the contract causes damage to the body or property of the employer, the contractor’s damages obligation arising from such consequential damage and the employer’s obligation to pay the construction price are not in a simultaneous performance relationship.
B: An obligation to cancel a transfer registration of ownership in the name of the creditor, or a provisional registration for the preservation of the claim therefor, which was completed for the purpose of securing a secured claim, is in a simultaneous performance relationship with payment of the secured claim.
C: Where a foreclosure auction for the execution of a mortgage is rendered void and Creditor A, who is the mortgagee, exercises, on behalf of Debtor C, the right to claim cancellation of the transfer registration of ownership against successful bidder B, A’s obligation to return the distribution money and B’s obligation to cancel the transfer registration of ownership are in a simultaneous performance relationship.
D: An employer who has assumed the contractor’s obligation to pay the construction price to a subcontractor may oppose the subcontractor’s claim for the construction price with a defense of simultaneous performance based on the contractor’s right to claim repair of defects against the subcontractor.
E: In a lease of a commercial building, the tenant’s obligation to return the leased object and the landlord’s obligation to compensate for damages arising from interference with the recovery of premium are not only based on the same cause, namely the termination of the lease contract, but even from the perspective of fairness, a connection in performance can be recognized.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2004DA37676]": "1. Judgment of the court below\\n\\nThe court below first, by synthesizing the evidence set forth in its reasoning, found the following facts: Non-party Jiaan Industry Co., Ltd. (whose trade name was later changed to “Kyungbu Industry Co., Ltd.,” hereinafter referred to for convenience as “Jiaan Industry”) was, on 1999. 12. 13., awarded by the Defendant a contract for the “anti-slip pavement work on the Olympic-daero section between Hail and Haengjoo Bridge” for the construction price of 410,575,146 won; Non-party 1, on 1999. 12. 27., received the above pavement work on subcontract from Jiaan Industry and completed the work around 2000. 5. 12.; the Plaintiff, on the basis of the original copy of an executory promissory note notarial deed, No. 77 of 2000, issued by the certified public notary joint law office Saeseoul Joint Law Office in relation to Jiaan Industry, obtained on 2000. 5. 23. from the Seoul District Court in Case No. 2000TAGI4798 an order of seizure and assignment (hereinafter referred to as “the assignment order in this case”) concerning Jiaan Industry’s claim for the above construction price against the Defendant, and that order was served on the Defendant around that time and became final on 2000. 8. 8.; thereafter, the Defendant, in consideration of the legislative intent of Article 88(1) of the Framework Act on the Construction Industry as then in force, directly paid 126,634,460 won, corresponding to the labor cost portion of the construction price in this case, to Jiaan Industry and Non-party 1 with the Plaintiff’s consent on 2000. 6. 5., and so forth.\\n\\nThe court below then, based on the above facts found, determined that the claim for the construction price in this case had been transferred to the Plaintiff by the assignment order in this case, and therefore, absent special circumstances, the Defendant had the obligation to pay the amount assigned under the assignment order in this case to the Plaintiff; and as to the Defendant’s subsequent defense of setoff, namely, the assertion that the indemnity claim the Defendant has against Jiaan Industry, as the automatic claim, is set off against the above assigned debt at equal value, the court rejected it on the ground that there was no evidence to show that the Defendant had in fact acquired an indemnity claim against Jiaan Industry, and ultimately upheld in substance the first-instance judgment that largely granted the Plaintiff’s claim in this case.\\n\\n2. Determination on the grounds for final appeal\\n\\nHowever, the court below’s such disposition is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nA. Since Article 136 of the Civil Procedure Act provides that “the presiding judge may question the parties on factual or legal matters and may urge them to produce proof in order to clarify the relation of the litigation.” (Paragraph 1), and that “the court shall give the parties an opportunity to state their opinions on legal matters which are deemed to have been clearly overlooked by the parties.” (Paragraph 4), where there exists a legal matter that a party clearly overlooked through negligence or misunderstanding, or where there is a contradiction or lack of clarity in a party’s assertions, the court should actively exercise its power to clarify and give the parties an opportunity to state their opinions; and if it neglects to do so, it should be deemed unlawful as a failure to fulfill the duty of clarification or indication (see Supreme Court Decision of January 10, 2003, 2002DA41435, etc.). According to the record, the Defendant also asserted that “if the cause of the traffic accident is determined to be a defect in the anti-slip bank construction, then, pursuant to the terms of the construction contract, the above Jiaan Industry must bear full responsibility for compensating the damages suffered by the above deceased persons” (record pp. 43, 139), and also asserted that “if the Defendant Seoul Metropolitan Government loses the damages action and pays compensation to the bereaved family members, the Defendant Seoul Metropolitan Government will acquire against the above Jiaan Industry, the creditor of the construction price claim in this case, a claim for reimbursement in the amount corresponding to the damages compensation paid” (record p. 162), and that “if the Defendant, who bears the obligation to pay damages compensation to the victims, offsets the claim for reimbursement in an amount corresponding to that damages compensation against the construction price claim in this case, then the above construction price claim will be entirely extinguished” (record pp. 241, 265, 306, etc.); however, in a preparatory brief dated 2002. 4. 9. and the like, the Defendant also asserted that “as the Defendant Seoul Metropolitan Government, which is recognized as bearing liability for payment of damages compensation in connection with the traffic accident, acquires either a damages claim or a claim for reimbursement arising from payment of the damages compensation against the above Jiaan Industry, offsetting the amount corresponding to such damages compensation or the claim for reimbursement arising from payment of the damages compensation against the construction price claim in this case will cause the above construction price claim to be entirely extinguished” (record p. 177), that “the specific amount of setoff for the automatic claims such as the damages amount or claim for reimbursement against the above Jiaan Industry by the Defendant Seoul Metropolitan Government, with the construction price claim of Jiaan Industry as the passive claim, can only be calculated once the judgment in the above case becomes final” (record pp. 241, 266), and that “Jiaan Industry has no way to avoid liability to pay damages compensation arising from this accident to the Defendant Seoul Metropolitan Government” (record p. 351). Thus, the Defendant’s above assertions concerning the ground of occurrence and nature of the automatic claim in this case were not without ambiguity from a legal perspective. In light of the foregoing legal principles, the court below should first have actively exercised its power to clarify and made clear whether the ground of occurrence and nature of the automatic claim asserted by the Defendant in this case were limited merely to a right of indemnity in the internal relationship among non-true joint and several obligors, or whether they also included, in addition thereto, a damages claim that the Defendant, as contractor, could assert against Jiaan Industry, as contractor, pursuant to Article 390 of the Civil Act (see Supreme Court Decision of August 20, 2004, 2001DA70337), and then, accordingly, should have further determined the propriety of the Defendant’s clearly revealed assertions. This cannot but be said.\\n\\nB. If, however, the Defendant also put forward such damages claim as the automatic claim for the setoff defense in this case, then the court below failed to determine at all the propriety of such setoff defense by the Defendant, thereby committing the error of omission of determination; and, as seen below, there is sufficient room to view such error as having affected even the result of the judgment in this case.\\n\\nNamely, where damage has arisen to the contractor’s person or property because the contractor failed properly to perform the obligations under the contract, it should be deemed that the contractor has the obligation to compensate for such damage unless it proves on its own that there was no attributable cause on its part (see the above Supreme Court Decision 2001DA70337). Originally, the defense of simultaneous performance is a system that, based on the concept of fairness and the principle of good faith, recognizes the interdependence in the performance process when the obligations borne by each party have reciprocal consideration, thereby allowing one party to refuse to perform its own obligation when the other party claims performance of that party’s obligation without itself performing or offering performance. In view of the purpose of this system, even if each obligation borne by the parties is not an obligation with an inherent reciprocal consideration in a bilateral contract relationship, where, according to the agreed contents concerning each party’s obligations in a specific contractual relationship, there exist circumstances whereby the obligations have reciprocal consideration and the interdependence in performance should be recognized, the defense of simultaneous performance must be acknowledged (see Supreme Court Decisions of August 30, 2004, 2004DA24236, 24243, etc.). Furthermore, as a result of Article 536 of the Civil Act being applied mutatis mutandis under Article 667(3) of the Civil Act, the damages claim that the contractor may assert against the contractor together with repair of defects and the contractor’s construction price claim are in a relationship of simultaneous performance with each other. In light of this, the contractor’s damages liability arising from expanded damages caused by defects and the contractor’s obligation to pay the construction price should also be viewed as being in a relationship of simultaneous performance. Moreover, where the passive claim of the attached claim and the automatic claim of the third debtor are in a relationship of simultaneous performance, even if the automatic claim arose only after the seizure order was served on the third debtor and the effect of seizure arose, the third debtor who may assert the defense of simultaneous performance may oppose the seizure creditor by setoff using that claim; in such case, because the cause underlying the occurrence of the automatic claim had already been established and existed before the passive claim was seized, such automatic claim does not fall under “a claim acquired thereafter by a third debtor who has been ordered not to make payment” as provided in Article 498 of the Civil Act (see Supreme Court Decision of September 28, 1993, 92DA55794, etc.).\\n\\nAccording to the record, the work in this case was the work of applying, over a certain area, anti-slip aggregate that increases friction at regular intervals so as to prevent vehicles from slipping on curved sections or sloped sections of Olympic-daero; if incompletely bonded aggregate came off, it could rather increase vehicle slipping, so after applying the aggregate, traffic had to be continuously controlled for at least one hour to allow sufficient curing, and thereafter residual aggregate that remained unattached had to be thoroughly collected; because aggregate could also fall off additionally due to vehicle passage, cleaning had to be repeated for one or two days after the work. Non-party 1, the subcontractor, immediately after approval by the Traffic Operation Improvement Planning Team and the change of the construction contract, on 2000. 2. 11., deployed subordinate employees, daily laborers, and construction equipment, first completed the work at the Amsa-dong site in Gangdong-gu, Seoul, and then continuously, from around 10:00 on 2000. 2. 13. (Sunday), proceeded with the work on lanes 3 and 4 out of the four lanes over the approximately 75-meter right-curving section in front of Cheongdam 2 Bridge in Samsung-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul. At that time, traffic police patrolling Olympic-daero discovered that traffic in the construction section was being controlled and congestion was occurring, and requested Non-party 1 and others to complete the finishing work as soon as possible for smooth passage of vehicles for the International Joint Blessing Marriage Ceremony to be held at Jamsil Sports Complex at 13:00 that day. Accordingly, Non-party 1, the subcontractor, and the laborers decided to do the work on lanes 1 and 2 later, roughly finished cleaning while the aggregate applied to lanes 3 and 4 had not yet fully cured, opened the road to traffic, and withdrew from the site; as a result, as vehicles continued to pass over the road surface that had not fully cured, a large amount of residual aggregate came off and became scattered on the road surface. Then, at around 00:45 on 2000. 2. 14., the day after the above pavement work, Non-party 3, while driving a commercial taxi and proceeding along lane 3 of Olympic-daero from east to west, reached the vicinity of Cheongdam 2 Bridge, the construction site, and, because of the residual aggregate scattered on the road surface, slipped and caused an accident by colliding with the guardrail toward the shoulder side of lane 4; thereafter, while waiting for a tow truck, he parked the taxi on the U-turn lane installed inside lane 1 on the left side toward Cheongdam Park, and the tow truck and traffic patrol car dispatched to handle the accident were standing by there. Then, at around 01:07 on 2000. 2. 14., immediately after the foregoing prior accident, Non-party 2 also, while driving a Potentia passenger car (vehicle registration number omitted) and proceeding along lane 4 of Olympic-daero from east to west at a high speed of approximately 116 km/h, reached the vicinity of Cheongdam 2 Bridge and, like Non-party 3, slipped toward lane 1 on the left side because of aggregate scattered on the road surface, and caused an accident by successively colliding with the rear part of the above tow truck, which was standing on the U-turn lane inside lane 1, and with the Cheongdam Park boundary stone on the left side; as a result of that accident, Non-party 2 and the passengers, Non-party 4, Non-party 5, and Non-party 6, all died at the scene. Thereafter, Non-party 7 and Non-party 8, the bereaved family members of the deceased Non-party 4, and Non-party 9, Non-party 10, and Non-party 11, the bereaved family members of the deceased Non-party 5 and deceased Non-party 6, filed a lawsuit seeking damages against the Defendant and Non-party 1, asserting that the traffic accident occurred due to a defect at the above accident site; they lost in the first instance and were rendered a judgment of dismissal, but only Non-party 7 and Non-party 8 appealed, and as a result, part of the appeal was granted, and on 2003. 1. 22. the Seoul High Court rendered a partially favorable judgment ordering the Defendant and Non-party 1 to jointly and severally compensate Non-party 7 with 66,206,515 won and Non-party 8 with 40,871,010 won, plus delay damages thereon (Case No. 2002NA29512). The Defendant and Non-party 1 appealed therefrom, but on 2004. 4. 16. the appellate judgment above was maintained except that part of the delay damages was reversed and decided by the Supreme Court on its own motion (Case No. 2003DA12489). According to the final and conclusive judgment, the Defendant actually paid a total of 84,716,006 won to Non-party 7 and Non-party 8 on 2004. 5. 20., while depositing the remaining 60 million won because Dongbu Fire & Marine Insurance Co., Ltd., which had paid Non-party 7 liability insurance money in that amount, attached on the basis of subrogation the above damages claim of Non-party 7, etc. against the Defendant, etc. It can be seen from the above that the traffic accident in this case appears to have occurred because, among other things, Non-party 1, the subcontractor, intentionally or negligently performed the anti-slip pavement work at the above accident site in a rough manner; therefore, under Article 44(3) of the Framework Act on the Construction Industry, Jiaan Industry, as the contractor, as well as Non-party 1, must be jointly and severally liable to compensate the victims for the damage thereby caused (see Supreme Court Decision of June 12, 2001, 2000DA58859). On the other hand, since damage occurred to the Defendant contractor’s property due to defects arising in the course of performing the obligations under the contract, the Defendant must, under Article 390 of the Civil Act, be liable to compensate for such damage unless it proves that there was no attributable cause on its part. Even if Jiaan Industry’s claim for the construction price in this case and the Defendant’s damages claim are not obligations having an inherent reciprocal consideration in a bilateral contractual relationship, it is reasonable, in light of Article 667(3) of the Civil Act and the principle of fairness, to recognize an interdependence in performance; thus, the two claims should be regarded as being in a relationship of simultaneous performance. In such circumstances, even if the Defendant’s above damages claim, as the automatic claim, arose only after the seizure of the construction price claim in this case, as the passive claim, because the cause underlying its occurrence had already largely been established and existed before the passive claim was seized, such automatic claim cannot be said to be “a claim acquired thereafter by a third debtor who has been ordered not to make payment” as provided in Article 498 of the Civil Act, and the Defendant must be able to lawfully oppose the Plaintiff by setoff.\\n\\nC. Even if, arguendo, the Defendant had put forward only the right of indemnity as the automatic claim, the court below’s disposition rejecting that assertion is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nArticle 44(3) of the Framework Act on the Construction Industry provides that “where a subcontractor, intentionally or negligently, performs the construction work subcontracted in a rough manner and thereby causes damage to another person, the contractor shall be liable, jointly and severally with the subcontractor, to compensate for such damage.” Thus, in a subcontract relationship involving construction work to which the Framework Act on the Construction Industry applies (see the main text of Article 2(4) of that Act), where a subcontractor, intentionally or negligently, performs the construction work in a rough manner and thereby causes damage to another person, not only the subcontractor but also the contractor without attributable fault should be deemed liable, jointly and severally, to compensate for such damage. The expression “performs the construction work in a rough manner” here means carrying out construction contrary to the Building Act and other various statutes and regulations, design documents, construction practices, general common sense as a construction businessman, etc., thereby impairing the safety of the structure itself or of the construction work, or creating danger to another person’s body or property (see Supreme Court Decision of June 12, 2001, 2000DA58859). In addition, since there is generally no relationship of command and supervision between a contractor and a subcontractor, the contractor does not bear liability for damages as an employer with respect to torts by the subcontractor or the subcontractor’s employees; however, in so-called labor subcontracting, such as where the contractor directs a specific act or subcontracts a specific project to the subcontractor, even if the party is the contractor, it bears liability for damages as an employer (see Supreme Court Decision of February 8, 1983, 81DA428, etc.). Accordingly, a contractor in such a position, where a subcontractor, intentionally or negligently, performs the subcontracted construction work in a rough manner and thereby causes damage to another person, is, in external relations, liable jointly and severally with the subcontractor to compensate for such damage; further, if the contractor actually compensates for that damage and thereby discharges the subcontractor’s liability, the contractor acquires against the subcontractor a right of indemnity corresponding to the contractor’s burden portion. And, as seen above, even if each obligation borne by the parties is not an obligation with an inherent reciprocal consideration in a bilateral contractual relationship, where there are circumstances requiring recognition of an interdependence in performance, the defense of simultaneous performance should be acknowledged; in light of this and the like, the contractor, who as one of the non-true joint and several obligors actually performed the obligation to compensate the victim for damages, acquires against the subcontractor, who bears employer liability, a right of indemnity that is a variant of the damages claim the contractor may assert together with repair of defects or the so-called claim for compensation of expanded damages caused by defects, and this right of indemnity has, in substance, a reciprocal consideration with the subcontractor’s construction price claim. Thus, in light of the principle of fairness, it is reasonable to recognize an interdependence in performance, and the two claims should be regarded as being in a relationship of simultaneous performance. Furthermore, even if the automatic claim arose only after the seizure order was served on the third debtor and the effect of seizure arose, the third debtor who may assert the defense of simultaneous performance may oppose the seizure creditor by setoff based on that claim.\\n\\nAccording to the record, Non-party 1, the subcontractor, and Non-party 12, then the site manager, stated to investigative authorities to the effect that they had received specific instructions from Non-party 13, the president of Jiaan Industry, regarding whether to commence construction and the timing of commencement (record, separate volume pp. 102, 178); Non-party 1 also asserted to the effect that Non-party 13 personally purchased the materials and supplies necessary for the subcontracted work and supplied them to the construction site (record p. 384); after conclusion of oral argument in the court below, the Defendant attached evidentiary materials showing that it had in fact filed a claim for reimbursement against Jiaan Industry, etc. on the basis of this automatic claim, and requested reopening of oral argument, asserting that “Jiaan Industry has no way to avoid responsibility to pay damages compensation arising from this accident to the Defendant Seoul Metropolitan Government” (record pp. 348, 351). Even in such circumstances, without examining at all whether, at that time, Jiaan Industry had reserved and exercised specific command-and-supervisory authority over the progress and method of the work by Non-party 1, etc., and whether it had specifically directed and supervised the execution of the work, the court below nonetheless rejected the Defendant’s setoff defense too hastily on the ground that there was no evidence to recognize the existence of the automatic claim asserted by the Defendant, and it cannot be denied that this also involved an error of insufficient examination (moreover, considering that after the court below rendered its judgment, a lower court judgment was in fact rendered in the above reimbursement claim suit recognizing the existence of the automatic claim in this case asserted by the Defendant, there appears to be room to view that this error by the court below even affected the result of the judgment).\\n\\nD. In the end, from any perspective, the court below, by prematurely rejecting the Defendant’s setoff defense solely on the grounds stated in its reasoning, cannot avoid being deemed to have committed unlawful conduct such as failure to exercise the power to clarify, violation of the rules of evidence affecting the judgment, insufficiency of examination, or misapprehension of the legal principles regarding the cause of occurrence or nature of the automatic claim asserted by the Defendant, or further regarding the setoff based on such automatic claim.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the portion of the court below’s judgment that went against the Defendant is reversed, and this case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination on that portion, and judgment is rendered as stated in the Disposition."}

{"[2006DA24049]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding the Plaintiff’s grounds of appeal\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below, the court below held that, where the successful bid is rendered void and each interested party must return what he acquired by reason of the successful bid, if performance of the duty of return were compelled first only against one party, it would result in a violation of equity and the principle of good faith; therefore, since the duty of return stands in a relationship of simultaneous performance with each other, it is proper that the Plaintiff’s duty to return the dividend and Defendant 1’s duty to cancel the registration of transfer of ownership concerning the land at issue be performed simultaneously. The court then reversed the portion of the first instance judgment concerning Defendant 1 and ordered Defendant 1 to perform the procedure for registration of cancellation of the registration of transfer of ownership concerning the land at issue concurrently with receiving the dividend refund from the Plaintiff.\\n\\nHowever, according to the reasons of the judgment below, the Plaintiff, by subrogating Non-party 1, the debtor in the auction at issue, is exercising Non-party 1’s right to claim cancellation of the registration of transfer of ownership against Defendant 1, and thus, the duty of Defendant 1 to cancel the registration of transfer of ownership is owed to Non-party 1, not to the Plaintiff. On the other hand, it can be seen that the right to claim return of the dividend, which Defendant 1 relies upon as the basis for the defense of simultaneous performance, is a claim against the Plaintiff, not against Non-party 1. Accordingly, the Plaintiff’s obligation to return the dividend to Defendant 1 is not an obligation directly owed to Defendant 1 arising from the auction being rendered void, but an obligation to return unjust enrichment, and cannot be said to be an obligation succeeded to from the debtor, Non-party 1. As such, where the Plaintiff’s obligation to return the dividend owed to Defendant 1 and Defendant 1’s duty to cancel the registration of transfer of ownership owed to Non-party 1 have different counterparties for performance, and the Plaintiff’s obligation to return the dividend is not an obligation succeeded to from Non-party 1 with the defense of simultaneous performance attached, it cannot be said to be a case in which there is such a nexus that they must be performed simultaneously under the principle of good faith or the principle of equity.\\n\\nTherefore, the court below erred in law affecting the judgment by adopting a view different from the foregoing, finding that the Plaintiff’s duty to return the dividend and Defendant 1’s duty to cancel the registration of transfer of ownership were in a relationship of simultaneous performance, and ordering Defendant 1 to perform concurrently. The Plaintiff’s appeal pointing out this issue is well-founded.\\n\\n2. Regarding the grounds of appeal by Defendant Kookmin Bank Co., Ltd.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below, the court below held that the auction of the real property at issue is void, and therefore both the registration of transfer of ownership effected by Defendant 1 concerning the real property at issue and the registration of the creation of a mortgage in favor of Defendant Kookmin Bank Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the “Defendant Bank”), which was completed on that basis, are all void for lack of cause, and thus the Defendant Bank is obliged to perform the procedure for registration of cancellation of the above registration of creation of a mortgage in favor of the Plaintiff. The court further held that the Defendant Bank cannot invoke Defendant 1’s defense of simultaneous performance, and that the above registration of creation of a mortgage was completed separately after the auction, without direct relation to the auction, so its duty of cancellation cannot be regarded as a duty of restoration to the original status arising from the auction being rendered void, and thus rejected the Defendant Bank’s defenses of simultaneous performance and violation of the principle of good faith. Such determination is proper, and, as noted above, since Defendant 1 is not recognized as having the defense of simultaneous performance, it is obvious that the defense of the Defendant Bank premised upon or invoking the same is without merit. Therefore, it cannot be said that there was any violation of the Constitution or statutes, etc., as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the portion of the judgment below concerning Defendant 1 is reversed and this part of the case is remanded to the Daejeon High Court, the Defendant Bank’s appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal as to the dismissed portion shall be borne by the Defendant Bank. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2007DA31914]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. The court below, after finding the facts as stated in its holding on the basis of the evidence stated therein, determined that, since the Defendant, as the employer of the construction work at issue, had agreed to pay directly to the Plaintiffs, who are subcontractors, the respective subcontract construction prices to be paid by the first-instance Defendant, Bangwon General Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Bangwon General Construction”), in the absence of special circumstances, the Defendant is obligated to pay the Plaintiffs the respective subcontract construction prices as stated in the holding.
