in such a case, if there is a special agreement concerning the overdue interest rate on the guarantee obligation, that agreement applies, and if there is no special agreement, the statutory interest rate prescribed by the Commercial Act or the Civil Act applies depending on the nature of the transaction, and the agreed overdue interest rate concerning the principal obligation does not automatically apply thereto (see Supreme Court Decision 99DA12123 dated April 11, 2000).\\n\\nIn this case, Article 18(1) of the Credit Guarantee Terms and Conditions applicable to the scope of performance of the guarantee obligation provides that the Defendant shall perform as a guarantee obligation “the principal not exceeding the guarantee amount, being the amount obtained by multiplying the outstanding balance of the guaranteed loan by the guarantee ratio, and the unpaid interest amount calculated at the agreed interest rate (the interest rate applied on the interest payment due date, excluding the overdue interest rate) up to the date of performance of the guarantee obligation.” As to the interest rate applicable to delay damages arising from the Defendant’s delay in performance of the guarantee obligation, the lower court determined that, in view of the fact that Article 18 of the Credit Guarantee Terms and Conditions at issue is titled “Scope of Performance of Guarantee Obligations,” its content merely sets the scope of the guarantee obligation itself borne by the Defendant, that is, the scope of the principal obligation and subordinate obligations for which the Defendant bears guarantee liability, and cannot be said to have fixed the delay damages on the guarantee obligation; therefore, there is no special agreement between the Plaintiff and the Defendant concerning the delay interest rate on the guarantee obligation, and because the Plaintiff’s guarantee claim against the Defendant corresponds to a claim arising from an act constituting a commercial transaction, the statutory interest rate of 6% per annum prescribed by the Commercial Act applies to such delay damages.\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principle and the fact that Article 29(2) of the Credit Guarantee Fund Act, Article 23(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the same Act, etc., which are the sources of the Credit Guarantee Terms and Conditions at issue, prescribe only the content of the “subordinate obligations” falling within the scope of the guarantee, the lower court’s determination as above is correct, and there is no error in its interpretation of Article 18 of the Credit Guarantee Terms and Conditions at issue or in its misapprehension of the legal principles concerning delay damages on the guarantee obligation.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, among the lower court judgment, the portion adverse to the Plaintiff concerning delay damages on 61,890,000 Japanese yen from May 1, 2010 through November 4, 2010 is reversed and vacated, and this part of the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination; the Defendant’s appeal is dismissed; and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the decision."}

{"[2020DA230239]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. Whether the procedural conduct of the lower court was unconstitutional\\nUpon reviewing the record, even though the lower court held only two oral argument hearings and then closed arguments, and thereafter overturned the first-instance judgment, which had dismissed the Plaintiff's principal claim, and partially upheld the principal claim and the alternative claim added at the lower-court stage, it cannot be said that there was any error in the lower court's procedural conduct, etc., infringing the constitutional right to a fair trial and the right to equality.\\n\\n2. Whether unjust enrichment arises with respect to interest exceeding the statutory limit (grounds for appeal concerning the principal claim)\\nThe lower court held that the Defendant, as a registered loan business operator, lent the Plaintiff the money set forth in serial numbers 1 to 11, 13, and 14 of Table 1 attached to the lower court judgment and received from the Plaintiff interest exceeding the maximum interest rate under the former Act on Registration of Loan Business, etc. and Protection of Financial Users (the version before amendment by Act No. 14072 on 2016. 3. 3.), and therefore determined that the Defendant has the obligation to return it to the Plaintiff as unjust enrichment.\\n\\nIn light of the record and the relevant legal principles, the reasons of the lower court judgment show that there is no error in the lower court's factual findings and determinations, such as, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, deviating from the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence in contravention of the rules of logic and experience, or failing to conduct necessary examination by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the burden of proof, thereby affecting the judgment.\\n\\n3. Whether an act in violation of the Interest Limitation Act constitutes a tort, and whether a person who intermediated a money transaction also bears joint tort liability (grounds for appeal concerning the alternative claim)\\na. The Interest Limitation Act was enacted to establish an appropriate maximum limit on interest, thereby realizing the stability of the national economic life and economic justice (Article 1), and to protect small-scale self-employed persons and low-income ordinary people from easily becoming credit delinquents due to high interest rates.\\n\\nIts main contents are as follows. The maximum contractual interest rate concerning a monetary loan agreement shall be determined by Presidential Decree within the limit not exceeding 25% per annum (Article 2(1)). The portion of contractual interest exceeding the maximum interest rate prescribed in Article 2(1) shall be void (Article 2(3)). Where a debtor voluntarily pays interest exceeding the maximum interest rate, the amount corresponding to the overpaid interest shall be appropriated to the principal, and when the principal is extinguished, the return thereof may be claimed (Article 2(4)).\\n\\nMeanwhile, Article 8(1) of the Interest Limitation Act provides a criminal penalty provision for violations of the Interest Limitation Act by prescribing that a person who receives interest exceeding the maximum interest rate prescribed in Article 2(1) shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 1 year or a fine not exceeding 10,000,000 won.\\n\\nIn light of the legislative purpose of the Interest Limitation Act, the regulatory content concerning the maximum interest rate, and the criminal punishment provisions for violations thereof, where a creditor who lent money intentionally or negligently violates the Interest Limitation Act and receives interest exceeding the maximum interest rate, thereby causing damage to the debtor, such conduct, barring special circumstances, shall be deemed to constitute a tort under Civil Act Article 750. Since interest paid in excess of the maximum interest rate is appropriated to the principal pursuant to Article 2(4) of the Interest Limitation Act, any excess payment remaining even after such appropriation and extinguishment of the principal may be regarded as damage caused by the violation of the Interest Limitation Act. A claim for restitution of unjust enrichment and a claim for damages arising from tort are separate and distinct claims from each other; thus, the mere existence of a claim for restitution of unjust enrichment regarding excess interest does not, by itself, preclude the establishment of a tort.\\n\\nFurthermore, a person who, jointly with the creditor, committed or participated in the above-mentioned violation of the Interest Limitation Act is also liable to compensate damages jointly and severally pursuant to Civil Act Article 760.\\n\\nb. According to the reasons of the lower court judgment, the following facts may be ascertained. Non-party 1 and Non-party 2, while lending the Plaintiff KRW 200,000,000 each on 2015. 12. 23., agreed to receive KRW 350,000,000, including interest equivalent to an annual rate of approximately 150%, on the due date of 2016. 6. 30. Non-party 1 received in total KRW 340,000,000 from 2016. 9. 2. to 2016. 9. 13., and Non-party 2 received in total KRW 435,000,000 from 2016. 9. 6. to 2016. 12. 28., thereby receiving interest exceeding the maximum interest rate prescribed by the Interest Limitation Act.\\n\\nBased on the foregoing facts, the lower court recognized that the torts of Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 were established, and calculated the amount of damage by applying the money repaid by the Plaintiff in the statutory order of appropriation to payment, namely interest, delay damages, and principal, as calculated according to the maximum interest rate prescribed by the Interest Limitation Act. It further found that the Defendant actively participated in the violation of the Interest Limitation Act by Non-party 1 and Non-party 2 in the process of brokering the above money transaction, and determined that the Defendant, as a joint tortfeasor, is obligated to compensate the damages suffered by the Plaintiff.\\n\\nIn light of the legal principles stated above, the reasons of the lower court judgment show that the lower court judgment is proper as it is based on those legal principles. There is no error in the lower court judgment, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, such as failing to conduct necessary examination and, in contravention of the rules of logic and experience, exceeding the limits of the principle of free evaluation of evidence and wrongly finding facts, or misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the Interest Limitation Act and joint torts, thereby affecting the judgment.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\nThe Defendant's appeal is without merit and is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party; accordingly, the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition, by unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court."}

question: A entered into a construction contract with B, a construction contractor, in order to newly construct Building Y on A’s land X. In order to enable B to obtain a loan from C using land X as security and to expend the construction costs, A established on land X a mortgage with C as the mortgagee and B as the debtor, and B used the money borrowed from C as the construction price. During the progress of the construction, D, a creditor of B, obtained an order of seizure and assignment for part of B’s claim for the construction price against A, and the order became final as it stood. Thereafter, even though the construction was completed, B was unable to repay the loan to C, so A, by subrogation for B, paid C the principal of the loan and the overdue interest. Among the following explanations, which are all correct? (In case of dispute, according to precedents) (a) When the order of assignment was served on A, retroactively, a divisible claim is established between D and B with respect to the portion of the claim that was assigned in full and the portion of the claim that was not assigned in full. (b) B’s obligation to deliver Building Y is in a concurrent-performance relationship with A’s debt to pay the construction price, but B’s obligation to cancel the mortgage on land X is not an obligation having an inherent quid pro quo relationship under the above construction contract for work, so a performance-connected relationship with A’s debt to pay the construction price cannot be recognized. (c) B’s reimbursement debt arising from A’s subrogated payment is, as a transformed form of B’s obligation to cancel the mortgage on land X, in a concurrent-performance relationship with A’s debt to pay the construction price within the extent of the equal amount. (d) If, in response to D’s claim for the assigned amount, A raises a set-off defense using A’s reimbursement claim against B, A cannot oppose D by set-off based on the above reimbursement claim because A’s active claim, namely A’s reimbursement claim against B, arose after D’s seizure order was served on A.
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[2007DA35152]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. With respect to the Plaintiff’s grounds of appeal\\n\\na. Ground 1 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\nAccording to the record, the Defendant’s preparatory brief dated 2006. 9. 1. states: “KPI General Construction Co., Ltd. borrowed KRW 350,000,000 from Plus Mutual Savings Bank Co., Ltd., using the site of the apartment at issue owned by the Defendant as security with a maximum secured amount of KRW 455,000,000; in addition, since there were other debts, such as credit loans, the Defendant suffered damages exceeding KRW 100,000,000 even after deducting from the construction price at issue discussed above the loan principal and interest debts in the amount of KRW 350,000,000 offset above by the Defendant by subrogation payment to the said bank in the amount of KRW 455,000,000, which is the above maximum secured amount.” It can be ascertained that the Defendant stated the above content at the first oral argument date of the first instance at which the Plaintiff’s litigation representative appeared.\\n\\nIt is sufficient to view the Defendant’s assertion as including the purport that, because the Defendant acquired a reimbursement claim by making subrogation payment of the above loan principal amount of KRW 350,000,000 and the overdue interest thereon, the Defendant raises set-off against the Plaintiff, who attached and obtained assignment of KPI General Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “KP Construction”)’s construction price claim against the Defendant, using that reimbursement claim as the automatic claim.\\n\\nAlthough there is some inadequacy in the lower court’s explanation of reasons, the lower court’s judgment reaching the same conclusion is proper, and there is no error of law, such as violation of the principle of pleading, as alleged by the Plaintiff as grounds of appeal.\\n\\nb. Ground 2 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\n(1) When an attachment and assignment order is issued with respect to a monetary claim, the attached claim is transferred from the attachment debtor to the attachment creditor while maintaining its identity; and since the third-party obligor may assert against the attachment creditor grounds that may be asserted against the attachment debtor before the claim was attached, where the automatic claim of the third-party obligor against the attachment debtor stands in a relationship of simultaneous performance with the attached claim, the third-party obligor may assert the defense of simultaneous performance even if the automatic claim arose after the attachment order was served on the third-party obligor and the effect of attachment arose. In such a case, since the cause on which the automatic claim is based had already been formed and existed before the passive claim was attached, it is proper to view that the automatic claim does not fall under the “claim acquired thereafter by a third-party obligor who received an order prohibiting payment” prescribed in Article 498 of the Civil Act, and the third-party obligor may assert set-off against the attachment creditor based on that automatic claim (see Supreme Court Decision 92DA55794, delivered on 1993. 9. 28.; Supreme Court Decision 2004DA37676, delivered on 2005. 11. 10.; etc.).\\n\\nMeanwhile, the defense of simultaneous performance must also be recognized where, even though the obligations borne by both parties are not obligations under a bilateral contract that are in an inherent reciprocal relationship of consideration, there are circumstances in a specific contractual relationship under which the obligations borne by both parties have reciprocal significance and a relationship of performance connection should be recognized. Further, where one contract or an agreement added to that contract comprehensively includes two or more typical contracts under the Civil Act or relations of claims and obligations under the Civil Act (hereinafter referred to as “typical contracts under the Civil Act, etc.”), and the various rights and obligations between the parties thereunder are closely interconnected for the same economic purpose, such rights and obligations shall not be separated into corresponding parts of the typical contracts under the Civil Act, etc., and only those obligations that are in a reciprocal relationship within the scope of each typical contract, etc. shall be deemed to be in a relationship of simultaneous performance. Rather, so long as it is recognized that one party’s various obligations, taken as a whole, are in a reciprocal relationship with the other party’s various obligations, such various obligations of one party and the other party may be viewed as being in a relationship of simultaneous performance (see Supreme Court Decision 95DA1521, delivered on 1995. 8. 22.; Supreme Court Decision 99DA47501, delivered on 2001. 6. 26.; etc.).\\n\\n(2) According to the reasons of the lower court judgment, the following facts can be ascertained: on 2003. 7. 30., the Defendant entered into a partnership agreement with Non-party 1, the representative director of KP Construction, under which the Defendant would become the owner-developer, provide the site for the villa at issue owned by the Defendant, and KP Construction would become the contractor, construct the villa at issue on the site of the villa at issue, and the parties would share the profits from sales; thereafter, the Defendant and KP Construction agreed to change the contract from a partnership method to a contracting-out method, and on 2004. 2. 5. entered into a construction subcontract agreement (hereinafter referred to as “the subcontract agreement at issue”) under which the Defendant would contract out to KP Construction the construction work for the villa at issue, with the construction price set at KRW 1,152,800,000 and the completion date set at 2004. 6. 29.; however, on 2004. 9. 24., the Defendant established a mortgage over the site of the villa at issue with Plus Mutual Savings Bank Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Plus Mutual Savings Bank”) as mortgagee, with a maximum secured amount of KRW 455,000,000, and KP Construction, as debtor, borrowed KRW 350,000,000 from Plus Mutual Savings Bank and used it as the construction price for the villa at issue; KP Construction went bankrupt around 2005. 4.; and, even after 2005. 5. 24., the date of approval for use of the villa at issue, had passed, the Defendant, because KP Construction had not repaid the above loan, on 2005. 6. 23. repaid by subrogation to Plus Mutual Savings Bank the loan principal amount of KRW 350,000,000 and overdue interest of KRW 36,857,459, on behalf of KP Construction; in order to secure its claim for agreed payment of KRW 551,588,000 against KP Construction, the Plaintiff obtained a decision of provisional attachment over the construction price claim for the villa at issue on 2005. 1. 12., and thereafter, on 2006. 7. 3., received an assignment order converting the provisional attachment into principal attachment with respect to the said agreed payment of KRW 551,588,000 and attaching the construction price claim at issue with respect to delay damages of KRW 76,768,960, assigning to the Plaintiff the construction price claim at issue corresponding to the total attached amount of KRW 628,356,960; the certified copy of the decision was served on the Defendant on 2006. 7. 5., and became final and binding on 2006. 8. 26.\\n\\n(3) We examine this in light of the legal principles set forth above. Since the Defendant provided, as security, the site of the villa at issue owned by the Defendant in order to support construction funds so that KP Construction could smoothly carry out the construction at issue, thereby enabling KP Construction to establish a mortgage thereon, borrow funds, and expend construction expenses, the Defendant’s provision of funds by way of security provision substantially functions like advance payment of the construction price under the subcontract agreement at issue. Accordingly, it is proper to view the relationship of rights and obligations concerning the establishment of the above mortgage between the Defendant and KP Construction as closely connected for the same economic purpose as the relationship of rights and obligations concerning the construction price under the subcontract agreement at issue. Therefore, when KP Construction exercises its construction price claim on the ground that, although it is legally the principal debtor for the loan debt, the construction price claim in an amount equivalent to the loan principal has not been extinguished, it is consistent with the economic substance of the transaction between the parties and their reasonable intent to consider not only the obligation to construct the villa at issue and deliver it to the Defendant, but also the connection with the obligation to cancel the above mortgage and restore the situation to what it was before the funding support (hereinafter referred to as the “mortgage cancellation obligation”). If, contrary to this, the Defendant were unconditionally required to comply with KP Construction’s claim for construction price, there is a risk that, after performing the construction price debt, the Defendant would be exposed to the risk of double payment, such as having to repay the loan on its own in order to prevent execution of the above mortgage if KP Construction fails to perform the mortgage cancellation obligation.\\n\\nTaken together and comprehensively considering these various circumstances, KP Construction’s mortgage cancellation obligation is not an obligation having an inherent reciprocal consideration relationship under the construction subcontract agreement with respect to the Defendant’s construction price debt, as is the obligation to deliver the villa at issue newly constructed; however, in light of the specific contractual relationship, including the background and purpose of the security provision, the purpose of use of the loan principal, the effect of the funding support as effectively advance payment of construction price resulting therefrom, and the risk of double payment that the Defendant would thereby face, it is proper to recognize a relationship of performance connection. Thus, the two obligations are in a relationship of simultaneous performance with each other. Furthermore, the reimbursement debt incurred by KP Construction when the Defendant made subrogation payment of the above loan principal and overdue interest as a result of KP Construction’s failure to perform the mortgage cancellation obligation should also be viewed as a transformed form of the mortgage cancellation obligation and, within the equivalent amount, as being in a relationship of simultaneous performance with the Defendant’s construction price debt.\\n\\nIf so, although the reimbursement claim acquired by the Defendant upon subrogation payment of the above loan principal arose only after the decision of provisional attachment and the attachment order in this case were served on the Defendant and the effect of provisional attachment and attachment arose, the Defendant may assert set-off against the Plaintiff, who is the attachment-and-assignment creditor of the construction price claim at issue, using that reimbursement claim as the automatic claim.\\n\\nThe lower court’s judgment to the same effect is persuasive and proper, and there is no error of law, such as misapprehension of the legal principles on the relationship of simultaneous performance or set-off, as alleged by the Plaintiff as grounds of appeal.\\n\\nc. Ground 3 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\n(1) When an assignment order concerning part of a divisible monetary claim becomes final and binding, unless special circumstances exist, separate and independent divisible claims are established retroactively from the time the assignment order is served on the third-party obligor, respectively, for the assigned portion and the unassigned portion of the claim. Therefore, the third-party obligor who intends to set off such claim against a counterclaim against the attachment debtor may, by designating either the assignment creditor or the attachment debtor as the counterpart of the set-off, set off or assert set-off against either of them. The assignment creditor who receives the third-party obligor’s declaration of intent to set off cannot raise an objection that the portion of the claim remaining with the attachment debtor must be set off first or that set-off must be made in proportion to each divisible claim amount relative to the total amount of the claim (see Supreme Court Decision 2000DA50596, delivered on 2002. 2. 8.).\\n\\n(2) Examining the reasons of the lower court judgment in light of the above legal principles, the lower court held that the Defendant could assert set-off against the Plaintiff, who received assignment of the 628,356,960 won portion, which is part of KP Construction’s construction price claim against the Defendant, using the entire reimbursement claim acquired by the Defendant on 2005. 6. 23. by making subrogation payment of the above loan principal amount of KRW 350,000,000 and overdue interest thereon in the amount of KRW 36,857,459 as the automatic claim. This is in accordance with the above legal principles and is proper, and there is no error of law, as alleged in ground 3 of the grounds of appeal, concerning the scope of the claim extinguished by set-off when part of a claim is assigned.\\n\\n2. With respect to the Defendant’s grounds of appeal\\n\\na. Grounds 1 and 2 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\n(1) According to the reasons of the lower court judgment, the lower court rejected the Defendant’s assertion that the remaining construction price was settled at KRW 432,000,000 on 2004. 10. 25. between the Defendant and KP Construction, and that the Defendant had fully paid the construction price at issue by, with KP Construction’s consent, selling and applying in kind as payment the three units of the villa at issue (Units 201, 301, and 401) as the remaining construction price, at KRW 144,000,000 per unit, totaling KRW 432,000,000, on the ground that there was no evidence to support such assertion, taking into account the circumstances stated in the judgment.\\n\\nIn light of the evidence lawfully adopted by the lower court, the lower court’s treatment and selection of evidence and its comparative evaluation of the probative value of evidence in this regard cannot be viewed as violating the laws of logic and experience or exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence. Accordingly, the Defendant’s grounds of appeal disputing this point cannot be accepted.\\n\\nAnd so long as this view is taken, the Defendant’s grounds of appeal to the effect that the Plaintiff’s provisional attachment in this case, and the attachment and assignment order, were invalid because they were directed to a construction price claim that had already been extinguished and no longer existed by reason of the alleged payment in kind, or that they were invalid because, due to the alleged agreement on payment in kind, the Defendant’s construction price debt to KP Construction had been changed into a villa sales debt and extinguished, and yet the provisional attachment, attachment, and assignment order were nevertheless directed to the construction price claim, likewise cannot be accepted.\\n\\n(2) According to the reasons of the lower court judgment, with respect to the Defendant’s assertion that Non-party 1, the representative director of KP Construction, went bankrupt without completing the construction at issue and disappeared, so the Defendant caused KP Construction’s subcontractors to carry out the window frame work and other works on the condition that the Defendant directly pay the construction costs, thereby incurring damages in the same amount of KRW 377,000,000 by way of payment in kind, the lower court held that the fact of payment in kind as asserted was recognized, but there was no evidence to support that the Defendant directly concluded subcontracting contracts with the subcontractors and caused them to carry out the work; rather, in light of the circumstances stated in the judgment, the subcontractors carried out the subcontracted work pursuant to subcontracting contracts with KP Construction, so KP Construction bears the obligation to pay the subcontracted construction price, and the Defendant, as the principal contractor, is properly viewed as having directly made payment in kind to Non-party 2, etc., who were subcontracted construction businesses, in lieu of paying KP Construction the subcontract price.\\n\\nIn light of the evidence lawfully adopted by the lower court, the lower court’s treatment and selection of evidence and comparative evaluation of the probative value of evidence in this regard cannot be viewed as violating the laws of logic and experience or exceeding the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence. Accordingly, the Defendant’s grounds of appeal disputing this point cannot be accepted.\\n\\nAnd so long as this view is taken, the lower court’s judgment to the effect that the performance of subcontracted work by the subcontractors should be viewed as performance by KP Construction of its construction obligations as contractor to the Defendant, and that therefore the subject to whom the construction price claim accrues should be viewed as KP Construction, is proper, and there is no error of law, such as misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the requirements for the accrual of a construction price claim, as alleged by the Defendant as grounds of appeal.\\n\\nb. Ground 3 of the grounds of appeal\\n\\n(1) According to the record, the Defendant asserted that it made subrogation payment to Plus Mutual Savings Bank of KP Construction’s various debts totaling KRW 455,000,000, and submitted the following: a subrogation payment confirmation certificate from Plus Mutual Savings Bank, an objective third party acknowledging the fact of subrogation payment in that amount (Defendant’s Exhibit No. 13); and a statement certificate of Non-party 3 consistent with the Defendant’s above assertion of subrogation payment (Defendant’s Exhibit No. 14). In response, the Plaintiff has not submitted any meaningful rebuttal evidence. Moreover, the lower court itself adopted the contents of the above subrogation payment confirmation certificate as evidence and recognized the fact that the Defendant, on 2005. 6. 23., made subrogation payment to Plus Mutual Savings Bank on behalf of KP Construction of the loan related to the construction at issue in the amount of KRW 350,000,000 and overdue interest thereon in the amount of KRW 36,857,459. Taken together, it is consistent with the rules of experience to view that, on 2005. 6. 23., the Defendant, on behalf of KP Construction, made subrogation payment to Plus Mutual Savings Bank of KRW 455,000,000, an amount exceeding the total of the above loan principal amount of KRW 350,000,000 and the overdue interest thereon, and thereby also made subrogation payment of KP Construction’s other loan debt to Plus Mutual Savings Bank (hereinafter referred to as “the other loan debt”), in addition to the principal and interest of the above loan.\\n\\nContrary to this, the lower court’s judgment that the contents of the above subrogation payment confirmation certificate alone were insufficient to recognize the fact that the Defendant made subrogation payment of the other loan debt, and that there was no other evidence to support this, is erroneous in that it failed to conduct the necessary examination or, in selecting and evaluating the probative value of evidence, exceeded the bounds of the principle of free evaluation of evidence, thereby affecting the judgment. The Defendant’s grounds of appeal pointing this out are well-founded.\\n\\n(2) And if, as above, the Defendant on 2005. 6. 23. made subrogation payment to Plus Mutual Savings Bank of the other loan debt on behalf of KP Construction, the Defendant would acquire against KP Construction a reimbursement claim in an amount equivalent to the subrogated payment (although the Defendant asserted that this was a claim for damages, in light of the fact that the Defendant asserted that it acquired a reimbursement claim against KP Construction by making subrogation payment of the loan principal amount of KRW 350,000,000 related to the construction at issue and the overdue interest thereon, that assertion may also be construed as meaning that it acquired a reimbursement claim).\\n\\nHowever, the above reimbursement claim arose only on 2005. 6. 23., after the decision of provisional attachment for the KRW 551,588,000 portion of the construction price claim at issue was served on the Defendant on 2005. 1. 12. Unlike the case of the above subrogation payment of the loan principal amount of KRW 350,000,000 discussed above, there is no basis to find that KP Construction’s other loan debt had an inherent reciprocal consideration relationship with the construction price debt at issue under the construction subcontract agreement, or that it had a relationship of performance connection with the construction price debt at issue. Moreover, even if a mortgage securing that loan debt had been established before service of the attachment order, payment thereof by subrogation cannot be asserted against the attaching creditor. Therefore, as to the above portion of the construction price claim in the amount of KRW 551,588,000, on which an attachment and assignment order converting the provisional attachment into principal attachment was issued, the Defendant cannot assert set-off against the Plaintiff by using as the automatic claim the reimbursement claim acquired by making subrogation payment of the other loan debt.\\n\\nHowever, as noted above in 1. a. (2), the portion of delay damages amounting to KRW 76,768,960 among the construction price claim at issue for which the Plaintiff received the attachment and assignment order was not converted from the provisional attachment into principal attachment; rather, after the Defendant acquired a reimbursement claim against KP Construction by making subrogation payment of the other loan debt on 2005. 6. 23., it was additionally attached on 2006. 7. 3., an assignment order was issued, and the certified copy of the decision was served on the Defendant on July 5 of the same year. Accordingly, with respect to the additional assigned portion of the construction price claim in the amount of KRW 76,768,960, the Defendant may assert set-off against the Plaintiff by using as the automatic claim the reimbursement claim acquired by making subrogation payment of the other loan debt before service of the attachment order.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower court held that since the time of occurrence of the reimbursement claim acquired by the Defendant by making subrogation payment of the other loan debt was after the provisional attachment decision, which formed the basis of the Plaintiff’s assignment order, was served on the Defendant, and that claim was not in a relationship of simultaneous performance with the construction price at issue, the Defendant could not assert set-off against the Plaintiff using that claim as the automatic claim. The lower court’s judgment in this regard contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning the time when an assignment order takes effect and concerning set-off when a claim is attached and assigned. The Defendant’s grounds of appeal pointing this out are well-founded to the extent recognized above.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, among the portions of the lower court judgment adverse to the Defendant, the portion concerning KRW 76,768,960 and the delay damages thereon is reversed, and this portion of the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. The Plaintiff’s appeal and the remainder of the Defendant’s appeal are dismissed in their entirety. It is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

question: A entered into a loan agreement with B on 2020. 8. 11., and, in order to secure A's claim against B, established a mortgage with a maximum secured amount of KRW 1.2 billion on land X owned by B. At B's request, C and D entered into a joint surety agreement with A. When B failed to repay the above debt, A filed an application for a voluntary auction based on the above mortgage over land X on 2023. 1. 23., and at the time of the auction application, A's claim against B amounted to KRW 1.2 billion. During the auction proceedings, C repaid KRW 400 million to A, and D repaid KRW 200 million to A, and accordingly received a registration of transfer of part of the mortgage from A. After filing the auction application, A additionally lent KRW 300 million to B on 2023. 5. 12., and in the auction proceedings, E purchased land X for KRW 900 million and paid the purchase price in full on 2023. 8. 18. Which combination of amounts to be distributed to A, C, and D in the above auction proceedings is correct? (Interest, delayed damages, and execution costs are not considered. If there is any dispute, according to precedents.) The amounts in the following choices mean, in order, the respective amounts for A, C, and D.
A: KRW 300 million, KRW 400 million, KRW 200 million
B: KRW 450 million, KRW 300 million, KRW 150 million
C: KRW 540 million, KRW 240 million, KRW 120 million
D: KRW 600 million, KRW 200 million, KRW 100 million
E: KRW 900 million, KRW 0, KRW 0
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2019DA222041]": "We examine the grounds of appeal (including the supplemental statements of grounds of appeal filed after the expiration of the period for filing the statement of grounds of appeal, to the extent that they supplement it).\\n\\n1. Outline of the case\\nAccording to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts can be ascertained.\\n\\na. The non-party, in order to obtain a loan, on 2004. 12. 23. had two registrations for the creation of a mortgage, with maximum secured amounts of KRW 70,000,000 and KRW 580,000,000, respectively, made with the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (hereinafter referred to as “the NFFC”) with respect to the real properties listed in items 1 and 2 of the attached list to the judgment below, owned by the non-party (hereinafter referred to as the “1st and 2nd real properties”) (hereinafter referred to as the “1st Mortgage”). In addition, around that time, the non-party obtained from the Defendant a guarantee certificate in the amount of KRW 423,000,000, to be provided to the NFFC. On 2004. 12. 30., the non-party provided the 1st Mortgage and the guarantee certificate as security and borrowed KRW 470,000,000 in facility damage restoration funds from the NFFC (hereinafter referred to as the “1st Loan”).\\n\\nOn 2008. 12. 9., the non-party entered into a mortgage creation contract with the NFFC, providing that all debts currently and in the future borne by the non-party to the NFFC through credit transactions, etc. would be secured, and had a registration for the creation of a mortgage, with maximum secured amount of KRW 650,000,000, made in favor of the NFFC with respect to the real properties listed in items 3 through 8 of the attached list to the judgment below, owned by the non-party (hereinafter referred to as the “3rd through 8th real properties”) (hereinafter referred to as the “2nd Mortgage”). On 2011. 12. 16., the non-party additionally borrowed KRW 500,000,000 in fisheries finance funds from the NFFC (hereinafter referred to as the “2nd Loan”).\\n\\nb. On 2012. 3. 9., the Plaintiff purchased the 3rd through 8th real properties from the non-party and had the registration of transfer of ownership made in the Plaintiff’s name on 2012. 3. 19.\\n\\nc. The non-party defaulted on the payment of interest on the 1st Loan from 2012. 4. 3., and on the 2nd Loan from 2012. 8. 9. On 2012. 8. 24., the NFFC applied for a voluntary auction based on the 2nd Mortgage with respect to the 3rd through 8th real properties to the Daegu District Court Pohang Branch as Case No. 2012TAGYEONG6906, and on 2012. 8. 28., the voluntary auction proceedings commenced (hereinafter referred to as “the auction in this case”). The amount claimed was KRW 650,000,000 out of a total of KRW 876,000,000, consisting of the remaining balance of the 1st Loan of KRW 376,000,000 and the 2nd Loan of KRW 500,000,000.\\n\\nOn 2012. 8. 24., the Defendant paid KRW 342,997,237 out of the 1st Loan to the NFFC pursuant to the guarantee certificate, and on 2012. 9. 18., had a marginal registration of partial transfer made in favor of the Defendant with respect to the mortgage among the 1st Mortgage whose maximum secured amount was KRW 580,000,000.\\n\\nOn 2012. 11. 19., in order to have the application for the auction in this case withdrawn, the Plaintiff paid to the NFFC a total of KRW 551,168,720, consisting of overdue interest on the 1st Loan in the amount of KRW 18,805,503, principal and interest on the 2nd Loan in the amount of KRW 525,068,491, and auction application costs in the amount of KRW 7,294,726, and, at the NFFC’s request, remitted KRW 150,000,000 to the Defendant. On 2012. 11. 19., the NFFC withdrew the application for the auction in this case and, on the ground of cancellation, cancelled the registration of creation of the 2nd Mortgage.\\n\\nd. Meanwhile, upon the application of Kookmin Bank Co., Ltd., which was the mortgagee with respect to the 1st and 2nd real properties, voluntary auction proceedings commenced on 2012. 9. 20. as Case No. 2012TAGYEONG5533 in the Gyeongju Branch of the Daegu District Court. In the auction proceedings, the Defendant submitted a statement of claim stating the full amount of the reimbursement claim against the non-party, KRW 445,526,188, without excluding the KRW 150,000,000 received from the Plaintiff. Around 2014. 8. 27., a distribution schedule was prepared that distributed KRW 315,413,800 to the Defendant, and the Defendant received the distribution money around that time.\\n\\nOn 2016. 6. 2., the Defendant made a deposit for performance under relative uncertainty with the non-party, the Plaintiff, the NFFC, and Kookmin Bank Co., Ltd. as the deposit beneficiaries. The facts constituting the cause of deposit are that, out of the KRW 315,413,800 distributed as stated above and the KRW 150,000,000 received from the Plaintiff on 2012. 11. 19., KRW 250,853,086 is appropriated to the Defendant’s reimbursement claim against the non-party, and the remaining distribution money of KRW 64,560,714, less the law office fee of KRW 264,800 for the deposit application, i.e., KRW 64,295,914, is deposited.\\n\\ne. The Plaintiff filed the instant action seeking restitution of unjust enrichment on the ground that the payment of KRW 150,000,000 to the Defendant on 2012. 11. 19. lacked legal cause.\\n\\n2. Whether the 1st Loan is included in the secured obligations under the 2nd Mortgage (Ground of Appeal No. 1)\\na. As a general rule, where, at the time a financial institution and a mortgagor enter into a mortgage creation contract, the mortgage creation contract contains language stating that it is to establish a so-called comprehensive mortgage securing all debts arising from the financial institution’s credit transactions, the mortgage creation contract is a dispositive instrument, and, absent special circumstances, the contents of the declaration of intention must be interpreted according to the wording of the contract. However, where the mortgage creation contract is uniformly printed in fixed type and used in the form of general terms and conditions, and, in light of various circumstances such as the circumstances and purpose of the conclusion of the mortgage creation contract, the amount of the secured obligations, and the mutual relationship among the mortgagor, debtor, and creditor, it can be recognized that the parties intended, contrary to the wording of the contract, to make only specific debts the secured obligations, the scope of the security liability must be limited in accordance with the parties’ intention (see Supreme Court Decisions 83DAKA2159, decided June 12, 1984, and 2001DA12430, decided April 11, 2003).\\n\\nb. The court below held, for the following reasons, that the debt for the 1st Loan is included in the secured obligations under the 2nd Mortgage, and determined that the Defendant, who had paid part of the 1st Loan, acquired a part of the 2nd Mortgage by subrogation upon performance.\\n\\n(1) The 2nd mortgage creation contract provides that all debts currently and in the future borne by the non-party to the NFFC through credit transactions, etc. shall be the secured obligations. At the time of creation of the 2nd Mortgage, the non-party was indebted to the NFFC for the 1st Loan. The debt for the 2nd Loan arose approximately 3 years after the 2nd Mortgage was created.\\n\\n(2) Before filing the instant action, the Plaintiff filed an action against the NFFC seeking damages, etc., and the Defendant participated as an intervenor in support of the NFFC. The cause of the claim was as follows: the secured obligations under the 2nd Mortgage are limited to the 2nd Loan and do not include the 1st Loan. Nevertheless, at the NFFC’s request, the Plaintiff paid KRW 150,000,000 of the principal and interest on the 1st Loan and overdue interest thereon, totaling KRW 168,803,503. Since the Plaintiff’s decision to repay the 1st Loan falls under an agreement to repay a non-existent debt, an unconscionable juristic act, a declaration of intention by fraud or duress, etc., the Plaintiff sought restitution of unjust enrichment or damages resulting from a tort with respect to KRW 168,803,503.\\n\\nThe appellate court dismissed all of the Plaintiff’s claims, and the reason was that the 1st Loan is included in the secured obligations under the 2nd Mortgage (Daegu High Court Decision 2015NA21081, decided December 16, 2015). The appellate judgment was affirmed as it was, as the final appeal was dismissed (Supreme Court Decision 2016DA201470, dated April 28, 2016).\\n\\n(3) It is recognized that the Financial Supervisory Service responded, in relation to the Plaintiff’s application for dispute mediation, to the effect that “the debt for the 1st Loan is not included in the secured obligations under the 2nd Mortgage.” However, these facts alone are insufficient to overturn the determination that the debt for the 1st Loan is included in the secured obligations under the 2nd Mortgage.\\n\\nc. Reviewing the reasons of the judgment below in light of the legal principles seen above and the record, the court below’s determination is proper, and, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, there is no error in failing to conduct the necessary examination, in violating the laws of logic and the rules of experience, in exceeding the limits of free evaluation of evidence, or in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the scope of secured obligations under a mortgage, the interpretation of terms and conditions and contracts, etc.\\n\\n3. Whether a marginal registration is always required in subrogation by a surety against a third acquirer (Ground of Appeal No. 2)\\na. Under Articles 480 and 481 of the Civil Act, a person who subrogates the creditor may exercise the rights in respect of the claim and its security to the extent that such person may seek reimbursement by virtue of his or her own rights (Article 482(1) of the Civil Act). Regarding subrogation between a surety and a third acquirer, Article 482(2) item 1 of the Civil Act provides: “A surety may not subrogate the creditor against a third party who acquires rights in the leasehold or mortgaged property unless the subrogation is entered in advance by way of marginal registration in the registration of the leasehold right or mortgage right.”\\n\\nThis provision is intended to protect third acquirers who, believing that the mortgage right, etc. has been extinguished by the surety’s performance, acquire rights in the subject real property from unforeseen loss (see Supreme Court Decision 2012DA99341, decided March 20, 2015). Therefore, if, after the surety has performed the debt, a third acquirer acquires rights in the subject real property while no marginal registration of subrogation has been made with respect to the registration of the mortgage right, etc., the surety may not subrogate the creditor against the third acquirer.\\n\\nHowever, if a surety who has performed the debt after a third acquirer acquired rights in the subject real property subrogates the creditor, such subrogation should be deemed possible even without a marginal registration of subrogation. A third party who acquired rights in the subject real property before the surety’s performance had already acquired the rights knowing the existence of the mortgage right, etc. on the register, and therefore there is no risk of unforeseen loss even if the surety later subrogates.\\n\\nb. The court below determined as follows.\\n\\nThe Plaintiff acquired ownership of the 3rd through 8th real properties, which are the subject matter of the 2nd Mortgage, on 2012. 3. 19., and the Defendant, as surety, thereafter paid KRW 342,997,237 out of the 1st Loan to the NFFC on 2012. 8. 24. Accordingly, even if the Defendant did not make a marginal registration of subrogation with respect to the 2nd Mortgage, the Defendant may subrogate the NFFC against the Plaintiff, who is the third acquirer.\\n\\nc. Reviewing the reasons of the judgment below in light of the record, the court below’s determination that the Defendant, as surety, may subrogate the creditor NFFC against the Plaintiff, who acquired the subject matter of the mortgage before the debt was performed, without a marginal registration of subrogation, is proper in accordance with the legal principles seen above. There is no error in this determination, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, in misapprehending the legal principles concerning subrogation upon performance.\\n\\n4. Remaining grounds of appeal (Grounds of Appeal Nos. 3 and 4)\\na. The court below determined as follows.\\n\\nThe Plaintiff’s payment of KRW 150,000,000 to the Defendant should be regarded as the consideration for the Defendant, who acquired by subrogation a part of the 2nd Mortgage, to withdraw the application for the auction in this case and cancel the 2nd Mortgage. Since the auction application in this case was withdrawn and the 2nd Mortgage was cancelled after the Plaintiff paid KRW 150,000,000 to the Defendant, it cannot be said that the KRW 150,000,000 was paid without legal cause.\\n\\nb. Reviewing the reasons of the judgment below in light of the record, there is no error in the judgment below, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, in failing to conduct the necessary examination, in violating the laws of logic and the rules of experience, in exceeding the limits of free evaluation of evidence, or in misapprehending the legal principles concerning the adversarial principle and unjust enrichment, etc.\\n\\nc. The Plaintiff argues that, although the NFFC had received payment of most of the claim for the 1st Loan from the Defendant, it caused the Plaintiff to pay KRW 150,000,000 to the Defendant, and that this constitutes an abuse of rights.\\n\\nSuch argument is a new contention first raised at the stage of final appeal and does not constitute a lawful ground of appeal against the judgment below. Furthermore, even upon review of the record in light of the relevant legal principles, there is no error in the judgment below in misapprehending the legal principles concerning abuse of rights, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\nThe Plaintiff’s final appeal is without merit and is therefore dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party. The judgment is rendered as follows, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices."}

{"[87DAKA545]": "We examine the grounds of appeal by the Defendant’s litigation representative.\\n\\nWhen a maximum mortgage right becomes fixed, the principal claim arising thereafter is not secured by that maximum mortgage right; where the mortgagee himself applies for auction on the ground of default in the secured obligation, it is appropriate to regard the maximum mortgage right as becoming fixed at the time of such application for auction.\\n\\nAccording to the facts lawfully determined by the lower court, the Defendant, as the holder of the first- and second-ranked maximum mortgage rights, applied for a voluntary auction of the real property in this case on 1984.4.20. based on each of those maximum mortgage rights, and the auction was carried out; according to the record, it is evident that the Defendant received an assignment of the claim at issue against the non-party from the non-party Hyomok Credit Cooperative on 1984.4.25., after the above application for auction had been made, and therefore, this assigned claim cannot be included in the secured claim under the above maximum mortgage right that had already become fixed by the above application for auction.\\n\\nThe lower court judgment rejected the Defendant’s argument to the effect that, in the event of execution of the above maximum mortgage right, there was an agreement to receive the claim of the above Hyomok Credit Cooperative by assignment and to include it in the secured claim, on the ground that there was no evidence to support such contention; examining the contents of the evidence selected by the lower court according to the record, this disposition by the lower court is persuasive, and there is no illegality as argued.\\n\\nUltimately, the argument that the lower court judgment contains an illegality in misunderstanding the scope of the secured claim under the maximum mortgage right and an illegality in misapprehending the evidentiary selection lacks merit; accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, and the costs of appeal shall be borne by the losing party, and the judgment is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating judges as stated in the order."}

{"[88DAKA1797]": "1. We examine Ground 1 of the grounds of appeal by Plaintiff’s counsel, Attorney Yu Gyeong-hui.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons for the lower court judgment, the lower court rejected the Plaintiff’s principal claim on the ground that the Defendant’s receipt from the Plaintiff of KRW 2,768,085,736 by subrogated payment could not constitute unjust enrichment, because it resulted from the Plaintiff’s provision of a payment guarantee for the Defendant’s debt to the Defendant under the reorganization plan of Non-party Beomyang Paper Industrial Co., Ltd., which had been approved by the Gwangju District Court and thereby became final.\\n\\nIn light of the record, the lower court’s above factual findings and determination are reasonable and acceptable, and there is no error in misapprehending the legal principles concerning unjust enrichment; therefore, the contention is without merit.\\n\\n2. We examine Ground 2 of the grounds of appeal by the same Attorney Yu Gyeong-hui and the grounds of appeal by the same Attorney Mun Haeng-du.\\n\\nWhere a person who has a legitimate interest in making payment makes a partial payment by subrogation of a claim for the debtor, the subrogated payer acquires, within the extent of the value paid, the rights concerning the claim and the security interest previously held by the creditor; accordingly, where the creditor has a mortgage over real property, the creditor has a duty to complete the additional registration of partial transfer of the mortgage arising from the partial payment by subrogation to the subrogated payer; however, even in such case, the creditor retains a preferential right of repayment over the partial subrogated payer.\\n\\nAccording to the facts as found by the lower court, after the Non-party Korea Credit Guarantee Fund, which had furnished a payment guarantee to the Defendant on 1983.5.24. for the principal and interest on the loan debt owed by the above company to the Defendant in the amount of US$590,846,575, paid that amount, it was agreed, in receiving transfer of US$500,000 out of the Defendant’s second-ranking mortgage of US$1,000,000 on the mortgaged property in this case, that upon enforcement of auction against the mortgaged property in this case, the Defendant would receive preferential repayment of the remaining claim from the auction proceeds, and the above Korea Credit Guarantee Fund would be repaid only if there were any remaining auction proceeds; and after the Plaintiff, on 1986.5.9., made subrogated payment to the Defendant in the amount of KRW 2,768,085,736, being the principal and interest of the Defendant’s reorganization secured claim for which payment guarantee had been provided under the reorganization plan of the above company, it can be seen that, in receiving transfer of the Defendant’s first-ranking mortgage and the mortgage right corresponding to the remaining US$500,000 out of the second-ranking mortgage on the mortgaged property in this case, with respect to the aforementioned second mortgage, there was an agreement between the Plaintiff and the Defendant that, upon enforcement of auction against the mortgaged property, the Plaintiff would succeed to the preferential right that the Defendant held against the above Korea Credit Guarantee Fund.\\n\\nIf that is so, the Defendant had a preferential right of repayment over the above Korea Credit Guarantee Fund, within the limit of the second-ranking mortgage of US$500,000 among the auction proceeds for the mortgaged property in this case; thus, it should be deemed that the Plaintiff succeeded to the Defendant’s above preferential right within that limit. The lower court’s judgment to the same effect is proper, and it cannot be said that there was any error in misapprehending the legal principles concerning nonperformance of obligations or the legal principles concerning subrogation by a payer as alleged; nor can it be said that the lower court judgment contains any illegality in misconstruing the content of the agreement. The contention is without merit.\\n\\n3. We examine Ground 3 of the grounds of appeal by the same Attorney Yu Gyeong-hui.\\n\\nEven upon close examination of the record, there is no trace that the Plaintiff, in addition to liability under the legal principles of unjust enrichment or nonperformance of obligations toward the Defendant, asserted contractual liability under the agreement of succession as the cause of action and sought reimbursement on that basis; nor does the court have a duty to explain whether a party has asserted a matter that that party is responsible for asserting. Accordingly, the contention that there was an omission to adjudicate or an illegality in failing to perform the duty to explain is also without merit.\\n\\n4. Therefore, since the appeal is without merit, it is dismissed, and the costs of appeal are to be borne by the losing party. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the judges participating in the case, as stated in the disposition."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning preparation, conspiracy, and attempt are correct? (where there is a dispute, according to case law) (a) If A participated in B's commission of the offense of preparatory robbery in the form of aiding and abetting, A cannot be punished as an aider and abettor to the offense of preparatory robbery. (b) Under the Criminal Act, in order to say that there is an agreement on the commission of a crime for the establishment of the offense of conspiracy, it is insufficient merely to externally express or communicate the resolve to commit a crime; objectively, it must be clearly recognized as preparatory conduct for the execution of a specific crime, and substantial danger must be recognized in that agreement. (c) In the case of an abandonment attempt, both the upper and lower limits of the statutory punishment are reduced by one-half, whereas in the case of a frustrated attempt, depending on the degree of danger of infringement of the legal interest, the punishment may either not be reduced or only the lower limit of the statutory punishment may be reduced by one-half. (d) Where acts of preparation or conspiracy, which are punished before the commencement of execution, are involved, the concept of an abandonment attempt cannot be recognized; therefore, even if the offense is discontinued at the preparatory stage, the provisions on an abandonment attempt cannot apply. (e) If A, recognizing that the victim was in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist, had sexual intercourse with the victim with the intent to exploit that condition, but from the time of commencement of execution the victim was in fact not in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist, then if, based on the circumstances A recognized at the time of the act, a reasonable person objectively judged that there was a risk that the result of quasi-rape would occur, an impossible attempt of the offense of quasi-rape is established.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2018DO16002]": "We decide on the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Course of the Case\\n\\na. The Military Prosecutor indicted the Defendant on the following charge of rape.\\n\\nAt around 22:30 on April 17, 2017, while drinking alcohol with the Defendant’s wife and the Victim at his home, after the Defendant’s wife fell asleep first at around 01:00 the next day and the Victim also entered the master bedroom at around 02:00, the Defendant followed the Victim inside, touched the Victim’s breasts while she was lying down, inserted his hand into her panties and touched her genitals, and then, after blocking the Victim’s mouth as she twisted her body and made noises to escape the situation, taking off her pants and panties, had sexual intercourse once and raped her.\\n\\nb. The court of first instance granted the Military Prosecutor’s motion to amend the indictment by adding, as an alternative charge, the following allegation of quasi-rape.\\n\\nAt the date, time, and place stated in subparagraph a. above, the Defendant, by the above method, had sexual intercourse once with the Victim, who was intoxicated and lying down. By doing so, the Defendant raped the Victim by taking advantage of her inability to resist.\\n\\nc. The court of first instance, on the grounds that it could not readily conclude, based solely on the evidence submitted by the Military Prosecutor, that there had been violence or intimidation sufficient to render resistance impossible or markedly difficult, found the principal charge of rape not guilty in the reasoning and found the alternative charge of quasi-rape guilty. Only the Defendant appealed.\\n\\nd. The lower court granted the Military Prosecutor’s motion to amend the indictment by adding, as an alternative charge, the following allegation of attempted quasi-rape.\\n\\nAt the date, time, and place stated in subparagraph a. above, although the Defendant could not rape the Victim, who was not actually so intoxicated as to be unable to resist and was in a state of inability to resist, because the Victim was believed to be so severely intoxicated as to be in a state of inability to resist, the Defendant, by the above method, had sexual intercourse once with the Victim, who was lying down. By doing so, the Defendant attempted to rape the Victim by taking advantage of her inability to resist, but the attempt was not completed.\\n\\ne. The lower court found the portion of quasi-rape that had been held guilty in the court of first instance not guilty in the reasoning, on the ground that the evidence submitted by the Military Prosecutor alone was insufficient to recognize that the Victim was, at the time of this case, in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist, and found guilty of the impossible attempt portion of quasi-rape added as an alternative charge. However, it deleted from the factual allegations the portion stating, “after blocking the Victim’s mouth as she twisted her body and made noises to escape the situation,” on the ground that this was an erroneous entry.\\n\\nf. Only the Defendant filed a final appeal with respect to the guilty portion. As grounds for the final appeal, the Defendant argues as follows: 1) there was no intent for quasi-rape; 2) because the Victim was in fact not in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist and thus engaged in sexual intercourse without infringing sexual self-determination, there was no possibility of the result of quasi-rape or risk of infringement of a protected legal interest, and therefore impossible attempt of the offense of quasi-rape is not established. We decide on these matters in order.\\n\\n2. Grounds of Appeal Alleging No Intent for Quasi-Rape\\n\\na. 1) Article 297 of the Criminal Act provides, “A person who rapes another by violence or intimidation shall be punished by imprisonment for a fixed term of not less than 3 years.” Article 299 provides, “A person who commits sexual intercourse or indecent conduct by taking advantage of another’s state of mental incapacity or inability to resist shall be punished in accordance with Articles 297, 297-2, and 298.” Since the Criminal Act punishes, by analogy to rape, the act of sexual intercourse by taking advantage of a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist, rather than by means of violence or intimidation, the intent for quasi-rape means an inner will to recognize that the victim is in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist and that sexual intercourse is being committed by taking advantage of such state, and to tolerate the possibility of the occurrence of the constitutive result.\\n\\n2) Where the Defendant denies intent, which is a subjective element of the constituent elements of the offense, the criminal intent itself cannot be proved objectively; therefore, by the nature of things, it must be proved by proving indirect facts or circumstantial facts that are related to the criminal intent. In determining what constitutes relevant indirect facts or circumstantial facts at this point, one must do so by rationally assessing the connected state of facts based on normal rules of experience and with careful observation and analytical ability (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2005DO8645, decided February 23, 2006). Meanwhile, conditional intent, which is a type of intent, requires recognition of the possibility of the occurrence of the criminal facts and, further, an inner will to tolerate the risk of the occurrence of the criminal facts. Whether the actor tolerated the possibility that the criminal facts would occur must be inferred from the actor’s psychological state by considering the form of the actor’s externally manifested conduct and the circumstances of the conduct, without relying on the actor’s statements, while taking into account how an ordinary person would evaluate the possibility that the relevant criminal facts would occur (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2004DO74, decided May 14, 2004; Supreme Court Decision 2016DO15470, decided January 12, 2017).\\n\\n3) In addition, recognition of criminal facts must reach the level of proof beyond a reasonable doubt (Article 359(2) of the Military Court Act; Article 307(2) of the Criminal Procedure Act), but the selection and weighing of evidence conducted as a premise for factual determination, and the probative value of evidence, belong to the free evaluation of the trial court of fact (Article 360 of the Military Court Act; Article 308 of the Criminal Procedure Act). This means that it is within the judge’s free evaluation of evidence to select and use the necessary evidence among the evidence having evidentiary capacity and to assess the substantive value of the evidence in recognizing the facts. Therefore, unless a judge rejects sufficiently probative evidence without reasonable grounds or, conversely, adopts and uses evidence that plainly contradicts objective facts without any reasonable grounds, thereby violating the rules of logic and experience, the judge may, based on free evaluation of evidence, adopt evidence and recognize facts (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2007DO1755, decided May 29, 2008; Supreme Court en banc Decision 2013DO11650, decided August 20, 2015).\\n\\nb. The lower court, for the reasons stated in its opinion, determined that the Defendant had intent for quasi-rape. The ground of appeal on this point merely disputes such factual findings of the lower court and criticizes the lower court’s choice of evidence and evaluation of probative value, which belong to the free evaluation of the trial court of fact. Even in light of the following circumstances discernible from the lower court’s reasoning and from the evidence lawfully admitted and examined above, namely, the circumstances in which the Defendant, the Defendant’s wife, and the Victim drank together; the respective amounts of alcohol consumed by the Defendant and the Victim; the situation in which the Victim, even if she had not reached a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist, was intoxicated after drinking for a long time beyond her capacity, entered the master bedroom, and lay down; the Victim’s condition when the Defendant commenced the act of quasi-rape; and the content of the text messages exchanged between the Defendant and the Victim after the offense, it was proper for the lower court to recognize that the Defendant had intent for quasi-rape. There is no error in the lower court’s judgment, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, that violates the rules of logic and experience, exceeds the limits of free evaluation of evidence, or misapprehends the legal principles on intent for quasi-rape.\\n\\n3. Grounds of Appeal Alleging That Impossible Attempt of Quasi-Rape Is Not Established\\n\\na. Article 300 of the Criminal Act punishes attempts of the offense of quasi-rape. In addition, Article 27 of the Criminal Act provides, “A person shall be punished when, although the occurrence of the result is impossible due to a mistake as to the means or object of execution, there is danger. However, the punishment may be mitigated or remitted,” thereby punishing impossible attempts.\\n\\nAccordingly, where the Defendant, believing that the Victim was in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist and, with the intent to commit sexual intercourse by taking advantage of such state, had sexual intercourse with the Victim, but the Victim was in fact not in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist, then, due to a mistake as to the means or object of execution, the occurrence of the constitutive result prescribed in the offense of quasi-rape was impossible from the outset, and it cannot be said that such result actually occurred. Since the Defendant commenced the execution of quasi-rape but the offense did not reach consummation, an attempt of the offense of quasi-rape is established. Because, from the standpoint of an ordinary person objectively evaluating the circumstances recognized by the Defendant at the time of the act, there was a risk of the result of quasi-rape occurring, impossible attempt of the offense of quasi-rape is established (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2005DO8105, decided December 8, 2005; Supreme Court Decision 2015DO7343, decided August 13, 2015).\\n\\nb. The specific reasons are as follows.\\n\\n1) Impossible attempt as provided in Article 27 of the Criminal Act refers to a case in which the actor has criminal intent and has engaged in conduct that can be regarded as commencement of execution, but due to a mistake as to the means or object of execution, there is from the outset no possibility of satisfying the constituent elements. However, although fulfillment of the constituent elements is impossible as a result, if the conduct is dangerous, it is punished as impossible attempt. Impossible attempt differs from factual mistake in that the actor mistakenly believes that a fact that does not actually exist does exist.\\n\\n2) The Criminal Act provides in Article 25(1), “When a person has commenced the execution of a crime but has failed to complete the act or the result has not occurred, the person shall be punished as an attempt,” thereby providing for a thwarted attempt, and in Article 26, “When an offender voluntarily ceases the act commenced for execution or prevents the occurrence of the result caused by such act, the punishment shall be mitigated or remitted,” thereby providing for an abandoned attempt. A thwarted attempt or abandoned attempt is distinguished from impossible attempt, because, when the act of commencement of execution is viewed, there was a possibility that the intended completed offense would be established, and thus there was a possibility that the constitutive result could occur.\\n\\n3) The “mistake as to the means or object of execution” prescribed in Article 27 of the Criminal Act means that, due to the nature of the means of conduct or object of conduct attempted by the actor, occurrence of the result is impossible from the outset. And “impossibility of occurrence of the result” should be understood to mean that the offense cannot be completed because of the original impossibility of the means or object of execution.\\n\\nMeanwhile, the “danger” constituting a requirement for impossible attempt, which is distinguished from an impossible offense, should be determined by objectively considering, from the standpoint of an ordinary person, the circumstances recognized by the Defendant at the time of the act, and asking whether there was a possibility of the occurrence of the result (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 77DO4049, decided March 28, 1978; Supreme Court Decision 2005DO8105, decided December 8, 2005).\\n\\n4) The offense of quasi-rape prescribed in Article 299 of the Criminal Act is an offense established by committing sexual intercourse by taking advantage of another person’s state of mental incapacity or inability to resist, and its protected legal interest is the sexual self-determination of a person who cannot exercise sexual self-defense due to mental or physical circumstances (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 98DO3257, decided May 26, 2000). Because a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist must exist in the victimized person, the object of the act in the offense of quasi-rape is a “person in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist.” And the act corresponding to the constituent elements is “committing sexual intercourse by taking advantage of such state of mental incapacity or inability to resist.” If sexual intercourse is committed against a person in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist by taking advantage of such state, the constituent elements are satisfied and the offense of quasi-rape is consummated.\\n\\nIf the Defendant believed that the Victim was in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist and had sexual intercourse with the intent to commit sexual intercourse by taking advantage of such state, but the Victim was in fact not in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist from the beginning of the commencement of execution, it may be said that, due to a mistake as to the means or object of execution, there was no possibility of consummation of the offense of quasi-rape from the outset. In such a case, if, from the standpoint of an ordinary person objectively considering the circumstances recognized by the Defendant at the time of the act, there was a risk that the result of quasi-rape would occur, thereby infringing the sexual self-determination of a person who cannot exercise sexual self-defense due to mental or physical circumstances, impossible attempt is established.\\n\\nc. Examining the reasoning of the lower court judgment in light of the legal principles above, this case corresponds to a situation in which the Defendant had sexual intercourse with the Victim with intent for quasi-rape, but the Victim was in fact not in a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist, so that the occurrence of the result of quasi-rape was impossible due to a mistake as to the means or object of execution, and, from the standpoint of an ordinary person objectively considering the circumstances recognized by the Defendant, there is danger because there was a possibility of the occurrence of the result. Although some portions of the reasoning of the lower court judgment are not entirely proper, the lower court’s conclusion that impossible attempt of the offense of quasi-rape is guilty is proper. There is no error in the lower court’s judgment, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, in misapprehending the legal principles on impossible attempt of the offense of quasi-rape.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, the final appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition. In this judgment, the opinions of the Justices were unanimous except for the dissenting opinion of Justices Kwon Soon-il, Ahn Chul-sang, and Kim Sang-hwan on whether impossible attempt of the offense of quasi-rape is established; there are also supplementary opinions by Justices Park Sang-ok, Park Jeong-hwa, and Kim Seon-su in support of the majority opinion, and supplementary opinions by Justices Min Yu-sook and No Jeong-hee.\\n\\n5. Dissenting Opinion of Justices Kwon Soon-il, Ahn Chul-sang, and Kim Sang-hwan\\n\\na. 1) Article 13 of the Criminal Act (Intent) provides, “An act that does not recognize the facts constituting an element of a crime shall not be punished.” Here, the “facts constituting an element of a crime” means the objective constituent elements, which are external indicia in the constituent elements of offenses prescribed in the Criminal Act, namely, the actor, object, act, result, etc. By contrast, the psychological or mental state belonging to the actor’s inner self is called a subjective constituent element, of which intent is the typical example. Since Article 13 of the Criminal Act provides that, for a willful offense to be established, the actor must have recognition of the actor, object, act, result, etc. that are objective constituent elements, where the constituent elements require a special mode of conduct, such as “violence or intimidation” in rape or “taking advantage of a state of mental incapacity or inability to resist” in quasi-rape, the actor must also recognize the existence of such circumstances.\\n\\n2) The Criminal Act provides in Chapter 32 of Part II the “Offenses of Rape and Indecent Acts.” The offenses prescribed in this Chapter are all crimes that involve infringement of an individual’s sexual freedom or sexual self-determination, and their basic constituent elements are the offense of rape (Article 297) and the offense of forcible indecent assault (Article 298). Rape is an offense established by raping another person by violence or intimidation. Rape means sexual intercourse with another person by making resistance impossible or markedly difficult through violence or intimidation. Sexual intercourse broadly means an unlawful act of satisfying sexual desire, but here it means insertion of the male genital organ into the female genital organ. In the offense of rape, the act constituting the offense is rape, its special mode of conduct is “violence or intimidation,” the object is a person, and the constitutive result is sexual intercourse.
