According to the facts established by the first-instance judgment as upheld by the court below and the evidence cited therein, at the time of the offenses in this case, Defendant 1, due to schizophrenic symptoms and an uncontrollable impulse toward arson, committed eight successive acts of arson over only 6 days while in a state of weakened ability to discern things or decide his will; therefore, the court below’s action in upholding the first-instance judgment that recognized the Defendant as a person of diminished capacity and punished him by applying Article 10(2) of the Criminal Act is proper, and there is no illegality in misapprehending the legal principles on diminished capacity or in misapprehending the facts. Accordingly, the ground of final appeal is without merit.\\n\\n2. With respect to Defendant 1’s grounds for final appeal,\\nTaken together, the evidence cited in the first-instance judgment as upheld by the court below is sufficient to recognize the arson of the hotel stated in item 1.(a) of the first-instance judgment, and there is no material to find that Defendant’s consistent confession from the time of the police investigation through the second trial date in the first-instance court lacked voluntariness or that the content of the confession lacked truthfulness and is therefore unreliable; nor can any illegality of insufficient deliberation or misapprehension of legal principles be found in the court below’s action. Thus, the ground of final appeal can only be said to lack merit.\\n\\nMeanwhile, examining from the record the Defendant’s age, character and conduct, intelligence and environment, relationship with the victim, motive for the offense, means and result, and circumstances after the offense, which serve as materials for sentencing, the court below’s action in upholding the first-instance court’s determination of the Defendant’s sentence appears reasonable, and there is no reason to deem it excessively heavy and improper. Accordingly, the ground of final appeal on this point is also without merit.\\n\\n3. With respect to the grounds for final appeal of Defendants 2 and 3,\\n(1) Taken together, the evidence cited in the first-instance judgment as cited by the court below is sufficient to recognize the facts constituting the offense of occupational negligence causing death or injury by the Defendants, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality of misapprehension of legal principles in the course by which the court below reached this conclusion.\\n\\nAccording to what the court below lawfully found, the Defendants, as the president and maintenance manager of each hotel, had a duty of care in the course of their duties to ensure that, if a fire occurred, type A fire doors blocking stairways and corridors so that the fire would not spread would always open and close automatically, and that type B fire doors (emergency doors) on each floor would be managed so that guests could promptly escape and evacuate and would open as they were whenever merely pushed from inside toward the outside escape direction; and to manage the facilities so that in the event of a fire the detector, receiver, main alarm bell, and local alarm bell notifying every floor and each room would operate perfectly and normally immediately. Nevertheless, they neglected this duty, and on the ground that false alarms occurred frequently, they turned off the local alarm bell switch of the receiver, which was the automatic fire detection and alarm equipment, and sealed over it with Scotch tape, and caused employees, on the ground that it spoiled the business appearance, to keep the type A fire doors installed on each floor open by securing them with wooden props from around 06:00 to 24:00 every day; and they kept the type B fire doors (emergency doors) leading to the outdoor emergency staircase fastened, for reasons such as preventing theft, by fitting the steel plate hook attached to the door into the long latch attached to the building, so that in an emergency a person making a hurried escape could not open them by pushing them as they were without removing the steel plate hook, thereby making them fail to fulfill their function as escape routes. The Defendants’ breach of duty would, as a result, in the event of a fire in the building, prevent the fire from being promptly reported to guests and others, make the prevention of spread to the upper and lower floors from the point of ignition inadequate, and also prevent guests and others from being promptly evacuated outdoors through the emergency exits; this is plainly apparent from experience and thus was sufficiently foreseeable.\\n\\nIn offenses of negligence, the intellectual element of blameworthiness means awareness of the possibility of the occurrence of the result; conscious negligence has such awareness, while unconscious negligence does not even have such awareness itself, but in the former responsibility arises of course, and even in the latter, negligence liability generally exists as normative liability for carelessness in not recognizing the occurrence of the result. Therefore, in light of the facts finally established in the preceding sentence, the argument that the Defendants had no negligence causally related to the occurrence of the result, or that there was no subjective foreseeability of the result and no possibility of expecting the actor to avoid the result, is an arbitrary view and cannot be accepted.\\n\\n(2) The first-instance judgment cited by the court below held, as to Defendant 2, that Defendant 2, as the private proprietor of the hotel, in overall control of the management and administration of the hotel, not only had the duty of care stated in the first half of subparagraph (1) above regarding Defendant 3, but also had the duty of care in the course of duties to prevent the occurrence and spread of fire accidents by confirming and directing and supervising Defendant 3 to take the measures stated therein; and this action of the court below is proper. Therefore, even if the circumstances advanced in the argument existed, they could not be grounds for relieving the Defendant of liability, and thus the ground of final appeal is also without merit.\\n\\n4. In the end, as the prosecutor’s final appeal against Defendant 1 and the respective final appeals of the Defendants are all without merit, they are each dismissed, and it is so adjudged as ordered by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[93Do1873]": "We jointly determine the grounds of appeal by the Defendant and his counsel.\\n\\nWhere a person who instigated another to commit bodily injury or serious bodily injury thereby instigated the person so instigated, but the person so instigated went beyond that and actually committed murder, the instigator will generally be liable as an instigator of the offense of bodily injury or serious bodily injury; however, in such a case, where the instigator had negligence or foreseeability with respect to the result of the victim’s death, liability as an instigator of the offense of bodily injury resulting in death may be imposed.\\n\\nThe court of original instance, on the same purport, and based on each piece of evidence recited in the first-instance judgment cited by the court below, found that, in order to retaliate against the victim, who had been interfering with the Defendant’s business on every occasion and had been threatening him, the Defendant, after being introduced to the person not party to the case who had previously been serving as the victim’s bodyguard but later became estranged, provided KRW 5,000,000 under the name of an advance payment and thereby instigated that person to inflict serious bodily injury on the victim so as to prevent him from carrying on his activities; that the said person not party to the case then stabbed the victim all over his body with a knife and killed him; and that, in light of the circumstances at that time, the Defendant could have foreseen that if serious bodily injury were inflicted, the victim might die, and then convicted the Defendant as an instigator of the offense of bodily injury resulting in death, and such disposition is just and well-founded, and there is no illegality in it, such as incomplete deliberation or error in fact-finding due to violation of the rules of evidence evaluation, or error of law concerning the instigator of the offense of bodily injury resulting in death, as alleged. All arguments are without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and part of the period of detention after the filing of the appeal is credited toward the principal sentence, and judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[94Do2842]": "The grounds of appeal submitted by the Defendants and their counsel are considered together.\\n\\n1. With respect to ground of appeal No. 1 raised by counsel for Defendant 1\\n\\nAlthough the offense of special obstruction of the performance of official duties resulting in injury is originally a result-aggravated offense, it is not a true result-aggravated offense punishable only in cases where the serious result was not foreseen despite foreseeability thereof, but rather an improper result-aggravated offense that includes not only cases where the serious result was not foreseen despite foreseeability thereof, but also cases involving intent (see Supreme Court Decision 90DO765, rendered on 1990.6.26.). However, it cannot be deemed that, because a result-aggravated offense thus includes cases in which a serious result is intentionally caused, even in cases where there exists a provision that punishes intentional offenses more severely, the offender cannot be punished with the punishment prescribed for intentional offenses. A result-aggravated offense is a crime in which the punishment is aggravated even when the actor did not foresee the serious result; if even in cases where the serious result is intentionally caused, the offense were to be treated as a result-aggravated offense and thus could not be punished with the punishment prescribed for the intentional offense that is punished more severely, the result would be that it is punished more lightly by being charged as a result-aggravated offense. Therefore, where a separate constituent element providing for heavier punishment has been established for cases in which a serious result is intentionally caused, it must naturally be punished with the punishment prescribed in that heavier-punishment constituent element, and where the punishment for a result-aggravated offense is heavier, it should be possible to punish it with the punishment prescribed for the result-aggravated offense. Therefore, in the case of an improper result-aggravated offense in which a serious result is intentionally caused through the basic offense, if the serious result corresponds to a separate constituent element, it must be deemed to stand in a relation of ideal concurrence between the result-aggravated offense and the intentional offense as to the serious result (see Supreme Court Decision 90DO670, rendered on 1990.5.8.).\\n\\nIn light of the foregoing legal doctrine, the court below's measure of maintaining in full the first-instance judgment, which convicted the criminal facts under item “2. (b)” as stated in the first-instance judgment against Defendant 1 as a case of ideal concurrence between the offense of special obstruction of the performance of official duties resulting in injury and the offense of violating Article 3(2)1 of the Act on the Punishment of Violences, etc. and Article 257(1) (Injury) of the Criminal Act, is proper, and there is no error of misunderstanding the legal doctrine concerning result-aggravated offenses and ideal concurrence. The portion of the grounds of appeal pointing this out is without merit.\\n\\n2. With respect to ground of appeal No. 2 raised by counsel for Defendant 1 and the ground of appeal by Defendant 1\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the judgment below in light of the record, the judgment below’s determination that Defendant 1 was not in a state of mental and physical loss or diminished mental and physical capacity at the time of the second offense stated in the first-instance judgment is proper, and there is no error in fact-finding due to a violation of the rules of evidence or due to incomplete deliberation, and upon examining the sentencing conditions shown in the record of this case, the determination of the sentence imposed on the Defendant is also appropriate. The portion of the grounds of appeal pointing this out is likewise without merit.\\n\\n3. With respect to the grounds of appeal by Defendant 2 and his counsel\\n\\nExamining the reasons of the judgment below in light of the record, it is proper that the court below maintained the first-instance court’s measure of finding Defendant guilty of the criminal facts stated in the relevant part of the judgment by comprehensively considering the evidence cited in that judgment, and there is no error of violating the rules of evidence or of failing to conduct a full hearing, and the point of mere factual error does not constitute a lawful ground of appeal in this case in which Defendant was sentenced to imprisonment for 3 years. All grounds of appeal are unacceptable.\\n\\n4. Therefore, all appeals are dismissed, and 30 days out of the period of detention after appeal are to be credited toward the principal sentence in the first-instance judgment against the Defendants, and the judgment is rendered in accordance with the disposition by the agreement of the participating Justices."}

question: Which of the following explanations concerning crimes protecting the judicial function of the State is incorrect? (If there is a dispute, according to precedents)
A: Criminal intent for the crime of false accusation may be recognized not only in cases where the informant reports facts that he is certain are false, but also in cases where he reports facts without being certain that they are true.
B: Even if a person reported false facts to a public office for the purpose of causing another person to receive criminal punishment, if the facts are such that, as an offense subject to complaint, the complaint period has elapsed and prosecution cannot be instituted, and this is clear from the contents of the report itself, the crime of false accusation is not established.
C: Where the falsely reported fact could have been the subject of criminal punishment at the time of the false accusation, the crime of false accusation is established, and even if precedents are later changed so that such fact does not become a criminal offense, it does not affect the already established crime of false accusation unless there are special circumstances.
D: If A, having appeared as a witness at the 9th trial date of Case A and having made a false statement, had the witness examination procedure end as it was without any withdrawal or correction, and thereafter A again appeared at the 21st trial date, was informed that the effect of the previous oath remained in force, and, while testifying, admitted that the statement made at the previous date was a false statement and made a statement to the effect of withdrawing it, then the crime of perjury is not established against A.
E: If Defense counsel A, in order to obtain a reduced sentence for A, repeatedly transferred money from A's bank account to a bank account in the name of Company B and then received it back, and thereafter obtained only the remittance records among them and submitted them to the court together with a false assertion that 200 million won had been repaid, the crime of fabrication of evidence is not established against A.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2010DO7525]": "The guilty portion of the lower court judgment and the acquittal portion concerning the charge of instigation of perjury are reversed, and this case is remanded to the Gwangju High Court. The remainder of the Prosecutor’s appeal is dismissed."}

{"[2015DO15398]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. The crime of false accusation is established when, for the purpose of causing another person to receive criminal punishment or disciplinary action, false facts are reported to a public office or public official (Article 156 of the Criminal Act). Although the crime of false accusation incidentally also protects the interest of an individual in not being unjustly punished or disciplined, its primary protected legal interest is the proper exercise of the State’s criminal justice authority or disciplinary authority (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2005DO2712, rendered on 2005. 9. 30.).\\n\\nIn order for an act of reporting “false facts” for the purpose of causing another person to receive criminal punishment to constitute the crime of false accusation, the reported facts themselves must be capable of being subject to criminal punishment; thus, even if false facts were reported, false accusation is not established if, at the time of the report, those facts themselves do not constitute a criminal offense (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2006DO558, rendered on 2007. 4. 13.). However, where the falsely reported facts could have been subject to criminal punishment at the time of the false accusation, the risk of impairing the proper exercise of the State’s criminal justice authority and the risk of infringing the individual’s legal stability against unjust punishment have already arisen; therefore, the crime of false accusation is consummated, and even if the precedent is later changed so that such facts are no longer deemed criminal, it does not affect an already established crime of false accusation absent special circumstances.\\n\\n2. a. The lower court found the charged facts of this case guilty on the following grounds, holding that the contents of the Defendant’s complaint constituted false facts, that the Defendant also knew of these circumstances, and that, at the time of the false accusation, the facts reported by the Defendant themselves could have been the cause of criminal punishment.\\n\\n(1) The Defendant was a director of Non-party 1 Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Non-party 1 Company”), and on 2014. 1. 9., he submitted to the civil petitions office of the Busan District Prosecutors’ Office a complaint against Non-party 3, who was the representative of Non-party 2 Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Non-party 2 Company”), stating: “The Defendant purchased ○○○○Ville (room number 1 omitted) and (room number 2 omitted) from the side of the accused Non-party 3 on 2009. 9. 2., but since the accused Non-party 3 double-sold them to another person, please punish him.” Thereafter, when making a statement as the complainant on 2014. 2. 6. at the office of the investigation division of the Busan District Prosecutors’ Office, the Defendant stated: “For the progress payment of KRW 150,000,000 for the interior finishing work of ○○○○Ville, which Non-party 1 Company had contracted from Non-party 2 Company and carried out, I agreed with Non-party 3 on 2009. 9. 1. to the construction price of KRW 90,000,000 and received two units of ○○○○Ville as the method of repayment. Nevertheless, since Non-party 3 did not transfer these to me and sold them to another person around 2014. 1., please punish him.” (hereinafter referred to as “the complaint in this case”).\\n\\n(2) The Defendant asserted that he agreed with Non-party 3 on the construction price for this construction work at KRW 90,000,000 and that, if Non-party 3 could not pay it, he would instead receive two units of ○○○○Ville as payment in kind; however, the Defendant has failed to submit objective materials concerning the contents of the work he performed, the progress rate, or the amount of completed work accordingly. Rather, the work performed by the Defendant consisted only of some paint work and fence work, and the construction price was only KRW 6,500,000; it appears that the Defendant received the full KRW 6,500,000 from Non-party 3, and that the creditor-debtor relationship between the two was fully settled.\\n\\n(3) Before the complaint in this case, the Defendant had filed a criminal complaint against Non-party 3 in relation to this construction work on suspicion of fraud, but on 2009. 12. 24., Non-party 3 was acquitted on appeal on the ground that the amount of construction payment to be received by the Defendant was only KRW 6,500,000, unlike the amount claimed to the investigative authorities (KRW 500,000,000) (Busan District Court 2009NO1085), and that judgment became final and conclusive as is when the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal on 2010. 4. 29. (Supreme Court 2010DO482).\\n\\n(4) Pursuant to the Defendant’s complaint in this case, Non-party 3 was investigated by the prosecution as a suspect regarding the above complaint facts.\\n\\n(5) At the time of the complaint in this case and the investigation, Supreme Court precedent held that “where a debtor who concluded a reservation for substitute performance concerning real property as security for a claim disposes of the real property agreed to be delivered in substitution, the crime of breach of trust is established” (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2000DO4293, rendered on 2000. 12. 8.); however, by a judgment of the Supreme Court en banc rendered on 2014. 8. 21., the Supreme Court changed its precedent and held that breach of trust is not established in such a case (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2014DO3363).\\n\\nb. The lower court’s determination is proper in light of the legal principles set forth above. There is no error in the lower court’s determination in misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the crime of false accusation, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nThe Defendant’s appeal is without merit, and is therefore dismissed. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the case."}

{"[2018DO1818]": "The Court examines ex officio.\\n\\n1. Even if a person reported false facts to a public office for the purpose of causing another person to receive criminal punishment, where the facts are, as an offense subject to complaint, such that prosecution cannot be instituted because the complaint period has expired and this is clear from the contents of the report itself, there is no risk of misleading the duties of the relevant state agency; therefore, in such a case, the offense of false accusation is not established (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 98DO150 rendered on 1998. 4. 14.).\\nMeanwhile, according to the provisions of Articles 354 and 328 of the Criminal Act, fraud committed between lineal blood relatives, spouses, cohabiting relatives, cohabiting family members, or their spouses shall be exempted from punishment, and between relatives other than such persons, prosecution may be instituted only upon complaint. In addition, under Article 230(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act, the complaint period is 6 months from the day the offender is known.\\nHere, “knowing the offender” means, from the standpoint of an ordinary person, knowing the facts of the crime and the offender to the extent that the person entitled to file a complaint can do so, and “knowing the facts of the crime” means that the person entitled to file a complaint has a definitive awareness of the factual circumstances that there was harm from a crime falling under an offense subject to complaint (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2001DO3106 rendered on 2001. 10. 9.).\\n2. The gist of the charges in this case is as follows.\\na. Defendant 1 was sentenced to imprisonment for 2 years and 4 months for an offense in violation of the Act on the Control of Narcotics, etc. (psychotropic substances), etc., and while he was incarcerated in ○○ Prison after the sentence became final, he instigated his biological older sister, Defendant 2, to falsely accuse him of fraud to the ○○ District Prosecutors' Office, △△ Branch Office, in order to be transferred to △△ Prison where his family was living.\\nb. Defendant 2 accepted this and, around 2015. 11. 30., drafted a false complaint to the effect that “Defendant 1 borrowed 50,000,000 won on 2012. 10. 1. and has not yet repaid it, so please punish him for fraud,” and submitted the complaint by mail to ○○ District Court, △△ Branch Court on the same day, and around 2015. 12. 3., caused a public official belonging to △△ Branch Court whose name is unknown to file the above complaint with the ○○ District Prosecutors' Office, △△ Branch Office, thereby falsely accusing Defendant 1.\\n3. a. Even according to the statement of the charges in this case, since the Defendants are biological siblings, the fraud case for which Defendant 2 complained against Defendant 1 falls within a case in which prosecution may be instituted only if Defendant 2 files a lawful complaint.\\nb. However, according to the record, the following facts can be ascertained.\\n(1) Defendant 2, in accordance with the instigation of false accusation as stated in the charges against Defendant 1, drafted a complaint stating that “the accused, Defendant 1, borrowed 50,000,000 won from the complainant, Defendant 2, on 2012. 10. 1. with the promise to open a coffee shop in □□ and repay the money, and was to repay it by 2015. 10. 1., but because he is currently serving his sentence at ○○ Prison and is not fulfilling the promise, I was compelled to file this complaint,” and attempted to file it with the △△ Police Station, but was refused by the police officer in charge of receiving filings on the ground that the Defendants were relatives.\\n(2) Accordingly, Defendant 2 submitted the above complaint by mail to ○○ District Court, △△ Branch Court, and around 2015. 12. 3., a public official belonging to △△ Branch Court whose name is unknown filed the above complaint with the ○○ District Prosecutors' Office, △△ Branch Office.\\n(3) Defendant 2, during her statement as complainant in the investigation conducted at the △△ Police Station pursuant to the above complaint, stated, in essence, that “my younger brother, Defendant 1, said that if I lent him the money necessary to open a coffee shop in □□, he would repay it by around 2012. 10., so I lent him a total of 50,000,000 won, consisting of 30,000,000 won around 2012. 3. and 20,000,000 won around 2012. 9.; however, he did not open the coffee shop and did not repay it even by October, so on 2012. 10. 1. I asked him to prepare a loan certificate. Accordingly, Defendant 1 prepared a loan certificate stating that he would repay 50,000,000 won by 2015. 10. 1.”\\n(4) Defendant 1 likewise, during police and prosecutorial interrogation as a suspect, made statements consistent with Defendant 2’s above police statement, and stated that, at the time he borrowed money from Defendant 2, he had almost no property in his own name and that he was correct in saying that he had neither the intention nor the ability to repay the money.\\nc. Examining Defendant 2’s complaint and her statements to the police as above in light of the legal principles set forth earlier, it appears from the contents of the report itself that, at the time Defendant 2 received a loan certificate from Defendant 1 on 2012. 10. 1., she knew that Defendant 1 had not used the above money for opening the coffee shop, which had been the purpose when he borrowed the money in the first place, and that he lacked the ability to repay.\\nTherefore, as of around 2012. 10. 1., Defendant 2 had a definitive awareness that she had suffered harm from a fraud offense to an extent sufficient to file a complaint against Defendant 1, so the complaint period began to run around that time, and there is considerable room to conclude that by 2015. 12. 3., when the complaint was filed with the ○○ District Prosecutors' Office, △△ Branch Office, that complaint period had already expired. If viewed in this way, Defendant 2’s false complaint of fraud would fall under a case where it is clear from the contents of the report itself that prosecution could not be instituted because the complaint period had expired, and thus the offense of false accusation would not be established; as a result, Defendant 1’s offense of instigating false accusation would also not be established.\\nd. Nevertheless, the court below, without conducting any particular examination as to whether Defendant 2’s complaint period had expired, found both the charge of instigating false accusation against Defendant 1 in this case and the charge of false accusation against Defendant 2 guilty. In this determination by the court below, there is error that affected the judgment by misunderstanding the legal principles concerning the complaint period for an offense subject to complaint and the establishment of the offense of false accusation.\\n4. Therefore, without omitting judgment on the Defendants’ grounds of appeal, the judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for a new trial and determination, and accordingly, the judgment is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as set forth in the disposition."}

{"[2020DO2642]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Summary of the Facts Charged\\nThe Defendant, while meeting the client, Non-party 1, at ○○ Prison located in ○○ City (address omitted) around April 2018, advised him to the effect that “if it is made to appear that all of the money received from Non-party 2 Company (hereinafter referred to as the ‘Non-party 2 Company’) has been returned, a reduction in sentence may be obtained. Since there is no money to return, there is a method of depositing money into the Non-party 2 Company’s account and then receiving it back, repeating this and revolving the funds.” Non-party 1 accepted this. Upon hearing through Non-party 1’s acquaintance, Non-party 3, words to the effect that “as a result of contacting the Non-party 2 Company side, it seems likely that if money is sent, it can be received back again,” the Defendant caused Non-party 3 to have Non-party 1’s older sister, Non-party 4, transfer funds to a △△ Bank account in the name of Non-party 2 Company. Non-party 4, around May 18, 2018, transferred 70,000,000 won to the △△ Bank account in the name of Non-party 2 Company, and then immediately received back the above 70,000,000 won from the Non-party 2 Company side into a □□ Bank account in Non-party 4’s name; thereafter, by the same method, she deposited 50,000,000 won on May 24, 2018, 30,000,000 won on May 30, 2018, 20,000,000 won on June 1, 2018, 60,000,000 won on June 7, 2018, 70,000,000 won on June 14, 2018, 20,000,000 won on June 26, 2018, and 30,000,000 won on June 29, 2018, each into the △△ Bank account in the name of Non-party 2 Company, and then immediately received them back into the □□ Bank account in Non-party 4’s name, and around that time faxed the deposit materials thus falsely created to the Defendant.\\n\\nAccordingly, the Defendant, notwithstanding that he had not returned any money at all to the Non-party 2 Company side as stated above, asserted that Non-party 1 had returned in full the 350,000,000 won received from the Non-party 2 Company side, and around June 20, 2018, submitted to the appellate trial panel in Non-party 1’s case one consolidated voucher received from Non-party 4 as above and five deposit confirmation certificates (total returned money: 300,000,000 won), and thereafter, on June 25, 2018, submitted to the same panel a written brief stating, to the effect that Non-party 1 had returned in full the brokerage compensation received and therefore should receive a reduction in sentence, and around July 2, 2018, further submitted two deposit confirmation certificates (total returned money: 50,000,000 won) to the same panel.\\n\\nBy doing so, the Defendant, in collusion with Non-party 3, fabricated sentencing evidence concerning Non-party 1’s criminal case and used the fabricated evidence.\\n\\n2. Judgment of the Lower Court\\nFor the reasons stated in its opinion, the court below held that “evidence concerning a criminal case or disciplinary case” in Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act includes not only materials relating to whether a crime is established but also materials relating to sentencing, and that the Defendant, in collusion with Non-party 1, etc., caused meaningless deposit and withdrawal entries to arise between Non-party 4 and Non-party 2 Company by remitting funds to a bank account in the name of Non-party 2 Company and then receiving them back again, and thereafter extracting only the deposit records, which were part of the entire transaction records, and submitting them to the court as sentencing materials, constituted an act of creating novel and spurious materials that possess content and value conforming to false factual elements, as evidence created to prove the nonexistent fact that “Non-party 1 returned 350,000,000 won to Non-party 2 Company and Non-party 2 Company received all of it,” and thus constituted “forgery” of evidence, and accordingly found the facts charged in this case guilty.\\n\\n3. Judgment of the Supreme Court\\nA. The term “evidence” in the offense of forgery of evidence under Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act means all materials deemed relevant to the investigative agency, court, or disciplinary authority’s confirmation of whether the State’s power to punish or disciplinary power exists with respect to another person’s criminal case or disciplinary case (see Supreme Court Judgment dated June 28, 2007, 2002DO3600, etc.). Therefore, not only materials concerning whether a crime or disciplinary cause is established, but also materials helpful in recognizing mitigating or aggravating circumstances relating to punishment or discipline, are included in the evidence prescribed by this provision.\\n\\nThe court below, for the reasons stated in its opinion, held that “evidence concerning a criminal case or disciplinary case” under Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act includes sentencing materials; this is proper, and there is no error, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, in misunderstanding the law concerning the scope of “evidence,” the object of forgery in the offense of forgery of evidence.\\n\\nB. However, the court below’s determination that the Defendant’s act in this case constitutes “forgery” under the offense of forgery of evidence is difficult to accept.\\n\\n(1) Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act punishes a person who destroys, conceals, forges, or alters evidence concerning another person’s criminal case or disciplinary case, or uses forged or altered evidence, and “forgery” here means, unlike the concept of forgery in offenses relating to documents, the creation of new evidence (see Supreme Court Judgment dated June 28, 2007, 2002DO3600). However, if a document prepared for the purpose of proving facts contains no falsity whatsoever in its content concerning those facts or in the name of its maker, it cannot be deemed to constitute “forgery of evidence.” The same applies even if a document concerning factual proof is submitted as evidence of a false claim in a criminal case or disciplinary case and thereby supports that claim. The reasons are as follows.\\n\\n(a) The Constitution prescribes crimes and punishments by law in order to protect individuals’ freedom and rights from the arbitrary exercise of the State’s power to punish (Article 13(1) of the Constitution). Laws restricting fundamental rights of the people or imposing duties must be clear, and in particular laws concerning punishment must be, above all else, clear so that state organs do not exercise their authority arbitrarily. In other words, penal statutes require that the elements of an offense be clearly defined so that an ordinary person can foresee what conduct will be punished and determine his or her own conduct accordingly.\\n\\nA penal provision that cannot be regarded as having a meaning and content sufficient to serve as a standard by which a person of sound common sense and ordinary legal sentiment may determine his or her conduct may violate the principle of clarity under the nulla poena sine lege principle and thus be unconstitutional (see, e.g., Constitutional Court en banc decision dated November 24, 2016, 2015HEONGA23). Therefore, this point must be kept in mind when interpreting unclear provisions in conformity with the Constitution. In addition, the interpretation of penal statutes must be strict, and interpretation beyond the possible meaning of the wording, in a manner unfavorable to the defendant, is not permitted under the prohibition against expansive interpretation, which is part of the nulla poena sine lege principle (see Supreme Court Judgment dated March 10, 2016, 2015DO17847).\\n\\n(b) The offense of forgery of evidence under the Criminal Act protects the State’s judicial function, in particular the functions of criminal adjudication and disciplinary adjudication. However, unlike the offense of obstruction of justice in the United States, which punishes all acts obstructing the performance of duties by persons in charge of judicial procedures or lawful law enforcement, Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act punishes only acts of destroying, concealing, forging, or altering evidence, or using forged or altered evidence. Even if the concept of “forgery” in the offense of forgery of evidence can be construed differently from that in the offense of document forgery, evidence containing no falsity whatsoever in its content, name of maker, or date of preparation cannot be said to have been forged.\\n\\nMeanwhile, even evidence that contains no falsity in itself may in some cases be combined with a false claim and thereby partially support a false fact. And there are cases in which evidence is prepared to prove, originally, another fact for such a purpose. However, deeming evidence that contains no falsity in its content and name of maker to constitute forgery of evidence merely because it was used to support a false fact would exceed the ordinary meaning of the statutory language and improperly expand the scope of punishment, and is therefore impermissible.\\n\\n(c) Since “forgery of evidence” as prescribed by this provision means “forgery of the means of evidence,” whether an act constitutes forgery must be determined based on the means of evidence itself, and whether it is forged should not be decided according to whether the fact sought to be proved thereby is false or true. This is because the authority and duty to evaluate the probative value of the submitted means of evidence and to determine the factual relationship on that basis lie with the court.\\n\\nAccordingly, even if the deposit confirmation certificates submitted by the Defendant were made to prove the false assertion that the relevant funds had all been returned to the Non-party 2 Company side, so long as there is no falsity in the certificates themselves, they cannot be deemed to constitute “false evidence” in relation to the false assertion.\\n\\n(d) As noted above, the “evidence” subject to the offense of forgery of evidence includes, in addition to evidence concerning the establishment of a crime, evidence concerning factual circumstances forming the basis for sentencing. However, the factual circumstances forming the basis for sentencing are not only highly complex and atypical, but also do not constitute the subject of strict proof prescribed by Article 307 of the Criminal Procedure Act. Accordingly, in actual trials, various sentencing materials concerning the defendant’s personal tendencies or the environment in which he or she was raised, in addition to sentencing materials directly related to the facts of the crime such as the motive for the offense or post-offense circumstances, are frequently submitted not only during the trial proceedings but also even after the close of argument.\\n\\nConsidering comprehensively such diversity of evidence, the judicial practice regarding sentencing proceedings, and the principle against expansive interpretation noted above, unless the concept of “forgery” prescribed in Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act is interpreted strictly, there is a risk that uncertainty and lack of clarity in the scope of punishment will chill the exercise of the defense rights of defendants, etc.\\n\\n(e) Of course, there is no denying that even though evidence itself contains no falsity, there are cases in which it is combined with a false claim and thereby proves a false fact, and such conduct is deserving of criticism as an act that may cause serious hindrance to the exercise of the State’s power to punish. However, apart from the question of creating a new statutory element criminalizing such conduct, achieving that purpose by expansively interpreting the meaning of “forgery of evidence” prescribed in Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act is not permitted under the principle of nulla poena sine lege.\\n\\n(2) Examining the facts found by the court below in light of the above legal principles, although the Defendant repeatedly remitted funds from a □□ Bank account in Non-party 4’s name to a △△ Bank account in the name of Non-party 2 Company and received them back again, then obtained only the remittance materials among them and submitted them to the court together with the false assertion that 350,000,000 won had been repaid, such conduct carries the risk of undermining the judicial function, which is the protected legal interest of the offense of forgery of evidence under the Criminal Act. However, in light of the above legal principles, the deposit confirmation certificates, etc. submitted by the Defendant are documents prepared by a financial institution to prove facts concerning financial transactions, and so long as there is no falsity whatsoever in their content or the name of their maker, they cannot be deemed to constitute “forgery” of evidence, and furthermore cannot be deemed to constitute the act of “using forged evidence.”\\n\\n(3) The court below’s judgment affirming the first-instance judgment, which found the facts charged in this case guilty on a different premise, contains an error affecting the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles concerning “forgery” of evidence prescribed in Article 155(1) of the Criminal Act.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the lower-court judgment is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower court for further proceedings and determination. It is so adjudged, in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices, as stated in the order."}

{"[85DO220]": "We judge the Defendant’s grounds of appeal.\\n\\nAs for the offense of false accusation, it suffices to report facts without being certain of their truth for the purpose of causing another person to receive criminal or disciplinary punishment, and it is not necessary to be certain that the reported facts are false; according to the evidence relied upon in the first-instance judgment upheld by the court below, the fact may be recognized that the Defendant, without being certain that the facts were true, submitted to the Chuncheon District Prosecutors’ Office a complaint stating the false fact that the persons complained against 1 and 2 had forged and used the Defendant’s guaranty portion of the loan certificate in this case; therefore, the court below’s disposition recognizing the establishment of the offense of false accusation with respect to the act as stated in the judgment is proper, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality such as a factual error due to violation of the rules of evidence or any misapprehension of legal principles concerning the offense of false accusation as alleged. The argument is without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition, by unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning the territorial scope of application of the Criminal Act are correct? (In case of dispute, according to precedents) (a) In the case where a British national murdered an American on a vessel of the Republic of Korea operating in the territorial waters of the United States, the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea applies. (b) In the case where a Japanese national forged a U.S. $100 banknote in China for the purpose of uttering it, the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea applies. (c) Under the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea, the offense of kidnapping, enticement, and trafficking in persons also applies to a foreigner who committed the offense outside the territory of the Republic of Korea, except for its preparation and conspiracy. (d) In the case where a Chinese national, in order to enter the Republic of Korea, forged a passport application form kept at the Consulate of the Republic of Korea located in China, the Criminal Act of the Republic of Korea applies under the protective principle. (e) With respect to a person who has had all or part of a sentence executed abroad by reason of an offense, the sentence may be mitigated or remitted.
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2006DO5010]": "We examine the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n1. Judgment on the Prosecutor’s Grounds for Final Appeal\\n\\nWith respect to the application of the Criminal Act, Article 2 of the same Act provides that it applies to nationals and foreigners who commit crimes within the territory of the Republic of Korea, and the main clause of Article 6 of the same Act provides that it applies to foreigners who commit, outside the territory of the Republic of Korea, crimes other than those listed in Article 5 of the same Act against the Republic of Korea or a national of the Republic of Korea. The interior of the Consulate of the Republic of Korea located in Beijing, China, still belongs to Chinese territory and cannot be regarded as falling within the territory of the Republic of Korea, nor is it obvious that the crime of forging private documents constitutes a crime committed against the Republic of Korea or a national of the Republic of Korea under Article 6 of the Criminal Act.\\n\\nTherefore, the court below’s determination that it had no jurisdiction over the Defendant on the indictment alleging that a Defendant who was not a national of the Republic of Korea forged, within that Consulate, one passport application form in the name of a person other than the accused, on the ground that this constituted an extraterritorial offense by a foreigner, is correct, and there is no error, such as misapprehension of the legal principles concerning jurisdiction, as argued in the grounds for final appeal. The grounds for final appeal cannot be accepted.\\n\\n2. Judgment on the Defendant’s Grounds for Final Appeal\\n\\nIn this case, in which a sentence lighter than 10 years’ imprisonment was imposed, the argument that the sentencing is improper does not constitute a lawful ground for final appeal. The argument in the final appeal on this point is also without merit.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nTherefore, all final appeals are dismissed, and the judgment is rendered in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court who participated, as stated in the order."}

question: Which of the following statements regarding the offense of interference with business is incorrect? (Where there is a dispute, according to precedents)
A: If it is not the performance of the business itself but only the propriety or fairness of the business that has been obstructed, the offense of interference with business is not established.
B: If brokerage business operated by a person who is not a licensed real estate agent is obstructed by force, the offense of interference with business is not established.
C: In order for the offense of interference with business by disruption of computer, etc. under Article 314(2) of the Criminal Act to be established, an actual disturbance to information processing is required; however, so long as a risk has arisen that the result of interference with business will occur by causing a disturbance to information processing, the offense is established even if the result of interference with business did not actually occur.
D: With respect to the act of, in the civil complaint office of the National Police Agency, complainants demanding an interview with the Commissioner General of the National Police Agency in connection with the handling of a petition case, and shouting abuse at and causing a disturbance toward police officers who were restraining them, the offense of interference with business is not established.
E: The offense of interference with business by force may be established even where the victim's free will was not actually suppressed by the force.
label: A
supporting_precedents: {"[2006DO6599]": "The grounds for appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. The judgment of the court below  \\nBased on the evidence it admitted, the court below found that the Defendant, without obtaining the consent of the Victim, filed a report of closure concerning the licensed real estate brokerage office at issue in this case, which was registered under the Defendant’s name but was in fact being principally operated by the Victim, who was the Defendant’s business partner; then, on the grounds that the Victim’s operation of the licensed real estate brokerage office could not be regarded as unlawful, and that even if, as the Defendant alleged, the Victim intended to operate the licensed real estate brokerage office unilaterally, such circumstance alone did not suffice to find that the illegality was so grave that it had an antisocial nature reaching the level of being utterly intolerable in social life, the court below determined that the Defendant, by abusing the status of having the licensed real estate brokerage office registered in his name and arbitrarily filing a report of closure, obstructed the Victim’s business by force.\\n\\n2. The judgment of this Court  \\nHowever, the foregoing determination of the court below is difficult to endorse for the following reasons.\\n\\nA. The “business” protected under the offense of interference with business under the Criminal Act means an occupation, or work or business engaged in continuously, and must be something worthy of protection under criminal law from another person’s unlawful infringement; therefore, where a certain work or activity itself bears an antisocial nature to such an extent that its illegality is grave and it is utterly intolerable in social life, it cannot be regarded as “business” protected under the offense of interference with business (see Supreme Court Decision 2001DO2015, rendered on November 30, 2001).\\n\\nB. Under the former Real Estate Brokerage Act (before its full amendment by Act No. 7638 of July 29, 2005; hereinafter referred to only as the “Act”), Article 4 and Article 5 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act, only a licensed real estate agent or a juristic person whose officers are licensed real estate agents or brokers may obtain registration for the establishment of a brokerage office, and Article 38(1)1 of the Act provides that a person who engages in brokerage business without obtaining registration for the establishment of a brokerage office shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 3 years or by a fine not exceeding 20,000,000 won, while Article 38(2)3 of the Act provides that a person who transfers or lends to another person, or acquires or borrows from another person, a brokerage business registration certificate or a licensed real estate agent certificate shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 10,000,000 won; accordingly, the act of engaging in brokerage business by a person who is not a licensed real estate agent, etc. is an act prohibited by the Act and constitutes a criminal act subject to criminal punishment.\\n\\nC. According to the record, the Victim, being a person who was not a licensed real estate agent, requested the Defendant, who was a licensed real estate agent, to lend his licensed real estate agent certificate, but the Defendant refused; thereafter, the Victim invested capital and the Defendant provided his certificate, while they agreed to operate as business partners by having the Defendant commute directly to the brokerage office at issue in this case and review the final documents concerning real estate contracts, and then completed registration for the establishment of the brokerage office under the Defendant’s name; after that, the Victim, contrary to the foregoing agreement, requested the Defendant not to make final confirmation of the real estate documents and to entrust his seal stamp to the Victim, which led to a dispute, and the Defendant came to file a report of closure concerning the brokerage office at issue in this case. From this, it can be seen that the business partnership relationship between the Defendant and the Victim concerning the operation of the brokerage office at issue in this case was terminated due to the Victim’s own fault, and since the Defendant, who was a licensed real estate agent, had decided to discontinue the real estate brokerage business at issue in this case upon termination of the partnership relationship, the Victim’s brokerage business, being that of a person who was not a licensed real estate agent, is an act prohibited by the Act and constitutes a criminal act subject to criminal punishment, and, as such, falls within a case bearing an antisocial nature to such an extent that it is utterly intolerable in social norms, and therefore cannot be regarded as “business” protected under the offense of interference with business.\\n\\nD. Nevertheless, the judgment of the court below, on the ground that even if the Victim had intended to operate the licensed real estate brokerage office unilaterally, such circumstance alone did not suffice to find that the illegality was so grave that it had an antisocial nature reaching the level of being utterly intolerable in social life, held that the Defendant, by abusing the status of having his name registered and arbitrarily filing a report of closure, obstructed the Victim’s business by force. In so doing, the judgment of the court below contains an error of law by misapprehending the legal principles regarding the business that is protected under the offense of interference with business, and such error affected the outcome of the judgment; therefore, the appellant’s argument pointing out this issue is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Therefore, without needing to examine the remaining grounds for appeal, the judgment of the court below shall be reversed and the case remanded to the court below, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices who participated."}

{"[2008DO11978]": "We decide the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. With respect to Ground 1 of the grounds for appeal\\nThe court of original instance, based on the statements of the witness, the non-indicted person, as recorded in the transcript of the fifth trial session in the court of original instance, etc., found the Defendant guilty of the charged facts that, as stated in the judgment, the Defendant interfered with the search service operations of NHN Co., Ltd. and Daum Communications Co., Ltd.\\n\\nHowever, among the statements of the witness, the non-indicted person, as recorded in the transcript of the fifth trial session in the court of original instance, the part stating that “the witness confirmed that ranking manipulation was being carried out in the same manner through IP address 211.43.217.55” is a statement concerning facts experienced by that witness and thus cannot be said to be hearsay evidence, whereas the part stating that “the Defendant was confirmed to be using the above IP address” is content heard from the prosecutor and therefore constitutes hearsay evidence; accordingly, unless the Defendant agrees to its use as evidence, it is in principle inadmissible as evidence pursuant to Article 310-2 of the Criminal Procedure Act.\\n\\nTherefore, the court of original instance’s adoption as evidence of the entire statement of the witness, the non-indicted person, as recorded in the transcript of the fifth trial session in the court of original instance, including the part constituting hearsay evidence, was erroneous; however, even according to the remaining evidence adopted by the court of original instance, the admissibility of which is recognized (including the written reply to the fact inquiry prepared by the Head of the Korea Internet Data Center), there is sufficient basis to find that the Defendant used IP address 211.43.217.55, and thus the court of original instance’s finding the charged facts of the offense of interference with business by hindering computers, etc. guilty is ultimately justifiable, so the above error by the court of original instance does not affect the conclusion of the judgment.\\n\\n2. With respect to Ground 2 of the grounds for appeal\\nArticle 314(2) of the Criminal Act provides for punishment of “a person who, by damaging a computer or other information-processing device, or special media records such as electronic records, or by inputting false information or an unlawful command into an information-processing device, or by any other means, causes an obstacle to information processing and thereby interferes with another’s business”; to constitute the above offense, it is required that, as a result of such act of infringement, the information-processing device fails to perform its function in accordance with its intended purpose or performs a function different from its intended purpose, thereby actually causing an obstacle to information processing (see Supreme Court Decision 2002DO631, rendered on July 9, 2004), but once a risk arises of causing an obstacle to information processing and thereby resulting in interference with business, the above offense is established even if the result of interference with business does not in fact occur.\\n\\nAccordingly, if false click information is transmitted to the statistics aggregation system server of a portal site operator and, in the process of determining search rankings, the false click information so transmitted is actually reflected in the statistics, thereby actually causing an obstacle to information processing, then the offense of interference with business by hindering computers, etc. is established even if this does not in fact cause any change in the search rankings.\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the judgment of the court below, the court below, after comprehensively considering the evidence admitted by it and finding the facts stated in the judgment, held that the Defendant’s act of transmitting false click information to the statistics aggregation system server of the portal site operator constitutes inputting false information or an unlawful command, and that since the false click information transmitted by the Defendant was reflected in the statistics, an obstacle to information processing actually occurred, and the victims’ search service provision operations should be deemed to have been interfered with; on that basis, the court below found all of the charged facts of interference with business by hindering computers, etc. against the Defendant guilty.\\n\\nUpon examination in light of the above legal principle and the record, the above factual finding and determination by the court below are proper, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality of factual error, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, or any misapprehension of the legal principle concerning the causal relationship for the occurrence of an obstacle to information processing.\\n\\n3. With respect to Ground 3 of the grounds for appeal\\nUpon examining the evidence lawfully admitted by the court below in light of the record, the court below’s finding the Defendant guilty of the offense against Daum Communications Co., Ltd. is proper. Since there is no illegality in the judgment of the court below in violation of the rules governing the weighing of evidence, the argument in the grounds for appeal, which merely criticizes the selection of evidence or the finding of facts, matters within the exclusive authority of the court below as the trier of fact, cannot constitute a lawful ground for appeal or is otherwise unacceptable.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2008DO9049]": "We consider together the grounds for appeal filed by the Defendant and the court-appointed defense counsel.\\n\\n1. As to the point of violation of the Act on Assemblies and Demonstrations\\nThe Act on Assemblies and Demonstrations provides that a person who intends to organize an outdoor assembly or demonstration must notify the chief of the competent police station in advance of certain matters, thereby enabling the chief of the competent police station, based on such notification, to ascertain in advance the nature and scale of the outdoor assembly or demonstration and to make advance measures for maintaining public peace and order by protecting lawful outdoor assemblies or demonstrations while preventing infringement upon the interests of others or the community through outdoor assemblies or demonstrations (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DO315, decided April 27, 2004, etc.), and it cannot be said that the above notification duty is waived merely because the opinion sought to be expressed through an outdoor assembly or demonstration is legitimate (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 90DO870, decided August 14, 1990, etc.).\\nIn light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, the court below's determination, for the reasons stated in its opinion, to find the Defendant guilty of this part of the facts charged is proper, and there is no illegality such as a violation of the rules of evidence, incomplete examination, or misapprehension of legal principles, as asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n2. As to the point of obstruction of business\\nThe crime of obstruction of business under Article 314(1) of the Criminal Act is an offense established when a person obstructs another's business by disseminating false facts or by other deceit or force, and its protected legal interest lies in protecting a person's social and economic activities through business. However, the Criminal Act separately provides, as one of the \"Crimes Concerning Obstruction of Public Duties,\" the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties for acts that obstruct a public official's performance of duties by force, intimidation, or deceit (Article 136(1), Article 137), and its protected legal interest lies in protecting the functions of the State or public institutions concretely carried out by public officials.\\nIn this way, the crime of obstruction of business and the crime of obstruction of performance of official duties differ not only in their protected legal interests and protected objects, but also in that the types of conduct constituting obstruction of performance of official duties are more limited than those constituting obstruction of business. In light of these points, the fact that the Criminal Act separately provides for the offense of obstruction of performance of official duties apart from the offense of obstruction of business should be understood as meaning that, by distinguishing private business from public duties, only in cases where, with respect to public duties, execution is obstructed by force, intimidation, or deceit against a public official will punishment be imposed; accordingly, it is proper to construe that acts obstructing public duties performed by a public official in the course of duty cannot be charged as obstruction of business (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2009DO4166, decided November 19, 2009).\\nThe court below, by comprehensively considering the evidence stated in its opinion, affirmed the first-instance judgment that found the facts charged of obstruction of business guilty on the ground that the Defendant, together with First-instance Co-defendant 2, caused a disturbance by scattering horse manure on the desk and floor of the Civil Complaints Office of the National Police Agency and shouting, thereby obstructing police officers' duties of receiving civil petitions by force; however, in light of the legal principles discussed above, the court below's determination misapprehended the law concerning the scope within which the crime of obstruction of business is established, and it is clear that this affected the outcome of the judgment. The assertion in the grounds for appeal including this point is well-founded.\\n3. Conclusion\\nTherefore, the portion of the court below's judgment concerning obstruction of business must be reversed; since the court below treated this offense as a concurrent offense under the first sentence of Article 37 of the Criminal Act together with the remaining offenses and imposed a single sentence, the entire judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination, and it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in the case, as stated in the order."}

{"[2009DO8506]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. The lower appellate court, in this case where it was recognized that, in connection with the hiring work for new employees in 2008 by ○○ City Fisheries Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as “the Cooperative at issue”), the employees described in the judgment who were involved in grading the written examination pursuant to the instructions of the Defendant, the president of the Cooperative (hereinafter referred to as “the persons in charge of the scoring work at issue”), manipulated the scores by newly preparing the written-examination answer sheets of Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2, who had applied for the restricted competitive recruitment portion, and thereby caused Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2 to pass the recruitment examination, held, in view of the various circumstances as stated in the judgment, that since both the Defendant and the persons in charge of the scoring work at issue had all conspired in or acquiesced to the above score manipulation act (hereinafter referred to as “the score manipulation at issue”), it could not be deemed that the persons in charge of the scoring work at issue or the Cooperative at issue had been deceived, and therefore the score manipulation at issue did not constitute “deception” in the offense of obstruction of business by deceptive means; and, on the other hand, on the grounds that, in the interview examination conducted for those who passed the written examination, there was no procedure to verify the written-examination scores or reconfirm the evaluation contents of the written examination, and that, in the case of restricted competitive recruitment limited to the children of members, the interview examination was conducted merely as a formality by hiring all interview candidates unless special circumstances existed, it also could not be deemed that the interview duties of some interview panel members who did not know of the score manipulation at issue were obstructed, the lower appellate court rejected all of the prosecutor’s grounds of appeal and affirmed the first-instance judgment that had acquitted the Defendant of the facts charged in this case.\\n\\n2. However, the lower appellate court’s determination is difficult to accept for the following reasons.\\n\\nIn the offense of Obstruction of Business by deceptive means, deception means that a person employs and takes advantage of inducing the other party to make a mistake, be confused, or be unaware, in order to achieve the purpose of the act, and the establishment of the offense of obstruction of business does not require that the result of obstruction of business actually occur; it is sufficient if a risk of causing such a result arises, and the offense of obstruction of business is established even where not the performance of the business itself but the propriety or fairness of the business is obstructed (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2006DO1721 rendered on January 17, 2008).\\n\\nAccording to the reasons stated in the lower court judgment, when Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2, who applied for new employee recruitment at the Cooperative at issue, received scores below the passing line in the written examination, the persons in charge of the scoring work at issue, pursuant to the Defendant’s instructions, caused Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2 to pass the written examination through the score manipulation at issue, thereby enabling them to take the interview examination conducted for those who passed the written examination. In such a case, if the score manipulation at issue enabled Nonindicted 1 and Nonindicted 2, who would not have been qualified to take the interview examination based on the unmanipulated written-examination scores, to take the interview examination, then the score manipulation at issue constitutes deception that causes the interview panel members to make a mistake, be confused, or be unaware as to whether the examinees are lawfully qualified, and, unless there are special circumstances such as the interview panel members having conspired in or acquiesced to the score manipulation at issue, it must be deemed that the propriety or fairness of the interview duties performed by the interview panel members was impaired by such deception.\\n\\nEven if the interview duties are of a passive nature, serving only to determine whether a person will ultimately pass or fail, and even if they were performed in a merely formal manner, they cannot be said to be business that lacks protectable value in relation to the Cooperative at issue. Moreover, by the score manipulation at issue, the interview panel members were made to conduct interviews with persons lacking qualification to take the examination, while persons who did possess the corresponding qualification to take the examination were unable to be interviewed; the very fact itself impairs the propriety or fairness of the interview duties, and because such a result occurs regardless of whether the performance of the interview duties was passive or formal, it cannot be said that there was no obstruction of the interview duties.\\n\\nIf that is so, in this case where there is no material in the record from which it can be deemed that some of the interview panel members conspired in or acquiesced to the score manipulation at issue, the interview duties performed by them as part of the new employee recruitment work of the Cooperative at issue must be deemed to have been obstructed by the score manipulation at issue.\\n\\nNevertheless, the lower appellate court, finding otherwise and holding that there was no such obstruction of business, merely affirmed the first-instance judgment that had acquitted the Defendant of the facts charged in this case. Thus, there is an illegality that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal principles on obstruction of business by deceptive means. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing this out is well-founded.\\n\\n3. Therefore, without examining the remaining grounds of appeal, the judgment of the lower appellate court is reversed, and the case is remanded to the lower appellate court for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, as stated in the disposition."}

{"[2021DO9055]": "The grounds of appeal are examined.\\n\\n1. Part concerning violation of the Act on Punishment of Violences, etc. (joint trespass to a residence)\\n\\na. The crime of trespass to a residence protects the peace and tranquility of a de facto residence as its protected legal interest. Since the act element of trespass in the crime of trespass to a residence must be interpreted in relation to the protected legal interest of the crime of trespass to a residence, trespass means entering a residence in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace of the residence, and, as a general rule, whether it constitutes trespass is to be determined based on the objectively and externally manifested manner of the act at the time of entry. If a person enters a residence in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace, this will generally be contrary to the resident’s intent, but it cannot be said to constitute trespass merely on the basis of the subjective circumstance that the act of simply entering the residence itself is contrary to the resident’s intent (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2020DO12630, rendered on September 9, 2021). Accordingly, whether the act constitutes trespass must be determined not by whether it is contrary to the resident’s intent, but by whether it is a manner of act that disturbs the actual state of peace.\\n\\nWhere an actor enters a residence with the resident’s consent, but the entry is for the purpose of committing a crime, etc., or where it is recognized that the resident would not have consented to the entry had the resident known the actor’s actual purpose of entry, in order for the actor’s entry to constitute the trespass prescribed in the crime of trespass to a residence, it must be evaluated, in light of the objectively and externally manifested manner of the act at the time of the actor’s entry, by comprehensively considering such circumstances as the form, use, and nature of the residence to be entered, the mode and status of control and management of entry by outsiders, and the circumstances and method of the actor’s entry, that the actual state of peace of the residence was infringed (see Supreme Court en banc Decision 2017DO18272, rendered on March 24, 2022; Supreme Court Decision 2021DO7087, rendered on June 16, 2022, etc.).\\n\\nAccordingly, if a person enters, by an ordinary method, a building that is generally open and freely accessible, in a state where there is no restriction or interference by the manager as to entry, it cannot be deemed that the person entered the building in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace, and therefore such conduct does not constitute the act of trespass prescribed in the crime of trespass to a building (see Supreme Court Decision 2022DO2907, rendered on May 12, 2022; Supreme Court Decision 2021DO7087, rendered on June 16, 2022, etc.).\\n\\nb. The facts charged in this part are that the Defendants, jointly, on May 28, 2020, at around 11:00 a.m., entered the second floor of the △△△△ ○○ branch through the main gate, against the victim’s intent, the victim being the branch manager of the △△△△ ○○ branch, in order to protest against the dismissals and transfer personnel orders to the representatives, etc. of △△△△ who visited the △△△△ ○○ branch in Seoul ○○ District, and thereby trespassed into a building.\\n\\nc. The court below, on the ground that the Defendants entered the △△△△ ○○ branch against the presumed intent of the manager and thereby disturbed the actual peace of the building, affirmed as it stood the first-instance court’s determination that found this part of the facts charged guilty.\\n\\nd. However, according to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts are established.\\n\\n1) The second-floor store of the △△△△ ○○ branch into which the Defendants, who were executives and union members of the Mart Industry Workers’ Union, entered is a place that is generally open without restrictions such as entry qualifications during business hours.\\n\\n2) The Defendants, as stated in the facts charged, entered the second-floor store by sequentially passing through the main gate and store entrance used by customers during business hours, but they did not take any special measures such as being restrained by security personnel or sneaking in when the security personnel were away.\\n\\ne. In light of the foregoing facts in conjunction with the legal principles discussed above, once it is seen that the Defendants entered, by an ordinary method, the store of the △△△△ ○○ branch, which is generally open and freely accessible, in a state where there was no restriction or interference by the manager as to entry, it cannot be deemed that they entered in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace, and therefore this does not constitute the act of trespass prescribed in the crime of trespass to a building. The explicit intent of the manager of the △△△△ ○○ branch to prohibit entry has not been confirmed, and even if the Defendants’ act of entering the store of the △△△△ ○○ branch, as charged in this part, was contrary to the manager’s presumed intent, such circumstance alone cannot be assessed as an entry made in a manner that disturbs the actual state of peace. Therefore, the crime of trespass to a building is not established against the Defendants.\\n\\nf. Nevertheless, the court below’s determination, which recognized the establishment of the crime of trespass to a building on the main ground that the manager’s presumed intent existed, contains an error that misapprehended the legal principles regarding the establishment of the offense and affected the judgment. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing this out is well taken.\\n\\n2. Part concerning obstruction of business\\n\\na. The “force” in the crime of obstruction of business means any power sufficient to suppress or confuse a person’s free will, regardless of whether it is tangible or intangible; it is not necessary that the victim’s free will be actually suppressed, but it must be of such degree that, in light of the offender’s arrogance, number of persons, surrounding circumstances, etc., it is sufficient to suppress the victim’s free will. Whether it constitutes such force must be determined objectively by considering all circumstances, including the time and place of the offense, the motive and purpose of the offense, the number of persons, the manner of the force, the type of business, and the status of the victim, etc. (see Supreme Court Decision 2016DO10956, rendered on October 27, 2016, etc.), and it is not determined by the will of the victim, etc.\\n\\nb. The facts charged in this part are that the Defendants, who entered the second-floor store of the △△△△ ○○ branch as above, jointly, by holding placards bearing the words “unfair dismissal,” and by following the victim (the branch manager of the ○○ branch) and the officers and employees of △△△△, including the representative director (hereinafter collectively referred to as the “victim, etc.”), and shouting loudly, “Stop forced transfers, stop integrated operation, employees are suffering, stop unfair dismissal,” obstructed the victim’s on-site inspection duties for about 30 minutes by force.\\n\\nc. The court below, on the ground that the first-instance court’s determination that a number of Defendants, while holding placards in the store, continuously followed the victim, etc., shouted loudly, and recorded this by camera, constituted the exercise of force sufficient to suppress the victim’s free will, affirmed as it stood the first-instance court’s determination that found this part of the facts charged guilty.\\n\\nd.
