However, according to the reasons of the judgment below and the record, the following facts are established.\\n\\n1) The acts as charged occurred at around 11:00 a.m. on a weekday in the food sales area of a large mart, and the Defendants, who were union executives and union members who had heard that the officers and employees, including the representative director of △△△△, were coming to conduct an on-site inspection of the △△△△ ○○ branch (some of them had been discharged several months earlier for failing to comply with transfer personnel orders), sought to directly request the representative director to reinstate them and to withdraw the transfer personnel orders in relation to the dismissals and transfer personnel orders, etc.\\n\\n2) The persons who carried out the acts as charged were all seven of the Defendants, of whom four were women, and among the three men, one was in his 50s. On the other hand, the number of persons who participated in the on-site inspection of the store at that time was more than about 20, including the victim, etc., and most of them, including the representative director, were senior-level management.\\n\\n3) While the Defendants followed the victim, etc., who were performing inspection work in the food sales area, they stood in the surrounding area holding placards at a distance of about 1 to 2 meters or more, or shouted, “Please stop forced transfers,” “I want to work,” and the like, but the victim, etc. continued the on-site inspection work for about 30 minutes.\\n\\n4) Defendant 2 filmed the activities of the other Defendants in order to inform the union members, and did not intend to film the appearance of the victim, etc.\\n\\ne. In light of the foregoing facts in conjunction with the legal principles discussed above, it is difficult to conclude that the Defendants, jointly, exercised force sufficient to suppress the free will of the victim, etc. The reasons are as follows.\\n\\n1) Whether the Defendants’ acts were sufficient to suppress the victim’s free will must be determined objectively by considering not only the victim’s will or statements, but also the manner of the Defendants’ acts, the number of Defendants, their sex and age, and the number and status of the victim’s side, etc.\\n\\n2) While carrying out the acts as charged, the Defendants stood holding placards at a distance of about 1 to 2 meters or more from the victim, etc., and followed them according to the victim’s, etc. progress, but they did not approach the victim, etc. any closer, nor did they physically block the victim’s, etc. progress or work.\\n\\n3) The Defendants did not use abusive language or threats toward the victim, etc., and contrary to the facts charged, they even used honorific speech while shouting their demands. There is also no objective evidence to the effect that the voices of the Defendants were noise sufficient to make it difficult for the victim’s on-site inspection work in the food sales area of a large mart where many customers visit and sales promotion events are also held.\\n\\n4) The Defendants were seeking, on the occasion of being able to meet directly the representative director who possessed decision-making authority over personnel policy and discretionary authority over personnel matters, to protest the dismissals and transfer personnel orders, etc., or to request reinstatement and withdrawal of the transfer personnel orders, and it cannot be said that they carried out the acts as charged with the intent to obstruct or suspend the management work of the ○○ branch of the victim, who is the branch manager of the △△△△ ○○ branch.\\n\\n5) Notwithstanding the Defendants’ acts as charged, the representative director’s on-site inspection work proceeded for about 30 minutes.\\n\\n6) In the court below, counsel for the Defendants also argued that, at other branches of △△△△, union members carried out similar activities in line with the representative director’s on-site inspection schedule, but no separate measures such as criminal complaints were taken there.\\n\\nf. Nevertheless, the court below’s determination, which recognized the establishment of the crime of obstruction of business on the view that the Defendants exercised “force,” contains an error that misapprehended the legal principles concerning “force” in the crime of obstruction of business and affected the judgment. The argument in the grounds of appeal pointing this out is well taken.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n\\nThe judgment below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged, with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning crimes of omission are incorrect? (Where there is a dispute, according to precedents) (a) Since the duty to act must be a legal duty, a legal duty to act is recognized where it arises from statutes, legal acts, or prior conduct, but where only a duty to act is expected under the principle of good faith and fair dealing, social norms, or the principles of reason, a legal duty to act cannot be recognized. (b) The intent for an improper omission offense must necessarily include a purpose or planned intent to commit the offense with respect to the occurrence of the constituent result. (c) The crime of breach of trust in the course of business can also be established by omission, and in order for such omission to be regarded as commencement of execution, the omission must occur in a situation in which, if the duty to act is not fulfilled, it is objectively foreseeable that the person who conferred the duty of handling affairs would be unable to exercise property rights, and the risk of the occurrence of the constituent result has become concrete. (d) In the sale of a used automobile, since the seller's installment debt to the installment finance company or guarantee insurer is automatically succeeded to by the buyer, failing to notify the buyer of the existence of that installment debt constitutes deception by omission. (e) Co-principal liability among crimes of omission is established only when a common duty is imposed on multiple offenders by omission and when that duty can be performed jointly.
label: B
supporting_precedents: {"[2008DO89]": "Article 3(1), first sentence, of the Public Health Control Act provides that “a person who intends to engage in a public health business shall equip the facilities and equipment prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Health and Welfare for each type of public health business and shall report to the Mayor, County Governor, or District Head,” and Article 20(1) item 1 provides that it punishes “a person who has not made the report pursuant to the provisions of the first sentence of Article 3(1)”; in light of the form and purport of those provisions, a violation of the Public Health Control Act resulting from a breach of the duty to report should be regarded as a true omission offense, the constituent elements of which can be realized only by omission, and, meanwhile, co-perpetration among omission offenses should be regarded as established only when a common duty is imposed upon multiple omission offenders and that duty can be performed in common. And the duty to report for a public health business is imposed upon “a person who intends to engage in a public health business,” and here, the phrase “a person who engages in business” means a person who is the subject to whom rights and obligations arising from the business accrue; therefore, it is reasonable to interpret that, in the case of an employee or assistant of the business operator, such person is not included within “a person who engages in business.”\\n\\nThe court below, after comprehensively considering the evidence it adopted and recognizing the facts as stated in its opinion, determined that the Defendants, who held the position of manager at each branch of the company Care Korea in this case (trade name omitted), were merely wage earners of the said company and were not the subject to whom the rights and obligations arising from the business belonged, and thus did not fall within the category of persons burdened with the duty to report under the said provision; and further determined that, unless the Defendants were given a common duty to report, co-perpetration of the offense of violation of the Public Health Control Act resulting from a failure to report, which is a true omission offense, could not be established. In light of the legal principle discussed above, the court below’s determination as such is correct, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality of misapprehension of law as asserted in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the Disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices involved."}

{"[2015DO15227]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nWhere a person who bears a legal duty to act to prevent the occurrence of a result infringing a legally protected interest prohibited by the Criminal Act can easily prevent the occurrence of that result by performing that duty, yet, having tolerated and stood by the occurrence of the result, fails to perform the duty, if such failure to act is deemed to be conduct of execution of the crime, he may be punished as an omission offense. Here, the duty to act is recognized not only where it arises from statutes, legal acts, or prior conduct, but also where, under the principle of good faith and fair dealing, social norms, or as a matter of reason, a duty to act is expected (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2007DO9354 rendered on February 28, 2008).\\n\\nThe court below held that the Defendant, as an employee managing the store at the store in this case, had a duty, within the possible scope, to immediately remove any danger if it arose in the above store, and that, given the form of the Defendant's work, at a time when working hours and rest hours were not clearly distinguished, while smoking with A in the passage next to the store in this case, where the Defendant had usually been in charge of cleaning and other management, the Defendant witnessed A throw a cigarette butt whose embers had not been completely extinguished toward the side where there was plastic for packaging clothes that was easily combustible and then enter the store; accordingly, the court below determined that the Defendant had a duty to act under the employment contract or as a matter of reason to check whether embers remained in the above cigarette butt and to eliminate the danger, but, by negligence in leaving the scene without performing that duty, caused the plastic, etc. to catch fire and spread the fire to the occupied building, including the store in this case, thereby committing the offense of negligent fire setting.\\n\\nThe court below, considering the contents of the Defendant's employment contract, the time and place where the fire in this case occurred, the Defendant's usual duties, the circumstances leading to the outbreak of the fire, and the ease of the act for preventing infringement of a legally protected interest, determined that the Defendant, at the time the fire in this case occurred, had, as a duty under the principle of good faith and fair dealing pursuant to the employment contract, a duty to act to check whether embers remained in the cigarette butt and eliminate the danger, but failed to perform it and thereby committed the offense of negligent fire setting; this is in accordance with the legal principle stated above, and therefore the allegation in the grounds of appeal that the law concerning the guarantor status of an offense by improper omission was misunderstood cannot be accepted.\\n\\nAccordingly, the appeal is dismissed, and, by the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating, judgment is rendered as stated in the order."}
{"[2015DO6809]": "All appeals are dismissed."}

{"[2020DO15529]": "The grounds of appeal are determined (supplementary briefs on the grounds of appeal submitted after the filing period for the statement of grounds of appeal are considered only to the extent that they supplement it).\\n\\n1. Summary of the Charged Facts\\n\\nThe summary of the charged facts is as follows.\\n\\nThe Defendant is a person who carried out the overall work necessary for the progress of the instant project, including the formulation of the replotting plan, for the Goyang Siksa District Urban Development Project Association (hereinafter referred to as the “Victim Association”), which was promoting an urban development project by the land readjustment method (hereinafter referred to as the “instant project”) in an area of 989,377 square meters in and around (address omitted), Goyang City (hereinafter referred to as the “instant project area”).\\n\\nAround Aug. 30, 2011, the amendment to the urban development and implementation plans concerning the instant project was approved (the implementation plan as amended in this manner is hereinafter referred to as the “2011 Implementation Plan”). As a result, the development method for the public open space between part of the land scheduled for replotting within the instant project area (land referred to as “Zone C”; hereinafter referred to as the “instant land scheduled for replotting”) and the major road (daero) was changed from a “screened type,” in which access to buildings on the land scheduled for replotting was substantially blocked, to an “open type,” in which such access was easy, and accordingly the economic value of the instant land scheduled for replotting increased. Therefore, the Defendant had an occupational duty, pursuant to the relevant statutes, to take measures such as reappraisal of the instant land scheduled for replotting, amendment of the replotting plan, and redesignation of the land scheduled for replotting, so that the Victim Association could reflect the increase in value of the instant land scheduled for replotting in the settlement procedure and collect an appropriate settlement money.\\n\\nNevertheless, by failing to take measures such as reappraisal of the instant land scheduled for replotting immediately after the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, the Defendant intended to allow his relatives by blood or marriage, acquaintances, and others who were to receive replotting of the instant land scheduled for replotting to obtain the benefit of the increase in land value, and to cause the Victim Association to suffer damage in the amount of KRW 3,470,766,900, which is the aggregate amount of the aforesaid increase in land value, but this remained at the stage of an attempt because the Victim Association proceeded with the procedure for an application for approval of an amendment to the replotting plan around May 2016.\\n\\n2. The Court of Appeals’ Judgment\\n\\nFor the following reasons, the court below reversed the first-instance judgment, which had found the instant charged facts not guilty, and found them guilty.\\n\\nThe Defendant, as a person who was entrusted with and entirely handled the affairs of the Victim Association, had the duty to appropriately assess the increase in value resulting from changes in the appraisal factors for the instant land scheduled for replotting and to enable the Victim Association to collect an appropriate settlement money. With respect to the above work, the Defendant was most familiar with it through active involvement, and it was difficult for others to easily confirm it.\\n\\nHowever, by resigning from Non-party 1 Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as “Non-party 1 Company”), which had been performing work concerning the instant project on behalf of the Victim Association, on Dec. 31, 2011, without fulfilling such duty or handing over the relevant matters to his successor and while remaining silent, the Defendant caused a situation in which the Victim Association, without recognizing the necessity of such reappraisal for several years, was exposed to the risk of failing to properly undergo the settlement procedure. The Defendant’s such omission was committed while recognizing that it could confer economic benefits on himself, his relatives by blood or marriage, and acquaintances who had received replotting concentrated in the main area of the project, and cause damage to the Victim Association. Therefore, it is proper to recognize that the Defendant had commenced the execution of the crime of breach of trust in the course of duty.\\n\\n3. The Supreme Court’s Judgment\\n\\nThe judgment of the court below cannot be upheld for the following reasons.\\n\\na. The crime of breach of trust in the course of duty is established when a person who handles another’s affairs, by an act in violation of his occupational duty, acquires pecuniary benefits or causes a third party to acquire such benefits, thereby causing damage to that other person (Articles 356 and 355(2) of the Criminal Act). Article 18 of the Criminal Act provides, with respect to the requirements for the establishment of an offense by omission, that “a person who has a duty to prevent the occurrence of danger or who, by his own act, has caused the source of danger to arise, shall be punished by the resulting consequence if he fails to prevent the occurrence of such danger.”\\n\\nThe crime of breach of trust in the course of duty may also be established by omission of a person who, in a relationship of trust with another, has a legal duty to handle affairs in accordance with a certain mandate, by failing to perform an act that is legally required in the circumstances (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision of Nov. 29, 2012, 2012DO10139). In order for such omission to be regarded as the commencement of execution, the omission must occur in a situation where the risk of the occurrence of the constitutive result has been concretized, for example, where it can be objectively foreseen that, if the duty to act is not performed, the person who entrusted the handling of affairs will be unable to exercise property rights. And the actor must have recognized, at the time of omission, that he was violating the duty assigned to him and that there was a risk of damage arising from such omission.\\n\\nb. According to the reasons of the judgment of the court below and the duly admitted evidence, the following circumstances can be found.\\n\\nDuring the process of promoting the instant project, a disagreement arose between the Victim Association and Goyang City regarding the development method of the public open space in the instant case, and the development method of the public open space in the instant case emerged as one of the major issues of the instant project from the end of 2009. Therefore, the fact that the development plan for the public open space in the instant case was changed pursuant to the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan was something that the executives of the Victim Association, who bore primary responsibility for the decision-making of the Victim Association, could sufficiently recognize.\\n\\nSince the development plan for the public open space in the instant case was changed pursuant to the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, the fact that this necessitated a reappraisal of the value of the instant land scheduled for replotting is not something that only the Defendant could know. Moreover, even after the Defendant, around Dec. 31, 2011, lost his position to perform work concerning the instant project by resigning from the position of representative director of Non-party 1 Company, officers and employees including Non-party 2, a certified urban planning engineer, continued to work at Non-party 1 Company, and among them Non-party 3, who was mainly in charge of replotting work, was in a position to know, no less than the Defendant, that amendment of the replotting plan was necessary pursuant to the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan.\\n\\nAround the time of the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, the Victim Association was suffering severe financial difficulties due to delays in the sale of reserve land, and in order to overcome such problems, it continuously promoted changes to the development plan and implementation plan concerning the instant project from around 2012 to around 2015. In light of this, it cannot be seen that, at the time of the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, there was an urgent situation in which, if the amendment of the replotting plan was not expedited, the replotting disposition would soon be made and the legal relations among the association members would be fixed.\\n\\nThe former Urban Development Work Guidelines (Directive No. 680) established by the Minister of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs contain the following: “If, during project implementation, the implementer needs to amend the replotting plan due to changes in public facilities or the determination of group reserve land, the replotting plan shall be amended immediately” (see Article 4-5-1). However, since the transfer of rights to land scheduled for replotting or the determination of settlement money is effected only upon a replotting disposition, it does not necessarily follow that the failure to take measures for amending the replotting plan “immediately” after the approval of the implementation plan will directly create a risk of adverse effects on the property relations of the Victim Association.\\n\\nc. When these circumstances are examined in light of the legal principles set forth in paragraph a. above, even if, as stated in the charged facts, the Defendant is deemed to have had a duty to act to take follow-up measures pursuant to the approval of the 2011 Implementation Plan, it is difficult to view that the Defendant violated such duty to act in a situation where the risk that the Victim Association would fail to reflect the increase in value of the instant land scheduled for replotting in the settlement procedure had been concretized; accordingly, it cannot be said that the Defendant commenced the execution of the crime of breach of trust in the course of duty by omission.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below found the charged facts guilty on the ground that the Defendant had commenced the execution of the crime of breach of trust in the course of duty. The judgment of the court below contains an error that affected the judgment by misapprehending the legal doctrine concerning the requirements for recognizing the commencement of execution in the crime of breach of trust in the course of duty by omission. The Defendant’s ground of appeal pointing this out is meritorious.\\n\\n4. Conclusion\\n\\nWithout addressing the remaining grounds of appeal by the Defendant, the judgment of the court below is reversed and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court."}

{"[98DO231]": "We examine the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe gist of the fraud charge against the Defendants, whom the court below found not guilty, is that the Defendants conspired to purchase vehicles on which installment payments remained and then sell those vehicles as if they were vehicles free of installment payments, thereby appropriating the purchase price, and that, although Defendant 1 and Defendant 2 had purchased the Credos passenger car from Nonindicted Person 1 and installment payments remained thereon, on February 21, 1997, Defendant 2, while impersonating Nonindicted Person 1, falsely told Victim Nonindicted Person 2 that there were no installment payments remaining on the above passenger car, and, thereby deceiving the victim, concluded on the spot a contract to sell the above passenger car for 9,500,000 won and received 9,500,000 won thereunder under the name of the purchase price, thereby obtaining it by fraud; and that, although Defendant 1 purchased an Avante passenger car from Nonindicted Person 3 for 1,000,000 won on condition that he assume the installment payments, on the 22nd of the same month Defendant 1 and Defendant 2 falsely told Victim Nonindicted Person 4 that there were no installment payments remaining on the above vehicle, and, thereby deceiving the victim, concluded on the spot a contract to sell the above passenger car for 6,000,000 won and received 6,000,000 won thereunder under the name of the purchase price, thereby obtaining it by fraud. According to the reasons stated in the judgment below, the court below held that even according to all the evidence adduced by the Prosecutor, there was no evidence to establish that the Defendants had conspired and lied to the victims that there were no installment payments remaining on the above Credos passenger car and Avante passenger car, concluded each vehicle sale contract with the victims thereby deceived, and received the sale proceeds and thereby obtained them by fraud, and accordingly rendered a judgment of not guilty on each of the above charges. Upon examination of the record, the above determination of the court below is acceptable, and there is also no evidence that the Defendants, in selling the above Credos passenger car to Nonindicted Person 2, impersonated Nonindicted Person 1. Therefore, the above determination of the court below cannot be said to be unlawful as a violation of the rules of evidence evaluation, as argued.\\n\\nOn the other hand, in a transactional relationship concerning property rights, if one party, knowing that by failing to notify the other party of some matter related to the transaction there may arise a risk that the rights to the contractual subject matter will not be secured in the future, nevertheless does not notify the other party of such matter, enters into the transaction, and receives delivery of property or obtains property benefits from the other party, and if it is clear from common experience that the other party would not have entered into the transaction had he or she been notified of such circumstances, then the recipient of the property has, under the principle of good faith, a duty to notify the other party of such circumstances, and the recipient’s failure to do so constitutes deceit by concealing a fact that should have been disclosed, and thus constitutes fraud (see Supreme Court Decision of September 25, 1984, 84DO882; Supreme Court Decision of March 12, 1985, 84DO93; Supreme Court Decision of December 24, 1991, 91DO2698, etc.). However, upon examination of the record, Defendant 1 purchased the above Credos passenger car from Nonindicted Person 1 and the above Avante passenger car from Nonindicted Person 3, each on condition that he assume the installment-payment debt, and when the Defendants sold them to Nonindicted Person 2 and Nonindicted Person 4, respectively, they are seen not to have notified them that there was an installment-payment debt; as to whether such act constitutes a fraudulent act by deceiving the other party in breach of a duty to notify, the record shows that Nonindicted Person 1 obtained financing from Nonindicted Person 5 Co., Ltd. and purchased the above Credos passenger car, thereby owing an installment-payment debt to Nonindicted Person 5 Co., Ltd., and that Nonindicted Person 3 purchased the above Avante passenger car by installment under the surety insurance coverage of a guarantee insurance company, but there appears to have been no circumstance such as that a mortgage had been created on the above Credos passenger car and Avante passenger car themselves, or that a provisional seizure had been executed thereon (see the entries in the respective motor vehicle registration registers at pages 25 and 284 of Book 5 of the investigation record). Nor is there any basis in the record to conclude that the installment-payment debt of Nonindicted Person 1 or Nonindicted Person 3 would naturally be assumed by the purchaser under a motor vehicle sale contract. If the circumstances are as such, then even if the former owners, Nonindicted Person 1 and Nonindicted Person 3, respectively, owed installment-payment debts in relation to the motor vehicles that were the subject matter of the sales, such fact would not create a risk that the purchasers of the vehicles, Nonindicted Person 2 and Nonindicted Person 4, would fail in the future to secure ownership of the vehicles that were the subject matter of the contract; therefore, it cannot be said that, had Nonindicted Person 2 or Nonindicted Person 4 been notified of the circumstance that such installment-payment debts existed, it would have been evident from common experience that they would not have purchased the respective vehicles. Accordingly, the Defendants cannot be said to have owed a duty to notify them thereof, and the Defendants’ such omission cannot be said to constitute a deceptive act.\\n\\nHowever, as to the point that Defendant 1, while purchasing the above Credos passenger car from Nonindicted Person 1 on condition that he assume Nonindicted Person 1’s installment-payment debt, deceived Nonindicted Person 1 and received Nonindicted Person 1’s seal, and without Nonindicted Person 1’s knowledge affixed a seal thereto on the power of attorney for transfer of motor vehicle and forged it, and that the Defendants delivered and used it in selling the above Credos passenger car to Nonindicted Person 2, the court below found this guilty and that judgment was left undisturbed and became final. According to the record, the Defendants sold the above Credos passenger car to Nonindicted Person 2 while posing as agents of Nonindicted Person 1 (see the receipt on page 568 of the investigation record, case No. 1997 HYEONGJE29186 of the Seoul District Prosecutors’ Office), and if so, there may be suspicion that the Defendants, having no authority from Nonindicted Person 1 to sell the above Credos passenger car, deceived Nonindicted Person 2 by acting as if they had such authority, and that Nonindicted Person 2, deceived thereby, purchased the above Credos passenger car. However, on the other hand, Nonindicted Person 2 states that when purchasing the above Credos passenger car, he or she received, in addition to the above power of attorney for transfer of motor vehicle, the seal certificate, motor vehicle inspection certificate, resident registration extract, compulsory insurance receipt, and other documents in Nonindicted Person 1’s name necessary for transfer registration (see the statement record of Nonindicted Person 2 prepared by the judicial police officer, page 91 of the above investigation record), and the record does not show how the Defendants came into possession of those documents (in the criminal complaint filed by Nonindicted Person 1 against the Defendants, Nonindicted Person 1 states that after selling the above Credos passenger car to Defendant 1, Defendant 1 said that he urgently needed the car, so without going through the procedure for succession to the installment-payment debt, Nonindicted Person 1 first delivered the above Credos passenger car, and that at the time of delivery he kept the seal certificate, motor vehicle inspection certificate, resident registration extract, compulsory insurance receipt, and other documents necessary for transfer registration inside the above passenger car, but later, thinking that nothing special would happen, he delivered the car as it was. However, that complaint was not adopted as evidence, and the Defendants deny such facts).\\n\\nIn addition, a fraud offense based on the allegation that, despite having no power of agency, the Defendants deceived Nonindicted Person 2 by posing as though they had such power of agency is different in its factual content from the fraud offense stated in the above indictment, and finding the Defendants guilty of fraud of such content without going through the procedure for amendment of the indictment would go beyond the scope of adjudication limited by the facts charged and would substantially infringe the Defendants’ right of defense, and thus cannot be permitted. Meanwhile, according to the record, Nonindicted Person 3 sold the above Avante passenger car to Defendant 1 on condition that Defendant 1 assume the installment-payment debt, and appears to have delivered the power of attorney for transfer of motor vehicle and the seal certificate necessary for transfer registration before Defendant 1 went through the procedure to assume the installment-payment debt. There is no material in the record to ascertain in what form the Defendants sold the above Avante passenger car to Nonindicted Person 4, but considering that the ownership transfer registration for the above Avante passenger car was made directly from Nonindicted Person 3 to Nonindicted Person 4, it may also be presumed that the Defendants posed as agents of Nonindicted Person 3. Even though the manifestation of intent was defective due to deceit, it is appropriate to view that Nonindicted Person 3, by delivering the power of attorney for transfer of motor vehicle and the seal certificate to Defendant 1, granted authority to sell the above Avante passenger car, and so long as such authority existed, even if the purchaser, Nonindicted Person 4, bought the above Avante passenger car believing that the Defendants had been granted authority by Nonindicted Person 3, there can be no mistake arising from deceit.\\n\\nIn the end, there can also be no legal error in misapprehension of law regarding fraud, as argued by the Prosecutor, in the judgment below. All arguments are without merit.\\n\\nTherefore, the appeal is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices as follows."}

question: Which of the following statements regarding the case below is correct? (Where there is a dispute, the precedents are followed.) Party A climbed over a wall into a neighbor’s house with the intent to commit theft, but before he even had time to look for anything to steal, he was immediately discovered by A, who had just returned home. When A shouted, “Who are you?” and tried to seize him, Party A assaulted A in order to escape.
A: If the above case occurred during the daytime, the offense of attempted theft is established against Party A.
B: If the above case occurred during the daytime, even if Party A was carrying a knife with the intent to use it in the offense when he climbed over the wall and entered, if Party A did not actually use the knife when assaulting A, the offense of special residential intrusion or the offense of aggravated assault is not established.
C: If the above case occurred at night, the offense of completed quasi-robbery is established against Party A.
D: If the above case occurred at night, and after Party A assaulted A, he was soon caught by B, who came after him, and then inflicted injury on B in order to escape, a single offense of robbery causing injury is established against Party A in the aggregate.
E: Separate from the above case, if Party A, while trying to steal items inside a vehicle, on the thought that a knife might help him evade arrest if he were discovered, was caught while carrying a knife and inspecting vehicles parked by the roadside on a deserted street at night, the offense of preparation for robbery is established against Party A.
label: D
supporting_precedents: {"[2001DO3447]": "The grounds for final appeal by the Defendant and the court-appointed defense counsel are considered together.\\n\\n1. The court of first instance, upon comprehensively reviewing the evidence it admitted, found that on 2001. 2. 2. at around 01:50, the Defendant, while entering through the front passenger door of the Besta van bearing license plate number Daejeon 70Ga3937 owned by Baek Seung-mok, parked in the underground parking lot of Pyeonghwa Villa located in Samseong-dong, Dong-gu, Daejeon, and rummaging through the toolbox inside, was discovered by Baek Seung-mok, who came running upon hearing the alarm of the theft alarm device installed in said vehicle, and thus failed to accomplish his intent to steal and remained at the attempted stage; thereafter, when Police Sergeant 1 and 2 of the Daejeon Police Station, who had been dispatched upon Baek Seung-mok’s report, attempted to apprehend him, the Defendant, for the purpose of evading arrest, struck Non-indicted 1’s face once with his elbow, thereby assaulting Non-indicted 1, and kicked Non-indicted 2’s shin once with his foot, thereby inflicting on Non-indicted 2 such injuries as a contusion to the right lower leg requiring approximately 2 weeks of treatment, and the court below did not accept the Defendant’s arguments regarding mistake of fact and diminished mental and physical capacity or mental and physical incapacity, dismissed the Defendant’s appeal, and upheld the judgment of the court of first instance.\\n\\n2. Examining the relevant evidence in light of the record, the measures taken by the court of first instance and the court below, which collectively found the charges in this case against the Defendant guilty based on the evidence lawfully examined and admitted, are proper and can be accepted. The record contains no material from which to ascertain that there was any illegality in the process of arrest of the Defendant. And according to the record, since the Defendant cannot be regarded as having been in a state of mental and physical incapacity at the time of the offense in this case, the measures of the court below, which did not accept the arguments on this point, are also proper.\\n\\nHowever, the court of first instance cited by the judgment of the court below, while finding the charges in this case against the Defendant guilty, separately found the Defendant guilty of quasi-robbery as to Non-indicted 1 and robbery causing injury as to Non-indicted 2, viewed these as real concurrence of offenses, and punished the Defendant by aggravating the offense with the heavier punishment of robbery causing injury; and the court below upheld this. However, where a theft offender, for the purpose of evading arrest, at the same opportunity uses force against multiple victims attempting to arrest him and thereby injures only one of them, such conduct of the Defendant should be comprehensively deemed to constitute only one offense of robbery causing injury (see Supreme Court Decision 66DO1392, rendered 1966. 12. 6.), and in this respect the judgment of the court below cannot escape illegality.\\n\\n3. Therefore, pursuant to Articles 391 and 396(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act, the judgment of the court below and the judgment of the court of first instance are both reversed; however, since the case record is sufficient for this Court to render a judgment, the Court will decide the case directly.\\n\\nThe gist of the facts constituting the offense and the evidence against the Defendant are the same as stated in the reasons of the judgment of the court of first instance, and thus they are incorporated by reference pursuant to Articles 399 and 369 of the same Act. In light of the law, the Defendant’s acts set forth in the judgment collectively fall under Article 337 of the Criminal Act; accordingly, among the prescribed punishments, the sentence of imprisonment with prison labor is selected, and, as the act of a person with diminished mental and physical capacity, the Defendant is sentenced to imprisonment for 3 years and 6 months within the range of the sentence mitigated pursuant to Article 10(2), 10(1), and Article 55(1)3 of the Criminal Act; and pursuant to Article 57 of the Criminal Act, the number of days of detention before pronouncement of the judgment of the court of first instance is credited toward the principal sentence, and so, by the unanimous opinion of the judges involved, judgment is rendered as ordered."}

{"[2003DO4417]": "We examine the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n1. Judgment of the court below\\n\\nThe portion of the facts charged against the Defendant concerning quasi-robbery states: \"The Defendant, on 2003. 3. 2. at around 19:45, arrived at the rear of Building 1909 of Kkumdongsan Sinan Apartment, located at 445 Sang-dong, Wonmi-gu, Bucheon-si, and, with the intent to steal property, grasped the railing and climbed up to the rear veranda of Unit 202 of Building 1909. While shining a small flashlight, which he had prepared in advance, at the window to inspect the interior, he was discovered by the victim Kim Gyu-jeong (58), a security guard working at the above apartment. As he jumped down from the veranda and fled in order to evade arrest, he pointed a screwdriver, which he had carried in advance, at the victim’s face and said, 'Don’t catch me; if you catch me, I’ll kill you,' thereby threatening the victim by showing an attitude as if he would inflict some harm on the victim’s body, etc. if the victim did not comply.\" In this regard, the court below held that the Defendant merely used the first-floor veranda railing of the above Sinan Apartment to grasp the veranda railing of Unit 202 on the second floor and, while shining a small flashlight prepared in advance at the window of Unit 202 to see whether the window was locked, was discovered by Kim Gyu-jeong, the security guard of the above Sinan Apartment (the portion of the indictment alleging that the Defendant had already climbed up to the rear veranda of Unit 202 by grasping the railing with his hand lacks evidence to support it); therefore, the Defendant’s conduct alone amounted only to a preparatory stage of the crime of nighttime intrusion into a dwelling with intent to steal, and it could not be concluded that he had further begun the execution of the crime of nighttime intrusion into a dwelling with intent to steal by commencing concrete acts to intrude into the dwelling of Unit 202. Accordingly, the court below upheld the first-instance court’s conclusion, which had acquitted the Defendant of the above facts charged.\\n\\n2. Judgment of this Court\\n\\nHowever, the court below’s determination that the Defendant could not be found to have already climbed up to the rear veranda of the above Apartment Unit 202, and that it could not be concluded that he had at that time commenced the execution of the crime of nighttime intrusion into a dwelling with intent to steal, cannot be accepted.\\n\\nThe subject of quasi-robbery is a thief, that is, a person who has committed theft; once execution of theft has commenced, whether the offense is attempted or completed is immaterial (see Supreme Court en banc decision rendered on 1973. 11. 13. 73DO1553, Supreme Court decision rendered on 1990. 2. 27. 89DO2532, etc.). Therefore, where a person intrudes into another’s dwelling at night with the intent to steal that person’s property, it must be deemed that the person has already commenced the execution of the criminal act of nighttime intrusion into a dwelling with intent to steal at the stage of intrusion into the dwelling (see Supreme Court decision rendered on 1999. 4. 13. 99DO689, etc.). In the case of the crime of unlawful entry into a dwelling, if, with the intent of unlawful entry, a person has begun concrete acts for entry, such as breaking the locking device of the door leading into the dwelling or opening the door, it must be deemed that there has been commencement of execution of the crime of unlawful entry into a dwelling (see Supreme Court decision rendered on 1995. 9. 15. 94DO2561).\\n\\nAccording to the record, the Defendant stated to the investigative authorities: \"When I looked around the apartment, the lights in the second-floor unit were off, so I thought no one was inside. I went around to the back of the apartment and, while holding the second-floor railing through the first-floor veranda railing, I was shining the flashlight I was carrying to see whether the veranda window of the second-floor unit was locked, when a security guard came and shouted, 'Thief!', and I immediately jumped down from there.\" (Investigation record, pp. 27, 49). In court, however, he stated: \"I selected a dark first-floor unit, went to steal things, and when I went to the apartment across the street and looked around, there was a dark second-floor unit, so I stood on the first-floor veranda railing and, while holding the second-floor railing, was shining a flashlight to see whether the veranda window was locked, when I heard someone shout, 'Thief!'\" (trial record, p. 35), \"I went up to the middle of the first floor and was shining a flashlight to confirm that the second-floor veranda door was locked, and I was caught while coming down.\" (trial record, p. 143), and \"I held the second-floor railing with my hand and shone [the light].\" (trial record, p. 144), thus changing his statement each time. The record further shows that the Defendant, at around 19:30 on 2003. 3. 2., entered Apartment 102 of Building 1618 at the Sarangmaeul Cheonggu Apartment, located at 417 Sang-dong, Wonmi-gu, Bucheon-si, by inserting a screwdriver prepared in advance into the window gap, prying up the doorknob to open the door, and trespassing into the above apartment to steal property; and then, at around 19:45 on the same day, upon discovering that Unit 202 of Building 1909 of the nearby Kkumdongsan Sinan Apartment, located at 445 of the same district, was dark, he attempted to trespass into the above apartment and steal property. According to the structure of the above Unit 202 apartment (trial record, p. 123), an aluminum sash glass window was installed on the exterior of the rear veranda of the apartment, and an iron railing approximately 1 to 1.5 meters in height was installed on the outside thereof. The sunset time on 2003. 3. 2. was around 18:26, and at the time of the Defendant’s offense in this case it was already after sunset and the surroundings were dark. Kim Gyu-jeong, the first-instance witness who, as the apartment manager of the above apartment, first discovered the Defendant, testified that at around 19:45 on the same day, when the infrared sensor in Line 2 of Building 1909 of the above apartment operated and he rushed to the scene, he saw the Defendant holding the veranda railing and shouted, \"Thief!\" (trial record, p. 59), and that at that time the Defendant, startled by the shout, jumped down from the second-floor veranda railing and fled (investigation record, p. 20).\\n\\nIf the circumstances are as above, then since the Defendant intended to open the glass window of Unit 202 even if it was locked and trespass into the apartment to steal property, he would have had no reason to stand on the iron railing of the first-floor apartment merely to check whether the door was locked. Further, as the Defendant claims, if he was standing on the iron railing of the first-floor apartment and holding the iron railing of the second-floor apartment, it appears impossible, given the structure of the above apartment, to shine a flashlight to determine whether the glass window of the above Unit 202 apartment was locked. In light of the fact that Kim Gyu-jeong stated that he saw the Defendant jump down from the second-floor veranda railing, it is more probable that the Defendant had climbed up to the iron railing portion of the above Unit 202 apartment, tried to open the glass window while holding that iron railing, and was then discovered by the apartment security guard.\\n\\nIn addition, the commencement of execution of the crime of unlawful entry into a dwelling does not require an act that actually realizes part of the elements of the offense, such as entry into a building managed or occupied by a resident, manager, occupant, etc. against their will; rather, it is sufficient to begin an act that includes an objective danger leading to the realization of the constituent elements of the crime. Therefore, if the Defendant, with the intent to trespass into the above Unit 202 apartment and steal property, climbed up to the iron railing of the above Unit 202 apartment’s veranda and attempted to open the glass window, such conduct may be regarded as a concrete act involving an objective danger of infringing the factual peace of the dwelling.\\n\\nNevertheless, the court below, without further examining when the infrared sensor of the above apartment operates, how long it took for Kim Gyu-jeong to discover the Defendant after confirming that the infrared sensor had operated, or the manner of the Defendant’s conduct at the time Kim Gyu-jeong discovered him, determined that the Defendant could not be deemed to have commenced execution of the crime of nighttime intrusion into a dwelling, thereby committing an error of fact in violation of the rules of evidence, as alleged in the grounds for appeal, or misapprehending the legal principles concerning the timing of commencement of execution of the crime of nighttime intrusion into a dwelling. The grounds for appeal pointing out this issue are well-founded.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the portion of the judgment below concerning acquittal shall be reversed, and this case shall be remanded to the court below for further trial and determination on this portion. It is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating in this case."}

{"[2004DO6432]": "1. Determination on the Grounds of Final Appeal\\n\\na. According to the record, it can be seen that the Defendant, habitually, continued to commit thefts by selecting automobiles parked late at night in sparsely populated residential-area parking lots or on the roadside, where there was little likelihood that the theft offense would be discovered, opening their doors, and stealing property such as coins. In light of this, even though the Defendant was carrying a hiking knife, etc. while roaming the residential area and searching for a target for the offense, it is difficult to conclude that it was proven beyond a reasonable doubt that the Defendant had the purpose of forcibly taking money and valuables from another. Therefore, the lower court’s determination affirming the first-instance judgment to the same effect is correct, and it cannot be said that there was any illegality such as a violation of the rules of evidence, as asserted in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\nb. Article 343 of the Criminal Act concerning the offense of preparation or conspiracy to commit robbery provides, “A person who has made preparations or conspired for the purpose of robbery shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 7 years.” Since the statutory penalty is set considerably heavily, exceeding the statutory penalty for simple theft, and considering that, originally, preparation and conspiracy are subject to punishment only exceptionally when there is a special provision in law (Article 28 of the Criminal Act), it would be desirable to limit cases recognized as the offense of preparation or conspiracy to commit robbery to acts of a type in which a substantial degree of illegality corresponding to the above statutory penalty is manifested.\\n\\nHowever, Article 335 of the Criminal Act concerning quasi-robbery provides only that “when a thief uses force or intimidation for the purpose of resisting recovery of the property, evading arrest, or destroying evidence of the crime, the provisions of the preceding two Articles shall apply,” and does not expressly provide that quasi-robbery must always be treated the same as robbery. Even if a theft offender has the purpose of committing quasi-robbery, that is intrinsically extremely exceptional and limited in that it presupposes the discovery of the theft offense, which is an extreme situation never desired by the theft offender. Moreover, while the Criminal Act punishes theft committed while carrying a deadly weapon as the aggravated constituent offense of aggravated theft (Article 331(2) of the Criminal Act), it does not provide a punishment provision for preparatory acts thereto. If even cases in which a person has the purpose of committing quasi-robbery were deemed punishable as preparation for robbery, then almost all acts of preparing aggravated theft while carrying a deadly weapon would inevitably be punishable as preparation for robbery, which would produce a result contrary to the fact that the Criminal Act does not provide a punishment provision for preparatory acts of aggravated theft committed while carrying a deadly weapon. In addition, considering that Article 7 of the Act on the Punishment of Violent Acts, etc. separately provides for punishment of the act itself of carrying a deadly weapon or other dangerous object without justifiable reason, it is reasonable to hold that, in order for the offense of preparation or conspiracy to commit robbery to be established, it must be recognized that the preparatory or conspiratorial actor had, at least conditionally, the purpose of committing “robbery”; and if it does not reach that level and merely amounts to having the purpose of committing “quasi-robbery,” punishment for the offense of preparation or conspiracy to commit robbery cannot be imposed.\\n\\nAccording to the Defendant’s prior record and the like recognized from the record, it is difficult to conclude that the Defendant, beyond merely thinking, as alleged, that the hiking knife he was carrying might help him evade arrest if the theft offense were unexpectedly discovered, had prepared it with the intention of using it to forcibly take property from another. Since the Defendant’s intent is only recognized to the extent of having the purpose of committing quasi-robbery in this manner, it cannot be said that the Defendant had the purpose of robbery, and thus criminal liability for the offense of preparation for robbery cannot be recognized.\\n\\nFrom the same purport, the lower court’s action in affirming the first-instance judgment that found the portion of the charge concerning the offense of preparation for robbery not guilty is correct, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality such as a misapprehension of the legal principle concerning the offense of preparation for robbery, as asserted in the grounds for final appeal.\\n\\n2. Ex Officio Determination\\n\\nArticle 364(4) of the Criminal Procedure Act provides that the appellate court shall dismiss the appeal by judgment when it finds that there are no grounds for appeal. According to the record, with respect to the portion of the charge against the Defendant concerning the offense of preparation for robbery, the first-instance court rendered a judgment of not guilty, and the Prosecutor appealed. The lower court, while determining in the reasons for its judgment that the Prosecutor’s appeal was without merit, did not pronounce a dismissal of the appeal in the operative part; thus, it can be seen that the lower court judgment was illegal in that it violated Article 364(4) of the Criminal Procedure Act (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2001. 4. 10. rendered 2000DO2049).\\n\\nTherefore, the portion of the lower court judgment concerning the offense of preparation for robbery cannot avoid reversal on this point, and since this portion of the case is deemed sufficiently ready for judgment based on the case record and the evidence examined up to the lower court, this Court will directly render judgment pursuant to Article 396 of the Criminal Procedure Act.\\n\\nThe gist of the Prosecutor’s grounds for appeal concerning the portion on the offense of preparation for robbery is that proof is lacking that the Defendant had the purpose of forcibly taking money and valuables, or that the first-instance judgment’s determination that robbery in the offense of preparation for robbery does not include quasi-robbery is illegal for violation of the rules of evidence and for misapprehension of the legal principle concerning the offense of preparation for robbery. However, as seen above in the determination on the grounds for final appeal, the above determination by the first instance is all correct, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality such as that asserted in the grounds for appeal.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the portion of the lower court judgment concerning the offense of preparation for robbery is reversed, and the Prosecutor’s appeal with respect to this portion is dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as ordered by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

{"[2007DO914]": "We address the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. The element of publicity required for the offense of defamation means a state in which an unspecified number of persons or many persons can perceive it (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 83DO3124, delivered February 28, 1984), and it is not necessary that the content actually become known to an unspecified number of persons or many persons.\\n\\nExamining the above legal principles and the record, the court below, based on the evidence it admitted, found that at the time the Defendant made the statement at issue to the victim, there was a customer, Nonparty 1, nearby; that the victim’s flower nursery, the [trade name 1 omitted] Flower Nursery, had the victim’s husband, Nonparty 2, and an employee; that the Defendant’s flower nursery, the [trade name 2 omitted] Flower Nursery, also had several people present; and that Nonparty 2 ran out upon hearing the Defendant and the victim fighting and tried to stop the fight, during which the Defendant again made the statement at issue. On the basis of those findings, the court below held that the statement had publicity and, accordingly, maintained the first-instance judgment that found the Defendant guilty of the defamation charge in this case. This disposition is proper and persuasive, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality, such as a mistake of fact due to a violation of the rules of evidence, a misapprehension of legal principles, or a violation of precedent, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n2. In light of the purpose of the Act on the Punishment of Violent Acts, etc. and the purport of the provisions of Article 3(1) thereof, the phrase “a person who, carrying a deadly weapon or other dangerous object, committed the offense” in Article 3(1) of the same Act refers to a case where, at the scene of the offense, a deadly weapon or other dangerous object is possessed or carried on one’s person under the intent to “use” it (see Supreme Court Decision 90DO401, delivered April 24, 1990), and it does not include a case where it came to be possessed entirely unrelated to the offense by chance. However, once a deadly weapon or other dangerous object is possessed or carried on one’s person at the scene of the offense under the intent to use it in the commission of the offense, it is not required that the victim recognized that fact or that it was actually used in the offense (see Supreme Court Decision 84DO353, delivered April 10, 1984; Supreme Court Decision 90DO401, delivered April 24, 1990; Supreme Court Decision 2002DO1341, delivered June 14, 2002, et al.).\\n\\nExamining the above legal principles and the record, the court below, after finding the facts as stated in its opinion based on the evidence it admitted, held that even if the Defendant did not originally carry the floral scissors at issue with the intent to inflict injury on the victim, since he intentionally wielded them in the course of an altercation with the victim and thereby inflicted injury on the victim, this constitutes carrying a dangerous object prescribed in Article 3(1) of the Act on the Punishment of Violent Acts, etc. That determination is proper and persuasive, and it cannot be said that there is any illegality, such as a mistake of fact due to a violation of the rules of evidence, a misapprehension of legal principles, or a violation of precedent, as alleged in the grounds of appeal.\\n\\nThe Supreme Court decisions cited in the grounds of appeal concern different factual circumstances and are not appropriate to invoke in this case.\\n\\n3. Therefore, the appeal is dismissed, and it is so adjudged as ordered by the unanimous opinion of the participating Justices."}

question: Which of the following statements are incorrect regarding bribery offenses? (Where there is dispute, according to precedents) (a) In a bribery offense, the “benefit” that constitutes the bribe includes not only money, goods, and other proprietary benefits, but also all tangible and intangible benefits sufficient to satisfy a person’s needs or desires; therefore, it is not to be viewed differently merely because what was provided constituted satisfaction of sexual desire. (b) Since the “third party” in the offense of receiving a bribe for a third party means a person other than the perpetrator and a co-principal, when a public official receives a bribe into an account in the name of Company A, which the official effectively controls, the offense of receiving a bribe for a third party is established. (c) Where, in receiving a bribe, the recipient deceives the giver, the public official who received the bribe is subject to both the offense of bribery and the offense of fraud; because the two offenses protect different legal interests, they must be punished as a real concurrence of offenses. (d) Confiscation of money or goods intended to be used as a bribe concerns identified property, and the proviso to Article 134 of the Criminal Act provides that, if such property cannot be confiscated, its equivalent value shall be collected; thus, where the money or goods intended to be used as a bribe are not identified, their equivalent value must be collected. (e) Where A made an expression of intent to give a bribe to public official A, was refused, and then, after a considerable period of time had passed, again provided A with a bribe under another pretext that can be evaluated as a separate act, and public official A received it, A’s former offense of expressing an intent to give a bribe is absorbed into the latter offense of giving a bribe.
label: E
supporting_precedents: {"[2003DO8077]": "All appeals are dismissed. One hundred days out of the period of detention after the appeal by Defendant 1 shall be credited toward the principal sentence imposed on the said Defendant."}

{"[2009DO2453]": "The grounds of appeal are considered.\\n\\n1. Regarding whether there is a nexus to official duties\\n   a. In bribery offenses, the “official duties” referred to include not only the public official’s duties as such that are under the jurisdiction of the relevant statutes and regulations, but also acts closely related to such duties or official acts in which the public official customarily or actually participates; however, whether a specific act falls within a public official’s official duties must be determined by taking into account both the formal aspect of whether it was performed as part of public service and the substantive aspect of whether it is deemed reasonably necessary in relation to the duties to be performed by that public official (see Supreme Court Decision 2001DO670, decided May 31, 2002, etc.).\\n   Meanwhile, according to Article 13(2) of the former Regulations on the Organization of the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and Its Affiliated Agencies (as in force before amendment by Presidential Decree No. 19868 dated February 5, 2007) and Article 3 [Attached Table] of the former Regulations on Delegation of Authority of the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (as amended by Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Directive No. 371 dated October 19, 2005 and before amendment by Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries Directive No. 422 dated November 22, 2006, and as amended by the aforementioned Directive No. 422), which sets forth the current status of designated delegated authority of the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, the duties of the Shipping Policy Division concern only vessels of Korean-flag shipping companies and do not include administrative dispositions concerning vessels of foreign-flag shipping companies; moreover, specific administrative dispositions concerning vessels of foreign-flag shipping companies cannot be said to have any influence capable of determining them upon public officials belonging to the Shipping Policy Division, and thus cannot be deemed acts closely related to the duties of a public official belonging to the Shipping Policy Division or acts in which such official participates.\\n   b. In light of the foregoing legal principles and the record, when examining the reasons of the judgment below, it is reasonable and persuasive that the court below, on the ground that there was no nexus to official duties, reversed the first-instance judgment, which had affirmed this point of nexus to official duties, and found the Defendant not guilty, even though the Defendant, a public official belonging to the Shipping Policy Division, had received the money stated in the judgment upon being asked by first-instance co-defendant 1 and others to make efforts so that the Defendant could obtain a shipping operation permit for the vessel of Nonparty 1 Co., Ltd., a Chinese-flag shipping company, which permit was under the jurisdiction of the department in charge of shipping operation permits within China. There is no error of law, as alleged in the grounds of appeal, concerning the nexus to official duties in bribery offenses.\\n   The Supreme Court Decision 97DO2609, decided December 26, 1997, etc., cited in the grounds of appeal concerns different facts and is therefore not appropriate for application to this case.\\n\\n2. Regarding the calculation of the amount of bribe and the amount to be collected\\n   a. Article 129(1) of the Criminal Act provides that a public official who receives a bribe in connection with his duties shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 5 years or suspension of qualifications for not more than 10 years, and Article 2(1) of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Crimes aggravates punishment for bribery under Article 129 of the Criminal Act according to the amount of the bribe received: where the amount is not less than 30,000,000 won but less than 50,000,000 won, imprisonment for a fixed term of not less than 5 years shall be imposed (subparagraph 3); where the amount is not less than 50,000,000 won but less than 100,000,000 won, imprisonment for a fixed term of not less than 7 years shall be imposed (subparagraph 2); and where the amount is not less than 100,000,000 won, life imprisonment or imprisonment for not less than 10 years shall be imposed (subparagraph 1). Meanwhile, Article 134 of the Criminal Act provides that bribes received in bribery offenses shall be mandatorily confiscated and, where confiscation is impossible, the equivalent value shall be collected.\\n   As the amount of bribe received in a bribery offense itself constitutes an element of the offense depending on its size, it is subject to strict proof; and even in the case of a simple bribery offense that does not constitute the elements of the offense under the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Crimes, it is likewise subject to proof by evidence because it is subject to confiscation and collection of the value, and where the amount of bribe received cannot be specified, the equivalent value cannot be collected (see Supreme Court Decision 2009DO4391, decided August 20, 2009, etc.).\\n   b. According to the reasons of the judgment below, the court below, with respect to the facts charged in this case that the Defendant received 80,000,000 won from first-instance co-defendants 1 and 2, who were former and current representative directors of Nonparty 2 Co., Ltd., under the pretext of a shipping operation permit from the Ministry of Communications of China and the pretext of facilitating the business affairs of Nonparty 2 Co., Ltd., and thereby received a bribe in connection with his duties, determined that the part concerning facilitating the business affairs of Nonparty 2 Co., Ltd. was related to the Defendant’s duties, but the part concerning the shipping operation permit from the Ministry of Communications of China was not related to the Defendant’s duties; then, in cases where remuneration or consideration for official acts and remuneration or consideration for acts outside official duties are inseparably combined, and the remuneration or consideration for acts outside official duties is assessed as greater in weight than that for official acts, but it is difficult to distinguish the size of each corresponding part by proof based on objective materials, the distinction must be made by estimation through assessment considering all circumstances. The court below, considering the circumstances as stated in the judgment, namely: ① the main pretext for which the Defendant received 80,000,000 won was related to the shipping operation permit, and the secondary pretext was the general facilitation of business affairs related to the operation of Nonparty 2 Co., Ltd.; ② although the Defendant had known first-instance co-defendants 1 and 2 for a considerable time, the time when he began to receive money was immediately after the issue concerning the shipping operation permit arose; ③ unless there was a specific and real problem that had arisen or was expected to arise in the future and the bribe was provided to the Defendant for that reason, it does not appear that a very large amount would have been provided in light of the Defendant’s position, and, in fact, the amount paid by Nonparty 3, etc., who were the Defendant’s subordinates, from first-instance co-defendants 1 and 2 was 9,000,000 won, and, among the amounts received by Nonparty 4, who was then Vice Minister of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries and was punished for bribery around the same period, the largest amount, when viewed by each briber, was 25,000,000 won, while in all other cases it was less than 20,000,000 won; ④ the Defendant appears to have expended a considerable amount of costs in the course of contacting Chinese officials in relation to the shipping operation permit issue; ⑤ given the magnitude of the economic loss sustained by Nonparty 1 Co., Ltd. or Nonparty 2 Co., Ltd. because the shipping operation permit issue was not resolved, the remuneration or consideration for efforts to resolve such issue appears likely to have reached a substantial amount; and based on these circumstances, it was appropriate to regard 75%, namely 60,000,000 won, of the 80,000,000 won received by the Defendant as the part related to the shipping operation permit, and 25%, namely 20,000,000 won, as the part related to facilitating the business affairs of Nonparty 2 Co., Ltd.; further, on the ground that this was a case where the amount of bribe received could not be objectively and accurately calculated by strict proof, the court below applied the offense of accepting a bribe prescribed in Article 129(1) of the Criminal Act to the Defendant, but held that only 20,000,000 won, being the consideration for facilitating the business affairs of Nonparty 2 Co., Ltd. out of the 80,000,000 won received by the Defendant, should be collected.\\n   c. However, according to the legal principles stated above, if the nature of the 80,000,000 won received by the Defendant as consideration for duties related to official duties and the nature of it as consideration for duties not related to official duties are inseparably combined so that their distinction is objectively impossible, then collection should not have been made at all; or, if collection was to be made, the amount of bribe received related to official duties should have been specified and the applicable provision and amount to be collected should have been determined accordingly. Nevertheless, the court below, as stated in the judgment, merely on the ground that it was difficult to distinguish between the two, estimated without clear basis, by a proportional method, the amount of bribe received in connection with duties related to official duties and ordered collection thereof. This constitutes an error of law concerning the calculation and collection of the amount of bribe received and a failure to conduct the necessary deliberation, and thus must be deemed to have affected the outcome of the judgment (the very fact that the court categorized this as a simple bribery offense under the Criminal Act on the ground that the amount of bribe received could not be calculated, while at the same time specifying and collecting the amount to be collected as 20,000,000 won, cannot but be said to be self-contradictory).\\n\\n3. Therefore, the judgment of the court below is reversed, and the case is remanded to the court below for further trial and determination; it is so adjudged in accordance with the unanimous opinion of the Justices participating."}

{"[2013DO13937]": "We adjudicate the grounds of appeal.\\n\\n1. Regarding the Defendant’s grounds of appeal (to the extent that the contents of the written brief of oral argument submitted after the expiration of the period for submitting the statement of grounds of appeal supplement the grounds of appeal)\\n   a. In the crime of bribery, the benefit that constitutes the subject matter of a bribe includes not only money, goods, and other pecuniary benefits, but also all tangible and intangible benefits sufficient to satisfy a person’s needs and desires (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2002DO3539, rendered on November 26, 2002), and it is not to be otherwise viewed merely because what was provided was the satisfaction of sexual desire.\\n\\n   In addition, the protected legal interest of the crime of bribery is the fairness of a public official’s execution of duties, the public trust therein, and the unpurchasability of official conduct, and since it does not require a request related to official duties or an improper act, the existence of a special request is not necessary in recognizing the bribery nature of the money or goods received. Furthermore, it is sufficient that the money or goods were received in relation to official duties, and there is no need for a quid pro quo relationship with individual official acts; where a public official receives money, goods, or other benefits from a person who is the object of the official’s duties, such receipt cannot be deemed unrelated to those duties unless there are special circumstances, such as where, in light of social norms, it is clearly recognized as being nothing more than a customary return or as being due to a need for social interaction arising from a personal acquaintance. If a public official has received money or goods in relation to official duties, then even if the money or goods were exchanged under the guise of social courtesy, the money or goods so received constitute a bribe (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2001DO3579, rendered on October 12, 2001).\\n\\n   Meanwhile, whether a benefit obtained by a public official constitutes a “bribe” as an improper benefit having a quid pro quo relationship with official duties should be determined by taking into account all relevant circumstances, such as the content of that public official’s duties, the relationship between the duties and the provider of the benefit, whether a special personal relationship exists between the two parties, the amount of the benefit, and the circumstances and timing of the receipt of the benefit; and, in light of the fact that the crime of bribery protects the fairness of a public official’s execution of duties, the public trust therein, and the unpurchasability of official conduct, whether the public at large would come to doubt the fairness of the execution of duties because the public official received the benefit also serves as a criterion in determining whether the crime of bribery is established (see, e.g., Supreme Court Decision 2010DO17797, rendered on March 24, 2011).\\n\\n   b. In light of the foregoing legal principles and the like, upon examination of the record, it is proper for the court below, for the reasons stated in its holding, to have deemed the acts of quasi-intercourse and intercourse in this case to constitute “bribery” and to have recognized their connection to official duties, thereby finding the charge of receipt of bribes among the facts charged in this case to be guilty. There is no illegality, as asserted in the grounds of appeal, such as finding facts in violation of the rules of logic and experience or misconstruing the legal principles concerning the relationship to official duties, quid pro quo relationship, or intent in the crime of bribery.\\n\\n2. Regarding the Prosecutor’s grounds of appeal\\n   Upon examination of the record in light of the relevant legal principles, it is acceptable for the court below, for the reasons stated in its holding, to have rendered a not guilty verdict on the charge of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights among the facts charged in this case on the ground that there was no proof of a crime. There is no illegality, as asserted in the grounds of appeal, such as finding facts in violation of the rules of logic and experience or misconstruing the legal principles concerning the crime of abuse of authority and obstruction of the exercise of rights.\\n\\n3. Conclusion\\n   Therefore, all appeals are dismissed, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the disposition by the unanimous opinion of the Justices of the Supreme Court involved."}

{"[2015DO12838]": "We examine the grounds of final appeal.\\n\\n1. Concerning the argument on the amount of the bribe in the offense of demanding a bribe\\n\\nAccording to the record, the Defendant merely argued in the lower appellate court, as a ground for appeal, that the lower court’s finding, with respect to the offense of receiving a bribe, that all of the money received by the Defendant was a bribe constituted a factual error or misapprehension of law; the argument that, in the offense of demanding a bribe, the amount of the bribe is the amount equivalent to the financial benefit on the loan, rather than the entire amount of money the Defendant demanded as a loan, was made only upon reaching the final appeal stage and therefore cannot constitute a proper ground for final appeal.\\n\\nEven if examined further, according to the reasons stated in the judgment of the lower court, the lower court upheld as proper the trial court’s finding that the 5 million won demanded by the Defendant from Non-Indicted Person 1 on 2014. 6. 23. and the 23 million won demanded by the Defendant from Non-Indicted Person 2 on 2014. 2. 8. both constituted bribes within the offense of demanding a bribe.\\n\\nIn light of the relevant legal doctrine and the evidence duly admitted by the lower court and the trial court, the above disposition by the lower court is proper, and there is no error in the lower court’s factual findings, such as by violating the rules of logic and experience and exceeding the limits of free evaluation of evidence, or in misapprehending the legal doctrine of the offense of demanding a bribe, as alleged in the grounds of final appeal.\\n\\n2. Concerning the argument on collection\\n\\na. Article 134 of the Criminal Act provides that money and valuables intended for bribery shall be mandatorily forfeited, and if forfeiture is impossible, their value shall be collected; in light of the fact that forfeiture is for specific objects and collection presupposes that forfeiture was originally possible, where the money and valuables intended for bribery were not specified, they cannot be forfeited, and their value cannot be collected either (see Supreme Court Decision 96DO221 rendered on 1996. 5. 8.).\\n\\nb.
