If the National Assembly turns away from this duty, it will be committing dereliction of duty. Accordingly, Assembly members Yoo Yong-tae, Hong Sa-deok, and 157 other members of the National Assembly, united by a bipartisan will to uphold the Constitution and the national legal order, hereby propose the impeachment of President Roh Moo-hyun as the final means to block the President’s unlawful and unconstitutional acts, restore the violated rule of law, secure the future of the Republic of Korea and the happiness of its people, and in particular ensure the proper conduct of the 17th general election."}

{"[2004HEONNA1]": "[Appendix 1] List of Counsel for the Impeachment Prosecutors: omitted  \\n[Appendix 2] List of Counsel for the Respondent: omitted  \\n[Appendix 3] Full Text of the National Assembly’s Impeachment Resolution\\n\\nImpeachment Resolution of President (Roh Moo-hyun)\\n\\nOrder\\n\\nAt the 2nd plenary session of the 246th National Assembly (extraordinary session) (2004. 3. 12), with approval obtained pursuant to Article 65, paragraph 2 of the Constitution, the impeachment of President (Roh Moo-hyun) is brought.\\n\\nPerson subject to impeachment\\n\\nName: Roh Moo-hyun (Roh Mu-hyeon)  \\nPosition: President\\n\\nGrounds for Impeachment\\n\\nPresident Roh Moo-hyun, as the Head of State who should uphold the Constitution and laws, has forgotten his duty and continued unlawful election campaigning for a specific political party, and as a result, on March 3, 2004, from the National Election Commission, a constitutional organ, he received, for the first time in constitutional history, a determination and warning that the incumbent President had violated the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act. Nevertheless, instead of reflecting on himself, he ignored this warning and stated that he would continue to openly support a specific political party regardless of the election law, thereby displaying an extra-constitutional and extra-legal dictatorial attitude that flatly denies the rule of law, which is the foundation of democratic constitutionalism. The National Assembly cannot leave such a situation denying the rule of law unchecked. In addition, President Roh Moo-hyun, due to the severe power-related corruption of himself and his close associates, created a national crisis in which he could not properly carry out state administration, and due to the political instability caused by President Roh Moo-hyun’s insincere performance of his duties and reckless administration of state affairs, state affairs have reached the point of collapse, plunging the people into extreme misery. Accordingly, it has become manifest that President Roh Moo-hyun no longer has the qualifications or ability to govern the country, and thus this impeachment resolution has been introduced for the sake of upholding the Constitution and the happiness of the people and the future of the nation; the specific three grounds are as follows.\\n\\nFirst, President Roh Moo-hyun has continuously violated the Constitution and laws and has thereby disturbed the legal order of the state.\\n\\n(A) As the National Election Commission on March 3, 2004 determined that recent remarks by President Roh Moo-hyun constituted a violation of the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act, President Roh Moo-hyun, at a joint press conference held on February 18, 2004 with six media outlets in the Gyeongin region at the Blue House, said, “If even the line for blocking constitutional revision collapses, I really cannot tell what will happen after that,” thereby threatening the people and inducing support for a specific political party; and at the presidential press conference invited by the Broadcast Press Club and broadcast live nationwide on February 24, 2004, President Roh Moo-hyun stated, “Whether you will let me do it properly for the next four years or whether you will drive me out because you cannot bear it, the people will make it clear,” and also, “I expect the people to give overwhelming support to the Open Uri Party in the general election,” and further, “If the President does something well and our party can gain votes, I want to do everything that is lawful,” and so on. This constitutes unlawful advance election campaigning, which not only violates Article 9, paragraph 1 of the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act (duty of political neutrality of public officials), but also violates Article 60, paragraph 1 of the same Act (persons prohibited from election campaigning), Article 85 (prohibition on election campaigning by using one’s status), and Article 86 (prohibition on acts by public officials, etc. influencing elections), and therefore should be punished under Article 255, paragraph 1, item 1 of the same Act (offense of illegal election campaigning).\\n\\n(B) On December 19, 2003, President Roh Moo-hyun attended the “Remember 1219” event hosted by Nosamo and incited illegal election campaigning by urging, “The citizens’ revolution is continuing; please step forward once again.” Also, at a meeting with journalists from the Gangwon region on February 5, 2004, he stated, “The political participation of people like Gukcham 0415 should be legally and politically permitted and encouraged,” and thereby, as a President who had sworn to observe the Constitution and who bears responsibility to uphold the legal order of the state, engaged in conduct disrupting the state by fostering a movement of civil disobedience. Furthermore, as determined by the Constitutional Court on August 30, 2001, that any form of campaign to elect or defeat a candidate by a third party other than an election campaign worker constitutes illegal election campaigning, he encouraged unlawful election campaigning in violation of Article 87 of the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act (prohibition on election campaigning by organizations), and simultaneously violated Article 9, paragraph 1 of the same Act (duty of political neutrality of public officials) and Article 59 (election campaign period).\\n\\n(C) In the Chosun Ilbo report dated February 27, 2004 concerning the Open Uri Party’s general election strategy document, the expressions “formation of a party-government-presidential joint command center” and “deployment of both hard-line and soft-line persuasion strategies for persons to be recruited by the joint command center” reveal organized election interference by the Blue House; this is clearly an illegal election using governmental authority, and President Roh Moo-hyun, as the head of the Blue House, bears responsibility for directing it and therefore violated Article 9, paragraph 1 of the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act (duty of political neutrality of public officials) and Article 86, paragraph 1, item 2 (prohibition on acts by public officials, etc. influencing elections, namely prohibition on participating in the planning of election campaigning or being involved in the implementation of such planning).\\n\\n(D) At the New Year press conference on January 14, 2004, he said, “There were people who supported reform and people who, because reform was uncertain, did not support it, so they split apart, and the people who supported me during the presidential election are in the Open Uri Party, so I want to be together with them,” thereby defining the Democratic Party as an anti-reform party; and at a meeting with close associates on December 24, 2003, he skillfully used an off-the-record setting to spread to the press the remark, “If you vote for the Democratic Party, you help the Grand National Party,” and, among other things, received an official sanction from the National Election Commission on December 30, 2003, in the form of a “request for cooperation in a fair election” on the ground that there was a concern of harming the freedom and fairness of the election. Thus, as the President representing the state, he repeatedly engaged in speech and conduct excluding and eliminating a specific political party, and violated Article 8, paragraph 3 of the Constitution (the state’s duty to protect political parties).\\n\\n(E) By threatening the people and inducing support for a specific political party and by repeatedly engaging in speech and conduct affecting public sentiment in the general election, President Roh Moo-hyun is obstructing the people’s free election; this constitutes an unlawful act falling under Article 237, paragraph 1, item 3 of the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act (crime of interfering with the freedom of election), and is an act violating Article 24 of the Constitution (right to vote as a fundamental right of the people), Article 19 (freedom of conscience), and Article 10 (state duty to guarantee fundamental rights).\\n\\n(F) As stated above, President Roh Moo-hyun, as the head of the executive branch, unlawfully interfered in the general election for the National Assembly members constituting the legislature, thereby destroying the spirit of separation of powers in the Constitution. Also, on March 4, 2004, President Roh, through Senior Presidential Secretary for Public Relations Lee Byung-wan, reacted to the National Election Commission’s decision warning against election interference by saying that he “cannot accept it,” expressing regret, and stating that he would continue to openly support a specific political party, thereby engaging in constitution-destroying conduct that flatly disregards the lawful decisions of another constitutional organ. Thereafter, Kang Kum-won terminated the contract but settled President Roh Moo-hyun’s personal debt by not taking back the money provided from Lee Ki-myung. It was confirmed that President Roh Moo-hyun had been informed in advance by Ahn Hee-jung and Kang Kum-won of this illegal sham sale transaction plan. Also, when Sun Bong-sul and O Cheol-ju, who had provided collateral for Jangsucheon in July 2002 but lost Jinyang Arcade through compulsory auction and demanded compensation for their losses, President Roh Moo-hyun instructed Ahn Hee-jung and Choi Doo-sop to “compensate for the losses,” and accordingly Ahn Hee-jung is confirmed to have raised a total of 790 million won in illegal political funds from September 2002 until December of that year and delivered it to Sun Bong-sul and others. During the 2002 primary to select the Democratic Party’s presidential candidate, Ahn Hee-jung also received a total of 50 million won in illegal political funds and used it as President Roh Moo-hyun’s primary campaign funds, as confirmed by the prosecution’s investigation. The prosecution also confirmed that Ahn Hee-jung received a total of 3 billion won in illegal presidential election funds from Samsung during the presidential election. In addition, after President Roh Moo-hyun took office, between March and August 2003, Ahn Hee-jung received 600 million won into a nominee account in the name of Kang Kum-won’s nephew, and in March and August 2003 he received a total of 400 million won from two businesses in the Busan area. Ahn Hee-jung also personally embezzled some of the received illegal funds, including purchasing an apartment with 200 million won of them. In other words, President Roh Moo-hyun, both during his candidacy and after becoming president-elect, instigated crimes in co-principal relationship with Ahn Hee-jung, and after the commencement of presidential duties, while introducing Ahn Hee-jung to the public as a “business partner,” he aided and abetted Ahn Hee-jung’s collection of illegal funds.\\n\\n3. Lee Kwang-jae, who has been found to have received a total of around 100 million won in illegal political funds so far, was President Roh Moo-hyun’s closest associate like his alter ego, and on November 9, 2002, at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel in Seoul, immediately after President Roh Moo-hyun finished a breakfast with Moon Byung-wook, chairman of Sun & Moon, and left the room, he received 100 million won in illegal political funds from Moon Byung-wook.\\n\\n4. Yang Kil-seung, Senior Presidential Secretary for the Blue House Annex Office, received entertainment from Lee Won-ho, the president of Kiss Tourism Night, who was under investigation in June 2003 on charges of tax evasion, extortion, and instigation of murder, and was arrested on charges including solicitation to suppress the investigation.\\n\\n5. Yeo Taek-soo, who has been found to have received a total of 330 million won in illegal political funds so far, as President Roh Moo-hyun’s alter ego and aide, received 30 million won in illegal political funds from Moon Byung-wook on December 7, 2002, while in President Roh Moo-hyun’s presence. Also, by appointing Yeo Taek-soo, who was in such a co-principal relationship, to serve as an administrative officer at the Blue House after taking office, President Roh Moo-hyun aided and abetted Yeo Taek-soo in receiving 300 million won in illegal funds from Lotte.\\n\\n6. What is even more shocking is that, with President Roh Moo-hyun’s connivance, Administrative Officer Yeo Taek-soo provided 200 million won out of this 300 million won of black funds to the Open Uri Party as founding funds. Since Yeo Taek-soo is an alter ego under the direct command and supervision of President Roh Moo-hyun, it cannot be viewed as a voluntary provision of founding funds. President Roh Moo-hyun acted as an indirect perpetrator in the process of providing these illegal founding funds. This 200 million won is presumed to be only the “tip of the iceberg” among the illegal founding funds raised through President Roh’s participation as a co-principal.\\n\\n(D) President Roh Moo-hyun stated at the Blue House meeting with leaders of political parties on December 14, 2003 that he would retire from politics if the amount of his illegal funds exceeded one-tenth of the Grand National Party’s. However, the amount of illegal political funds received by President Roh’s side reached 11.3 billion won, already exceeding one-tenth of Lee Hoi-chang’s side’s illegal funds of 82.3 billion won and reaching one-seventh. This result came from an investigation focused only on the illegal presidential campaign funds received from the five largest conglomerates by the Grand National Party. If, starting with the recent revelation that Ahn Hee-jung received illegal presidential election funds such as 600 million won from Lotte and 3 billion won from Samsung, an investigation into the five largest conglomerates is fairly conducted, the scale of the illegal presidential election funds on President Roh Moo-hyun’s side will increase further. Therefore, before suffering even greater political damage, it would be appropriate for President Roh to resign from the presidency in accordance with his promise to retire from politics. President Roh is already at risk of completely losing the people’s trust as Head of State, as the illegal presidential election funds are approaching one-seventh. However, far from feeling responsible for this situation, President Roh has merely been hurrying to conceal the fact of corruption involvement, and recklessly repeated threats of renewed confidence and boasts of retiring from politics, as if discarding even the grave duties of the presidency like a used rag, and now is engaging in a shameful exercise by manipulating the amount of illegal funds in a bizarre manner. But now that the scale of the illegal presidential election funds is beginning to be revealed as equal to or exceeding the “one-tenth” line that President Roh himself set, there is no choice left but to step down. The loss of public trust in the President means that the minimum authority and leadership required to perform presidential duties has collapsed. The people cannot simply keep waiting forever for the President’s confession. The National Assembly also cannot leave this situation unattended any longer. After much discussion, anguish, and agony, the National Assembly first urged the President to apologize and waited for President Roh’s public declaration and pledge that he would respect the Constitution and laws. However, the President, dismissing the election law violation determined by the National Election Commission as something “minor,” “trivial and ambiguous,” has continued to make anti-rule-of-law remarks that he will not submit to the National Assembly’s discussion of impeachment, and ultimately refuses to apologize and promise prevention of recurrence. Accordingly, the National Assembly is faced with the situation where, because President Roh denies the rule of law, the foundation of democratic constitutionalism, in this way and ignores even his own promise to retire from politics while stubbornly refusing to step down, it cannot but bring an impeachment motion according to legal procedures with an urgent sense of necessity.\\n\\n(E) Furthermore, in order to mislead the corruption cases in which he was involved, President Roh Moo-hyun has intimidated the prosecution and the people by saying that he would hold a referendum on renewed confidence or that he would find another way for renewed confidence, and has presented investigative guidelines by saying things like “retire from politics if the one-tenth line is exceeded,” “Tico level,” and “several million won, several tens of millions of won.” In this way, President Roh has directly and indirectly interfered with and obstructed investigations into the four major categories of illegal funds: presidential primary campaign funds, presidential election campaign funds, congratulatory money for winning the election, and Open Uri Party founding funds. Also, whereas opposition lawmakers are arrested even for minor reasons, the investigations concerning Open Uri Party figures close to the President, such as Kim Won-ki, Presidential Political Advisor; Shin Kye-ryun, former chief secretary to the president-elect; and Lee Ho-woong, former head of organization at President Roh’s presidential campaign, are uniformly limited to exculpatory investigations, such as non-prosecution or non-custodial booking. This is all due to President Roh Moo-hyun’s obstruction of the investigation. President Roh’s interference with and obstruction of the prosecution’s investigation has reached a level that can by no means be politically tolerated.\\n\\n(F) President Roh Moo-hyun cannot avoid moral and political responsibility regarding corruption by close associates and obstruction of corruption investigations, and in particular, with respect to criminal acts committed through close associates in co-principal relationship after the commencement of the performance of official duties on February 25, 2003, he cannot avoid legal responsibility and therefore has “violated laws in the performance of official duties.” This is because, even after February 25, 2003, the date on which President Roh Moo-hyun began performing duties as President, he aided and abetted the corrupt crimes of Ahn Hee-jung, Choi Doo-sop, Yeo Taek-soo, Yang Kil-seung, and others, and thus was directly and indirectly involved in those corrupt crimes as a co-principal specified under Articles 30, 31, 32, and 33 of the Criminal Act and as an indirect perpetrator under Article 34 of the same Act. On December 29, 2003, the prosecution also publicly stated that it had recognized and confirmed the co-principal relationship between President Roh Moo-hyun and his close associates. However, the prosecution said, “We have our own conclusion, but in light of the President’s constitutional privilege against criminal prosecution, the continuity of official duties, and the spirit of the Constitution, it would not be appropriate to disclose the contents,” and thus inevitably deferred direct investigation and prosecution of President Roh Moo-hyun. Whenever a corruption case involving him as a co-principal was exposed, President Roh Moo-hyun directly or indirectly influenced the investigation by giving the prosecution the direction and policy of the investigation, and in order to cover up his own involvement, he threatened the people with the renewed-confidence card and shook the country amid economic hardship. It goes without saying that, in a situation where President Roh, a co-principal in the corruption of close associates, is obstructing the investigation, the prosecution cannot uncover the power-related corruption cases of the so-called “living power.” For this reason, the National Assembly must now step forward and impeach President Roh Moo-hyun according to the procedures prescribed by the Constitution and laws.\\n\\nThird, as shown by the fact that our economy is remaining at a growth rate far lower than that of the United States despite the global economic boom, President Roh Moo-hyun is causing the national economy and state affairs to collapse and plunging the people’s livelihood into ruin, thereby subjecting the people to even more severe pain and misery than during the IMF crisis.\\n\\n(A) Economists have characterized one year of Roh’s rule as “failure in state administration, the lost year,” and even the citizens who voted for President Roh in the last presidential election have turned their backs on President Roh, confronting an astonishing situation in which, only one year into his administration, he has fallen into a lame-duck state.\\n\\n(B) The fundamental cause of this collapse of state administration cannot be denied to lie in President Roh Moo-hyun’s repeated verbal blunders and reversals, beginning with his rash remark that “I cannot go on as President,” his change of position to an anti-war stance on the Iraq War after declaring troop dispatch to Iraq, his unconstitutional proposal for a referendum on renewed public confidence and his declaration that he would retire from politics, his insincere performance of duties and reckless administration that lack any seriousness or consistency, and the so-called “all-in strategic” illegal advance election campaigning that pours all efforts only into the general election while neglecting presidential duties.\\n\\n(C) Therefore, President Roh Moo-hyun is now violating Article 10 of the Constitution, which prescribes the people’s “right to pursue happiness” and the “state’s duty to guarantee fundamental rights,” and is abandoning the duty of “faithful performance of duties as President” specified in Article 69 of the Constitution.\\n\\nAt present, our country is in a crisis of constitutional destruction in which the President, with an extra-constitutional and extra-legal attitude, denies the rule of law and disregards the warning of the constitutional organ, the National Election Commission, as well as the National Assembly’s own authority. {"[2004HEONNA1]": "[Appendix 1] List of Counsel for the Impeachment Committee: omitted  \\n[Appendix 2] List of Counsel for the Respondent: omitted  \\n[Appendix 3] Full Text of the National Assembly’s Resolution on Impeachment\\n\\nImpeachment Resolution of President Roh Moo-hyun (盧武鉉)  \\nOrder\\n\\nAt the 2nd plenary session of the 246th National Assembly (extraordinary session) on March 12, 2004, with the approval under Article 65(2) of the Constitution, impeachment of President Roh Moo-hyun is proposed.\\n\\nPerson Subject to Impeachment  \\nName: Roh Moo-hyun (盧武鉉)  \\nPosition: President\\n\\nGrounds for Impeachment\\n\\nPresident Roh Moo-hyun, as the Head of State who should uphold the Constitution and the laws, has forgotten his duty and has continued illegal election campaigning for a particular political party, and as a result, on March 3, 2004, he received from the National Election Commission, a constitutional organ, for the first time in constitutional history, a determination that a sitting President had violated the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act, along with a warning measure; nevertheless, instead of self-restraint, he ignored this warning and stated that he would continue to publicly support a particular political party regardless of the election laws, thereby displaying an ultra-constitutional and ultra-legal dictatorial attitude that flatly denies the rule of law, the foundation of democratic constitutionalism. The National Assembly cannot leave such a situation denying the rule of law unattended. In addition, President Roh Moo-hyun has caused a national crisis in which the State could not be normally administered due to severe power-related corruption by himself and his close associates, and political instability caused by President Roh Moo-hyun’s insincere performance of duties and reckless administration has brought State affairs to the point of collapse, plunging the people into extreme misfortune. Thus, it has become manifest that President Roh Moo-hyun no longer has the qualifications or ability to govern the country, and therefore, in order to uphold the Constitution and for the happiness of the people and the future of the nation, this impeachment motion has been initiated; the three specific grounds are as follows.\\n\\nFirst, President Roh Moo-hyun has continuously violated the Constitution and the laws, thereby disrupting the legal order of the State.\\n\\n(a) As the National Election Commission on March 3, 2004 determined that President Roh Moo-hyun’s recent remarks constituted a violation of the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act, President Roh Moo-hyun, at a joint press conference with six media outlets in the Gyeongin area held at the Blue House on February 18, 2004, stated, “If even the line for blocking constitutional revision collapses, I myself really cannot tell what will happen after that,” thereby threatening the people and inducing support for a particular political party; and at the presidential press conference hosted by the Broadcasting Journalists Club and broadcast live nationwide on February 24, 2004, President Roh Moo-hyun stated, “The people should clearly decide whether [I] will be allowed to do it properly for the next four years or whether they cannot bear it and will make [me] step down,” and “I expect the people to overwhelmingly support the Uri Party in the general election,” and also, “If the President does something well and only if our party can obtain votes, I would like to do everything that is lawful,” which constitutes illegal advance election campaigning subject to punishment under Article 255(1)1 of the same Act (crime of unlawful election campaigning), while simultaneously violating Article 9(1) (duty of political neutrality of public officials), Article 60(1) (persons who may not engage in election campaigning), Article 85 (prohibition on election campaigning by use of position), and Article 86 (prohibition of acts by public officials, etc. influencing elections) of the same Act.\\n\\n(b) On December 19, 2003, President Roh Moo-hyun attended the “Remember 1219” event hosted by Nosamo and incited illegal election campaigning by exhorting, “The civic revolution is continuing; this is manifestly illegal government-backed election manipulation, and President Roh Moo-hyun, as the head of the Blue House, bore responsibility for directing it and thereby violated Article 9(1) (duty of political neutrality of public officials) and Article 86(1)2 (prohibition, among acts by public officials, etc. influencing elections, of participating in the planning of election campaigning or being involved in the implementation of such planning) of the Public Official Election and Election Malpractice Prevention Act.\\n\\n(d) At the New Year press conference on January 14, 2004, he stated, “People who supported reform and people who did not support reform because they were uneasy have become divided, and I would like to be together with those who supported me in the presidential election and are now in the Uri Party,” thereby defining the Democratic Party as an anti-reform party; and also, at a meeting with close associates on December 24, 2003, he cleverly used an informal setting to spread to the media the statement, “If you vote for the Democratic Party, you help the Grand National Party,” and thus, by repeatedly using speech and conduct as the representative of the State to reject and destroy a particular political party, he violated Article 8(3) of the Constitution (the State’s duty to protect political parties), while receiving from the National Election Commission, on December 30, 2003, a formal sanction measure in the form of a “request for cooperation in a fair election” on the ground that it was likely to harm the freedom and fairness of the election.\\n\\n(e) By threatening the people and inducing support for a particular political party and repeatedly engaging in speech and conduct affecting public sentiment for the general election, President Roh Moo-hyun has been obstructing the people’s free elections; Starting with the recent revelation that Ahn Hee-jung received illegal presidential election funds such as 600 million won from Lotte and 3 billion won from Samsung, if the investigation into the five major conglomerates proceeds fairly in the future, the scale of illegal presidential election funds on President Roh Moo-hyun’s side will increase even further. Therefore, before suffering even greater political damage, President Roh Moo-hyun would do well to resign from the Presidency in accordance with his promise to retire from politics. President Roh is already in danger of completely losing the people’s trust as Head of State because the illegal presidential election funds have nearly reached one-seventh. However, far from feeling responsible for such a situation, President Roh has been preoccupied only with concealing the fact of corruption involvement, and rashly repeated threats of confidence reaffirmation and declarations of retirement from politics, as if he would discard even the heavy duties of the Presidency like a used rag, and is now engaging in a disgraceful game of figures through manipulation of strange amounts of illegal funds. But now that the scale of illegal presidential election funds has begun to emerge as being at or above the one-tenth line that President Roh himself presented, there is no choice left but resignation. The President’s loss of public trust means that the minimum authority and leadership required to perform the duties of the Presidency has been destroyed. The people cannot simply wait endlessly for the President’s confession. The National Assembly also cannot leave this situation unattended any longer. After many debates, anguish, and agony, the National Assembly first urged the President to apologize and waited for President Roh’s declaration and pledge to the people that he would respect the Constitution and the laws. However, the President continues to disregard the election-law violations found by the National Election Commission as “minor things” and “small and ambiguous things,” and while continuing anti-rule-of-law remarks that he will not yield to the National Assembly’s impeachment discussion, he has ultimately refused to apologize and to promise recurrence prevention. Accordingly, because President Roh refuses to resign while denying the rule of law, which is the foundation of democratic constitutionalism, and ignoring even his own promise to retire from politics, the National Assembly has reached a situation in which, with a desperate heart, it cannot but impeach him according to legal procedure.\\n\\n(e) Furthermore, in order to mislead the corruption cases in which he was involved, President Roh Moo-hyun has been threatening the prosecution and the people by talking about holding a referendum on reaffirming confidence or searching for another method of reaffirming confidence, and has been giving investigative guidelines by saying things like “retirement from politics if the one-tenth line is exceeded,” “Tico level,” and “several million won, tens of millions of won.” In this way, President Roh has directly and indirectly interfered with and obstructed the investigation into the four major illegal funds, namely the presidential nomination campaign funds, presidential election funds, congratulatory money for the election victory, and Uri Party founding funds. As shown by the investigation results into the illegal presidential election funds provided by the five major conglomerates, namely 73.2 billion won received by the Lee Hoi-chang campaign and 3.6 billion won received by the Roh Moo-hyun campaign, or the midterm investigative result on the entire illegal presidential election funds showing 82.3 billion won versus 11.3 billion won, the investigation into the four major illegal funds has been conducted extremely unfairly and has also been grossly insufficient; and as for the founding funds, which revealed only “the tip of the iceberg,” they have been brushed off as merely Yeo Tae-soo’s personal corruption, and as for the primary campaign funds, the investigation has barely reached a preliminary stage. Also, while opposition lawmakers are arrested even for minor reasons, the investigations concerning Kim Won-ki, Presidential Political Affairs Special Advisor of the Uri Party; Shin Kye-ryun, former Chief of Staff to the President-elect; and Lee Ho-woong, former Head of the Organization Headquarters of candidate Roh Moo-hyun’s presidential campaign, who are aides close to the President, have been handled either as no-charge dispositions or non-custodial indictments, consistently amounting to a merely exculpatory investigation. This is all because of President Roh Moo-hyun’s obstruction of the investigation. President Roh’s interference with and obstruction of the prosecution’s investigation has reached a level that is politically intolerable.\\n\\n(f) President Roh Moo-hyun cannot avoid moral and political responsibility regarding corruption by close associates and obstruction of corruption investigations, and particularly with respect to criminal acts committed through close associates in a co-perpetrator relationship after the commencement of performance of official duties on February 25, 2003, he cannot avoid legal responsibility and therefore has “violated the law in the execution of official duties.” This is because, even after President Roh Moo-hyun began performing the duties of the Presidency on February 25, 2003, he abetted corrupt crimes by Ahn Hee-jung, Choi Do-sool, Yeo Tae-soo, Yang Gil-seung, and others, and thus directly and indirectly participated in these corrupt crimes of the co-perpetrators as co-perpetrators specified in Articles 30, 31, 32, and 33 of the Criminal Act and as an indirect perpetrator under Article 34 of the same Act. On December 29, 2003, the prosecution also publicly stated that it had recognized and confirmed the co-perpetrator relationship between President Roh Moo-hyun and his close associates. However, the prosecution inevitably deferred direct investigation and indictment of President Roh Moo-hyun, stating that “although we have our own conclusion, it would not be appropriate to disclose its content in light of the President’s special privilege against criminal prosecution under the Constitution, the continuity of performance of official duties, and the spirit of the Constitution.” Each time a corruption case involving President Roh as a co-perpetrator came to light, he directly and indirectly influenced the investigation by providing the prosecution with the direction and policy of the investigation, and in order to conceal his own involvement, he has threatened the people with a confidence-reaffirmation card and shaken the nation amid economic hardship. It goes without saying that, in a situation where President Roh, a co-perpetrator of corruption by close associates, is obstructing the investigation, the prosecution cannot be expected to uncover corruption cases involving the so-called “live power.” For this reason, the National Assembly now has no choice but to step forward and impeach President Roh Moo-hyun according to the procedures prescribed by the Constitution and the laws.\\n\\nThird, as evidenced by the fact that our economy remains at an exceptionally low growth rate far below that of the United States despite a worldwide economic boom, President Roh Moo-hyun is causing the national economy and State affairs to collapse, plunging the people’s livelihood into ruin and bringing the people even more severe suffering and misfortune than during the IMF crisis.\\n\\n(a) Economists have characterized the first year of Roh’s rule as “failure in State administration, a lost year,” and even the people who voted for President Roh in the last presidential election have turned their backs on him, producing the alarming phenomenon of a lame duck only one year into his term.\\n\\n(b) The fundamental cause of such collapse in State administration cannot be denied: it lies in President Roh Moo-hyun’s repeated verbal blunders and retractions, beginning with his rash remark, “I cannot continue being President,” his announcement of troop dispatch to Iraq followed by a pro-withdrawal stance on the Iraq war, his unconstitutional proposal for a referendum on reaffirming confidence, and his declaration that he would retire from politics, as well as in his insincere performance of duties and reckless administration that cannot be found to have any seriousness or consistency, and in the so-called “all-in strategy” illegal advance election campaigning in which, while neglecting his duties as President, he poured all efforts solely into the general election.\\n\\n(c) Therefore, President Roh Moo-hyun is now violating Article 10 of the Constitution, which prescribes the people’s “right to pursue happiness” and the “State’s duty to guarantee fundamental rights,” and is neglecting the duty of “faithfully performing the duties of the President” set forth in Article 69 of the Constitution.\\n\\nOur country is now in a crisis of destroying the constitutional order, in which the President denies the rule of law with a supra-constitutional and ultra-legal attitude and ignores the warnings of the National Election Commission, a constitutional organ, and the National Assembly’s inherent authority. The National Assembly, entrusted by Article 65 of the Constitution with the sacred authority to bring impeachment charges, bears the duty to protect the Constitution and the rule of law from President Roh’s arbitrary exercise of power. If the National Assembly turns away from this duty, it will be committing dereliction of duty. Accordingly, Representative Yoo Yong-tae, Representative Hong Sa-deok, and 157 other members of the National Assembly, gathering bipartisan will to uphold the Constitution and the legal order of the State, propose impeachment of President Roh Moo-hyun as the final means to block the President’s unlawful and unconstitutional acts, restore the rule of law, which has been infringed, and thereby ensure the future of the Republic of Korea and the happiness of the people, and in particular to hold the 17th general election in a normal manner."}

question: Which of the following correctly combines the statements that are correct (○) and incorrect (×) regarding the electoral system and suffrage? (Where there is a dispute, according to case law.) (a) The provision of the Public Official Election Act that, with respect to an elector who cannot mark the ballot himself or herself due to a physical disability, if the voting assistant is not a family member, permits assistance in voting only when accompanied by two voting assistants, sets forth an exception to the principle of secret ballot, but does not infringe the right to vote because it maintains the secrecy of the vote by preventing, through criminal punishment, the voting assistant from infringing the secrecy of the elector's vote. (b) The former provision of the Public Official Election Act that criminally punishes campaign activities conducted individually face-to-face and orally before the campaign period infringes the freedom of political expression. (c) The provision of the Public Official Election Act that provides for a single-member district plurality system, under which a person who obtains the majority of valid votes in the relevant National Assembly constituency in an election for a member of the National Assembly from a constituency is determined as the elected person, excludes other electoral systems and therefore infringes the right to equality and the right to vote. (d) In an election for the head of a local government, since the opportunity to attend the interviews and debates that the Election Broadcasting Debate Commission at each level is required to hold must be afforded equally to all candidates, the provision of the Public Official Election Act that restricts eligibility for invitation infringes the right to equality in relation to the principle of equal opportunity for candidates' campaign activities.
