The name, date of birth, sex, and registered domicile of the person subject to revocation\\n2. The grounds for revocation and the year, month, and day thereof"}

{"[2016HEONMA889]": "1. Case Summary\\n\\nThe Claimant was born on 1999. 5. 15. in the United States of America (hereinafter referred to as the “United States”) to a father who was a national of the United States and a mother who was a national of the Republic of Korea. The Claimant acquired the nationality of the Republic of Korea at birth as a person whose mother was a national of the Republic of Korea at the time of birth under Article 2(1) Item 1 of the Nationality Act, and also acquired United States nationality at birth by being born in the territory of the United States, and thus is a multiple-nationality holder who has held both Korean and United States nationality since birth.\\n\\nThe main text of Article 12(2) of the Nationality Act provides that “a person who has been placed in the pre-military service reserve pursuant to Article 8 of the Military Service Act shall choose one nationality within 3 months from the time of placement, or one nationality within 2 years from the time any of the items of Paragraph 3 applies.” Thus, it limits the period during which a person placed in the pre-military service reserve may choose nationality. In addition, according to the proviso of Article 14(1) of the Nationality Act, in the case of a person falling under the main text of Article 12(2), the person may file a declaration with the Minister of Justice of the intent to withdraw from Korean nationality within the period during which the above nationality may be chosen, and if that period has elapsed, a declaration of withdrawal from nationality may not be filed until the military service obligation is discharged. As a male national of the Republic of Korea, the Claimant is in principle obliged to choose one nationality by 2017. 3. 31., which is within 3 months from 2017. 1. 1., the year in which he turned 18 under the Military Service Act, and once that period has passed, he may not file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality until the military service obligation is discharged.\\n\\nMeanwhile, Article 12(2) Item 1 of the Enforcement Rule of the Nationality Act provides that a person filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality shall attach a “certificate concerning registered family relationship matters” when submitting the “declaration form for withdrawal from nationality.” In this regard, in practice, the Minister of Justice requires submission of the declarant’s own Basic Certificate and Family Relation Certificate, as well as the Basic Certificates of the father and mother, etc., pursuant to the “Act on the Registration, etc. of Family Relationships.” Since these documents may be issued for a person whose family relationship register has been prepared through birth registration, etc., a birth registration, etc. must first be completed so that a family relationship register can be prepared in order to file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality. In the Claimant’s case, although he acquired Korean nationality at birth, no birth registration has even been made in the Republic of Korea.\\n\\nThe Claimant seeks to withdraw from Korean nationality, but pursuant to the above provision of the Enforcement Rule of the Nationality Act, a birth registration must first be made in order to file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, and pursuant to the above provisions of the Nationality Act, if 2017. 3. 31. passes, withdrawal from nationality is restricted unless the military service obligation is discharged. Arguing that these provisions infringe his fundamental rights, he filed the constitutional complaint in this case on 2016. 10. 13.\\n\\n2. Subject Matter of Adjudication\\n\\nThe subject matter of adjudication in this case is whether the main text of Article 12(2) of the Nationality Act (as amended by Act No. 14183 on 2016. 5. 29.), the portion concerning the main text of Article 12(2) in the proviso of Article 14(1) of the Nationality Act (as amended by Act No. 10275 on 2010. 5. 4.) (hereinafter, these provisions collectively referred to as the “provisions subject to adjudication of the Act”), and Article 12(2) Item 1 of the Enforcement Rule of the Nationality Act (as amended by Ministerial Decree of the Ministry of Justice No. 817 on 2014. 6. 18.) (hereinafter, the “provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule,” and together with the above provisions subject to adjudication of the Act, the “provisions subject to adjudication”) infringe the Claimant’s fundamental rights. The provisions subject to adjudication and the related provisions are as follows.\\n\\n[Provisions Subject to Adjudication]\\n\\nNationality Act (as amended by Act No. 14183 on 2016. 5. 29.)\\n\\nArticle 12 (Duty of Multiple-Nationality Holder to Choose Nationality) ② Notwithstanding the main text of Paragraph 1, a person who has been placed in the pre-military service reserve pursuant to Article 8 of the Military Service Act shall choose one nationality within 3 months from the time of placement, or one nationality within 2 years from the time any of the items of Paragraph 3 applies. (proviso omitted)\\n\\nNationality Act (as amended by Act No. 10275 on 2010. 5. 4.)\\n\\nArticle 14 (Requirements and Procedures for Withdrawal from Korean Nationality) ① A person who, as a multiple-nationality holder, intends to choose a foreign nationality may file a declaration with the Minister of Justice of the intent to withdraw from Korean nationality through the head of the overseas mission having jurisdiction over the place of domicile only where the person has an address in a foreign country. Provided, that a person falling under the main text of Article 12(2) or Paragraph 3 of the same Article may file such declaration only within that period or from the time the relevant cause arises.\\n\\nEnforcement Rule of the Nationality Act (as amended by Ministerial Decree of the Ministry of Justice No. 817 on 2014. 6. 18.)\\n\\nArticle 12 (Form of Declaration of Withdrawal from Nationality and Attached Documents) ② The documents to be attached to the declaration form for withdrawal from nationality under Paragraph 1 shall be as follows:\\n1. Certificate concerning registered family relationship matters\\n\\n[Related Provisions]\\n\\nNationality Act (as amended by Act No. 16851 on 2019. 12. 31.)\\n\\nArticle 12 (Duty of Multiple-Nationality Holder to Choose Nationality) ① A person who became a multiple-nationality holder before attaining 20 years of age shall choose one nationality pursuant to Articles 13 and 14 by the time he or she attains 22 years of age, and a person who became a multiple-nationality holder after attaining 20 years of age shall choose one nationality pursuant to Articles 13 and 14 within 2 years from that time. Provided, that multiple-nationality holders who, pursuant to Article 10(2), have pledged to the Minister of Justice that they will not exercise foreign nationality in the Republic of Korea shall be excluded.\\n③ A person born while a lineal ascendant was staying in a foreign country without the purpose of permanent residence may file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality under Article 14 only in any of the following cases in connection with the performance of military service obligations:\\n1. Where he or she has completed, or is deemed to have completed, service as an active-duty soldier, a full-time reserve soldier, a supplementary service member, or an alternative service member\\n2. Where he or she has been placed in wartime labor service status\\n3. Where he or she has received a disposition of exemption from military service\\nArticle 14-2 (Order to Choose Nationality for Multiple-Nationality Holders) ① The Minister of Justice shall order a multiple-nationality holder who has not chosen nationality within the period prescribed in Article 12(1) or (2) to choose one nationality within 1 year.\\n④ A person who, despite having been ordered to choose nationality pursuant to Paragraph 1 or 2, fails to comply therewith shall lose Korean nationality when the relevant period has elapsed.\\n\\nMilitary Service Act (as amended by Act No. 14183 on 2016. 5. 29.)\\n\\nArticle 2 (Definitions, etc.) ② Where the time of performance of military service obligations is indicated by age in this Act, “from the age of ○○” means from January 1 of the year in which that age is attained, and “until the age of ○○” means until December 31 of the year in which that age is attained.\\nArticle 8 (Placement in the Pre-Military Service Reserve) Male nationals of the Republic of Korea are placed in the pre-military service reserve from 18 years of age.\\n\\n3. Claimant’s Arguments\\n\\nThe provisions subject to adjudication of the Act violate the principle of due process because they do not provide for individual notice regarding the withdrawal-from-nationality procedure and the effects of noncompliance. In addition, because the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act restrict the period for choosing nationality and provide that, once that period has elapsed, a declaration of withdrawal from nationality may not be filed unless the military service obligation is discharged, they violate the principle against excessive restriction and infringe the freedom to withdraw from nationality, the right to self-determination regarding nationality choice, and the freedom of occupation choice, and discriminate between multiple-nationality holders who have their basis of life in a foreign country and those who have their basis of life in the Republic of Korea, as well as between men and women.\\n\\nThe provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule is unclear as to which specific documents must be submitted in connection with a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, and therefore violates the principle of clarity. In addition, because it compels a birth registration before a declaration of withdrawal from nationality can be filed, it forces an unnecessary procedure, causes the fact that the declarant is a multiple-nationality holder to remain in public records, and makes withdrawal from nationality unduly difficult for multiple-nationality holders who have continuously resided in a foreign country, thereby violating the principle against excessive restriction. Further, it treats a person who acquired multiple nationality at birth, such as the Claimant, less favorably than a person who possessed only Korean nationality and later acquired another nationality, and therefore violates the principle of equality. Accordingly, the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule infringes the Claimant’s fundamental rights.\\n\\n4. Holding\\n\\nA. Restriction on the period for choosing nationality and on declarations of withdrawal from nationality for multiple-nationality holders who are Korean men\\n\\n(1) In principle, a multiple-nationality holder must choose one nationality by age 22 if he or she became a multiple-nationality holder before attaining 20 years of age, and within 2 years from that time if he or she became a multiple-nationality holder after attaining 20 years of age (main text of Article 12(1) of the Nationality Act). However, where a person has been placed in the pre-military service reserve pursuant to Article 8 of the Military Service Act, the person must choose one nationality within 3 months from the time of placement or within 2 years from the time the military service obligation is discharged (main text of Article 12(2) of the Nationality Act). A male national of the Republic of Korea is placed in the pre-military service reserve from 18 years of age, and therefore a multiple-nationality holder who acquired Korean nationality and was placed in the pre-military service reserve before January 1 of the year in which he attains 18 years of age must choose one nationality by March 31, which is 3 months after that date (see Article 2(2) and Article 8 of the Military Service Act).\\n\\n(2) A multiple-nationality holder may voluntarily withdraw from Korean nationality. A multiple-nationality holder who intends to withdraw from Korean nationality shall file a declaration to that effect with the Minister of Justice, and if the declaration of withdrawal from nationality is accepted, Korean nationality is lost (main text of Article 14(1) and Paragraph 2 of the Nationality Act).\\n\\nHowever, a male national of the Republic of Korea who bears the military service obligation may file a declaration of intent to withdraw from Korean nationality within the period during which he may choose nationality as described above, and after that period has elapsed, he may file such declaration only in the case where the military service obligation has been discharged, as set forth in each item of Article 12(3) of the Nationality Act (see the proviso of Article 14(1) of the Nationality Act). In other words, if a multiple-nationality holder who is a male national of the Republic of Korea acquired nationality before January 1 of the year in which he attains 18 years of age, he must file a declaration of intent to voluntarily withdraw from Korean nationality before March 31 of that same year; if he acquired nationality after that date, he must file such declaration within 3 months from the date of acquisition. If he fails to do so, he cannot voluntarily withdraw from Korean nationality until the military service obligation is discharged.\\n\\n(3) To file the above declaration of withdrawal from nationality, the declaration form must be submitted with a certificate concerning registered family relationship matters, documents proving acquisition or possession of foreign nationality, documents proving the reason for and date of acquisition of foreign nationality, and a copy of the foreign passport. In addition, if a male national of the Republic of Korea files a declaration of withdrawal from nationality before March 31 of the year in which he attains 18 years of age, he must attach and submit documents prescribed by the Minister of Justice proving that he was not born while a lineal ascendant was staying in a foreign country without the purpose of permanent residence; if he files such declaration after that date, he must attach and submit documents proving that he has been discharged from the military service obligation (Article 12(1) and (2) of the Enforcement Rule of the Nationality Act).\\n\\n(4) The Minister of Justice shall order a person who, as a multiple-nationality holder, has not chosen nationality within the prescribed period to choose one nationality within 1 year. However, in practice, where a multiple-nationality holder who has been placed in the pre-military service reserve has not chosen one nationality within the nationality-choice period, an order to choose nationality is not, in principle, issued to that person (see Article 14-2 of the Nationality Act).\\n\\n(5) Taken together, the above means that a multiple-nationality holder who is a male national of the Republic of Korea cannot withdraw from Korean nationality until the military service obligation is discharged, unless he files a declaration of intent to voluntarily withdraw from Korean nationality before March 31 of the same year if he acquired nationality before January 1 of the year in which he attains 18 years of age, or within 3 months from the date of acquisition if he acquired nationality after that date.\\n\\n(6) In a case in which it was at issue whether provisions of the Nationality Act (as amended by Act No. 7499 on 2005. 5. 24.)—which required a multiple-nationality holder to choose one nationality within 3 months from the date of placement in the first national service reserve and, if the person did not withdraw from Korean nationality by then, allowed withdrawal only after the military service obligation was discharged—such as the proviso of Article 12(1) and the proviso of Article 14(1), infringed the claimant’s fundamental rights, the Constitutional Court held that the above provisions did not infringe the claimant’s freedom to withdraw from nationality (Constitutional Court 2006. 11. 30. 2005HEONMA739). Thereafter, in a case in which it was at issue whether the main text of Article 12(2) and the proviso of Article 14(1) of the Nationality Act (as amended by Act No. 10275 on 2010. 5. 4.), containing the same content, infringed the claimants’ fundamental rights, it held that the above provisions did not infringe the claimants’ freedom to withdraw from nationality or the right to equality (Constitutional Court 2015. 11. 26. 2013HEONMA805 et al.).\\n\\nB. Fundamental rights restricted and organization of issues\\n\\n(1) Portion concerning the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act\\n\\n(a) The provisions subject to adjudication of the Act impose on multiple-nationality holders who are male nationals of the Republic of Korea a duty to choose nationality while limiting the period therefor, thereby restricting the “freedom to withdraw from nationality,” which allows free departure from Korean nationality (see Constitutional Court 2006. 11. 30. 2005HEONMA739; Constitutional Court 2015. 11. 26. 2013HEONMA805 et al.). Accordingly, we examine whether the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act violate the freedom to withdraw from nationality by contravening the principle against excessive restriction.\\n\\n(b) The Claimant argues that the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act infringe not only the freedom to withdraw from nationality but also the right to self-determination regarding nationality choice and the freedom of occupation. However, since the concept of “freedom to withdraw from nationality” already presupposes the “right to self-determination regarding nationality choice,” there is no practical benefit in separately examining the “right to self-determination regarding nationality choice,” and because the possibility that selection of a particular occupation may be restricted is not a direct disadvantage caused by the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act even according to the Claimant’s assertion, we do not examine whether the freedom of occupation choice is infringed.\\n\\n(c) The Claimant asserts, in substance, that the failure of the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act to provide that multiple-nationality holders be notified of the withdrawal-from-nationality procedure violates the principle of due process. However, because this will be taken into account in determining whether the principle against excessive restriction has been violated, we do not separately examine whether the principle of due process has been violated.\\n\\n(d) The Claimant asserts, in substance, that the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act discriminate between “multiple-nationality holders with an address and basis of life in a foreign country” and “multiple-nationality holders with an address and basis of life in the Republic of Korea,” and between men and women. However, because all of this will be taken into account in determining whether the principle against excessive restriction has been violated, we do not separately examine it.\\n\\n(2) Portion concerning the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule\\n\\n(a) The provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule merely stipulates that a “certificate concerning registered family relationship matters” must be attached as a document to be submitted when filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, and the issue is whether this violates the principle of clarity in relation to what documents it refers to.\\n\\n(b) The provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule indirectly requires, in practice, the submission of documents based on entries in the family relationship register, etc., and thereby indirectly requires persons whose family relationship register has not been prepared to first have a family relationship register prepared pursuant to the “Act on the Registration, etc. of Family Relationships” (hereinafter referred to as the “Family Relationship Registration Act”) through birth registration, etc., before filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality. The issue is whether this violates the principle against excessive restriction as a restriction on the freedom to withdraw from nationality.\\n\\n(c) The Claimant argues that, due to the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule, a person who became a multiple-nationality holder at birth must undergo a more burdensome withdrawal-from-nationality procedure than a person who became a multiple-nationality holder after birth, and therefore the above provision infringes his right to equality. However, the two cannot be set as comparison groups for purposes of equality review, and because the procedural difficulty experienced by a person who became a multiple-nationality holder at birth, as pointed out by the Claimant, may be examined in determining whether the principle against excessive restriction has been violated, we do not separately determine this issue.\\n\\n(3) Conclusion\\n\\nBelow, we first determine whether the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act violate the principle against excessive restriction, and then determine whether the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule violates the principle of clarity and the principle against excessive restriction.\\n\\nC. Whether the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act violate the principle against excessive restriction\\n\\n(1) Legitimate purpose and appropriateness of means\\n\\nThe provisions subject to adjudication of the Act provide that a multiple-nationality holder who has been placed in the pre-military service reserve pursuant to Article 8 of the Military Service Act must choose one nationality within 3 months from the time of placement, and if that period elapses, may not file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, thereby not allowing withdrawal from Korean nationality before the military service obligation is discharged.\\n\\nThe legislative purpose of the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act is to secure fairness in the performance of military service obligations by restricting withdrawal from nationality as a means of evading the military service obligation by a person placed in the pre-military service reserve. Article 39(1) of the Constitution provides that all citizens bear the duty of national defense as prescribed by law, and male nationals are obligated to faithfully perform military service obligations as prescribed by the Constitution and the Military Service Act, etc. (see Article 3(1) of the Military Service Act). Accordingly, the legislative purpose of the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act, which seeks to secure fairness in the performance of military service obligations, is legitimate.\\n\\nIn addition, by limiting the period during which withdrawal from nationality is possible as above, the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act are an appropriate means of achieving the objective of securing fairness in the performance of military service obligations, because they prevent a person placed in the pre-military service reserve from escaping the military service obligation through withdrawal from nationality thereafter.\\n\\n(2) Least restrictive means\\n\\n(a) The provisions subject to adjudication of the Act require a multiple-nationality holder who is a male national of the Republic of Korea to choose one nationality before March 31 of the same year if he acquired nationality before January 1 of the year in which he attains 18 years of age, or within 3 months from the date of acquisition if he acquired nationality after that date, and, unless he files a declaration of intent to withdraw from Korean nationality by then, they impose no exception at all to the effect that he may not withdraw from Korean nationality before the military service obligation is discharged. Despite the fact that the freedom to withdraw from nationality is restricted without exception for male multiple-nationality holders in this manner, no individual notice is given regarding the nationality-choice procedure for multiple-nationality holders or the restrictions arising if the nationality-choice period elapses. The Nationality Act provides that a person whose father or mother was a national of the Republic of Korea at the time of birth acquires Korean nationality at birth without filing any declaration (Article 2(1) Item 1 of the Nationality Act). Taking these circumstances into account, there remains the possibility that multiple-nationality holders who lack sufficient understanding of the fact of acquisition of Korean nationality, the nationality-choice procedure for multiple-nationality holders, and the restriction on withdrawal from nationality under the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act may arise.\\n\\n(b) Depending on the specific circumstances, such as a multiple-nationality holder’s principal base of life or experience of staying or residing in the Republic of Korea, there may be grounds under social norms for finding it difficult to expect a declaration of withdrawal from nationality within the period prescribed by the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act. For example, if a multiple-nationality holder who acquired Korean nationality at birth without filing any declaration has lived with his or her main base of life in a foreign country for study or economic activity, it may be difficult to expect him or her to understand the laws and system of the Republic of Korea concerning acquisition of multiple nationality and withdrawal from nationality. Nevertheless, if, once he or she recognizes that he or she is a multiple-nationality holder and only then seeks to withdraw from Korean nationality, the declaration of withdrawal from nationality is uniformly not permitted before the military service obligation is discharged on the ground that the nationality-choice period has elapsed, this constitutes a substantial restriction on the freedom to withdraw from nationality for reasons for which, under social norms, it is difficult to hold him or her responsible.\\n\\n(c) The legislative purpose of the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act is to secure fairness in the performance of military service obligations, and Constitutional Court precedents have also expressed concern that if such restrictions as those in the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act are not imposed, opportunistic behavior may become widespread, such as multiple-nationality holders enjoying the benefits of being Korean nationals while keeping their basis of life in the Republic of Korea and then withdrawing from nationality when the time comes to perform military service obligations, thereby undermining fairness in the performance of military service obligations (see Constitutional Court 2006. 11. 30. 2005HEONMA739; Constitutional Court 2015. 11. 26. 2013HEONMA805 et al.). However, if the competent authority operates the system by conducting a specific review and, excluding multiple-nationality holders who keep their main base of life in the Republic of Korea and seek to withdraw from nationality at a time close to when they must perform military service obligations, exceptionally permits withdrawal from nationality even after the nationality-choice period has elapsed only where it can be seen that fairness in the performance of military service obligations would not be undermined, such concern can be dispelled.\\n\\n(d) Therefore, even if the nationality-choice period has passed for a multiple-nationality holder who has been placed in the pre-military service reserve, where there are circumstances for which, under social norms, it is difficult to hold that person responsible for failing to file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality within that period, that is, where there exists a justifiable reason, and where it is also objectively recognized that the legislative purpose of securing fairness in the performance of military service obligations would not be undermined, it should not be said that a multiple-nationality holder placed in the pre-military service reserve is uniformly unable to withdraw from nationality merely because the nationality-choice period has elapsed; rather, there is room to devise a means of exceptionally permitting withdrawal from nationality.\\n\\nEven though there are means that would infringe fundamental rights less while not undermining the legislative purpose of “securing fairness in the performance of military service obligations,” the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act do not provide for any such exception and uniformly prevent withdrawal from nationality before the military service obligation is discharged. This violates the principle of minimum restriction.\\n\\n(3) Balance of legal interests\\n\\n(a) The provisions subject to adjudication of the Act seek to secure the public interest of fair performance of military service obligations by absolutely preventing a multiple-nationality holder from withdrawing from nationality before the military service obligation is discharged, even where the person does not wish to retain Korean nationality.\\n\\nHowever, if a multiple-nationality holder mainly resides in a foreign country and has not even had a birth registration made in the Republic of Korea, it is difficult for the Korean Government to identify that person as a citizen, and thus difficult to place that person in the pre-military service reserve in practice; even if that person is somehow placed in the pre-military service reserve, it is difficult in reality to have the person perform military service obligations if he or she does not enter the Republic of Korea. In other words, there are cases where the public interest pursued by the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act is not substantially achieved because the limitation on withdrawal from nationality cannot be matched with actualization of the military service obligation. As cross-border movement of persons becomes more active and marriages between persons of different nationalities continue to increase, under the current approach of the Nationality Act, the number of multiple-nationality holders who do not reside in the Republic of Korea will also continue to increase, and the gap between the normative purpose and reality is likely to widen further.\\n\\n(b) On the other hand, depending on the specific circumstances, the actual disadvantage that the subject must bear by retaining multiple nationality due to the existence of the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act may be considerable. Depending on the country, there is a possibility that a multiple-nationality holder may be restricted from engaging in public office or work directly related to national security, or work that may involve conflicts of interest with the country of the other nationality. Where such restrictions exist in reality, the private-interest infringement arising from restrictions on choosing a particular occupation or performing particular work cannot be regarded lightly.\\n\\n(c) As set forth above, there are cases where the private interest infringed is greater than the public interest achieved through the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act, and in such cases the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act also fail to satisfy the principle of balance of legal interests.\\n\\n(4) Conclusion\\n\\nTaking the above circumstances together, the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act violate the principle against excessive restriction and infringe the Claimant’s freedom to withdraw from nationality.\\n\\nD. Determination regarding the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule\\n\\n(1) Whether the principle of clarity is violated\\n\\n(a) The provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule requires a person filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality to attach and submit a “certificate concerning registered family relationship matters” to the declaration form. The Claimant argues that, by itself, the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule makes it impossible to foresee what documents are required when filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, particularly whether the documents must necessarily be Korean public documents, and therefore violates the principle of clarity.\\n\\n(b) At present, in practice, a person filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality must submit the declarant’s own Basic Certificate and Family Relation Certificate under the Family Relationship Registration Act, the Basic Certificates of the father and mother, and, where the person was born between a Korean-national father and a foreign-national mother, the father’s Marriage Relation Certificate, etc. (hereinafter referred to as the “Basic Certificates, etc.”). Although the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule does not expressly specify this, making it difficult for a person filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality to know exactly which documents are referred to, the nationality and other nationalities acquired by the declarant, sex, nationality of the parents, and other specific circumstances at the time of the filing vary, so it may not be appropriate for the Enforcement Rule to directly specify the names of the attached documents, and it is difficult to conceive of a method other than the present expression, considering the content and evidentiary purpose of the documents to be attached.\\n\\n(c) Although no other statute expressly states what documents are meant by the “certificate concerning registered family relationship matters” prescribed by the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule, the Korean Government introduces and guides this through various means, and even if the declarant does not understand this and fails to submit the Basic Certificates, etc., in practice the declaration form is first received as a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, and the attached documents may later be supplemented, so in this process the Claimant can ascertain what these documents refer to.\\n\\n(d) Taken together, these circumstances show that the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule does not violate the principle of clarity.\\n\\n(2) Whether the principle against excessive restriction is violated\\n\\n(a) Legitimacy of purpose and appropriateness of means\\n\\nAs noted above, the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule requires a declarant filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality to attach and submit a “certificate concerning registered family relationship matters” to the declaration form. Accordingly, the Basic Certificates of the declarant and the Family Relation Certificate, etc., which are required to be submitted in practice, are materials necessary to identify the declarant and to confirm the fact of possession of Korean nationality, which is the premise for withdrawal from nationality. The provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule requires the declarant to attach and submit the necessary documents so that the Minister of Justice may properly process the acceptance of a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, and its legitimacy of purpose is recognized. Through this, the Minister of Justice can obtain the information necessary to determine whether the declarant satisfies the requirements for withdrawal from nationality, and thus the appropriateness of means is also recognized.\\n\\n(b) Least restrictive means and balance of legal interests\\n\\nIn order for the Minister of Justice to accept a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, it is necessary to accurately identify the declarant and to confirm the fact that he or she acquired and possesses Korean nationality as a premise for withdrawal from nationality. Because the circumstances surrounding a declaration of withdrawal from nationality vary, such as the declarant’s place of residence, place and date of birth, age, sex, the process by which Korean nationality was acquired, and whether the father or mother acquired or lost nationality, the Minister of Justice has no choice but to require the declarant to submit standardized and reliable documents in order to accurately determine whether the requirements for withdrawal from nationality are met. The Basic Certificates, etc. under the Family Relationship Registration Act are Korean public documents containing such information, and it is difficult to conceive of another type of document that both sufficiently contains the information necessary for the Minister of Justice to determine whether the requirements are met and is also reliable.\\n\\nThe Claimant argues that, due to the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule, a person who has not filed a birth registration and is a multiple-nationality holder must first file a birth registration in order to obtain the Basic Certificates, etc. Of course, it is true that the documents necessary for a declaration of withdrawal from nationality can be issued only after birth registration is completed, but birth registration is an obligation under the Family Relationship Registration Act borne by the father or mother of the person born (see Article 44(1) and Article 46(1)), and the burden of having to file a birth registration only at the time of filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality is merely a problem arising because the Claimant’s father or mother did not fulfill the obligation to file a birth registration under the Family Relationship Registration Act; it is not that the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule directly imposes the obligation to file a birth registration.\\n\\nIn practice, even when a declarant files a declaration form without attaching the mandatory documents such as the Basic Certificates, etc. under the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule, the declaration is accepted, and documents not submitted or incorrectly submitted are later supplemented upon guidance from the responsible official; even when supplementing, submission by mail or email and submission through an overseas mission are permitted, showing that the Minister of Justice sufficiently considers the convenience of declarants. In light of such practical examples, although the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule requiring the declarant to submit the Basic Certificates, etc. may cause some inconvenience, it cannot be regarded as making withdrawal from nationality virtually impossible.\\n\\nAccordingly, the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule cannot be said to violate the principles of minimum restriction and balance of legal interests.\\n\\n(c) Conclusion\\n\\nThe provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule does not violate the principle against excessive restriction or infringe the Claimant’s freedom to withdraw from nationality.\\n\\nE. Constitutional nonconformity decision and temporary application order regarding the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act\\n\\nThe unconstitutionality of the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act lies in the fact that, where a multiple-nationality holder placed in the pre-military service reserve does not file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality within the nationality-choice period, it restricts, without exception, withdrawal from Korean nationality before the military service obligation is discharged even if the multiple-nationality holder keeps his or her main base of life in a foreign country. The legislature can eliminate the unconstitutionality of the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act by stipulating, in cases involving a multiple-nationality holder who keeps his or her main base of life in a foreign country, that if the person could not file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality within the period prescribed by the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act for justifiable reasons, the requirements and procedures for doing so may exceptionally be provided.\\n\\nHowever, if the Constitutional Court were to render a simple unconstitutional decision on the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act and their effect were to be extinguished immediately, the period limitation on nationality choice or withdrawal from nationality would disappear immediately even in cases where such limitation is justified, and this could create difficulties in securing fairness in the performance of military service obligations.\\n\\nTherefore, a decision of constitutional nonconformity shall be rendered with respect to the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act, and temporary application shall be ordered until the legislature enacts remedial legislation. The legislature shall enact remedial legislation by no later than 2022. 9. 30., and if no remedial legislation is enacted by then, the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act shall lose their effect from 2022. 10. 1.\\n\\n5. Conclusion\\n\\nAmong the petitions in this case, a decision of constitutional nonconformity shall be rendered with respect to the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act, but they shall be applied temporarily until remedial legislation is enacted by the deadline of 2022. 9. 30., and the remaining petition shall be dismissed. Accordingly, the decision is made as set forth in the text of the judgment. The Constitutional Court’s decision of 2006. 11. 30. 2005HEONMA739, which previously held, in a view contrary to the present one, that provisions of the Nationality Act containing the same content as the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act did not violate the Constitution, and the Constitutional Court’s decisions of 2015. 11. 26. 2013HEONMA805 and 2014HEONMA788 (consolidated), are modified to the extent they conflict with the purport of this decision.\\n\\nWith respect to this decision, except for the dissenting opinion of Justice Lee Seon-ae and Justice Lee Mi-seon regarding the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act, as set forth in 6 below, and the dissenting opinion of Justice Lee Seok-tae and Justice Moon Hyung-bae regarding the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule, as set forth in 7 below, the opinions of the remaining participating Justices were unanimous.\\n\\n6. Dissenting Opinion of Justice Lee Seon-ae and Justice Lee Mi-seon regarding the portion on the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act\\n\\nWe believe that the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act do not violate the principle against excessive restriction or infringe the Claimant’s freedom to withdraw from nationality, and therefore state our opinion as follows.\\n\\nA. The Constitutional Court has already decided twice, taking into account the legislative purpose, the need to prevent loss of military manpower and the undermining of the principle of equality in military service burdens, and the degree of regulation affecting multiple-nationality holders, that provisions of the Nationality Act prescribing the same or substantially the same content as the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act do not infringe the freedom of multiple-nationality holders to withdraw from nationality (see Constitutional Court 2006. 11. 30. 2005HEONMA739; 2015. 11. 26. 2013HEONMA805 et al.). The reasons stated by the Constitutional Court in those precedents remain valid in this case as well, as explained below, and we cannot say that there has been a change in circumstances or a need sufficient to alter that judgment.\\n\\nB. In a democratic state, the military service obligation, together with the tax obligation, is necessarily borne by citizens, the members of the state as a political community, for the existence and maintenance of that political community, and promoting national defense through the imposition of the military service obligation can be regarded as a constitutional value inherent in the national community. Article 5(2) and Article 39 of our Constitution clearly state this constitutional value of national defense and the military service obligation (see Constitutional Court 2004. 8. 26. 2002HEONBA13 et al.). Meanwhile, the principle of equality in military service burdens derived from Article 39 of the Constitution, which provides for universal military service, and Article 11 of the Constitution, which provides for the principle of equality, is not only a constitutional demand but also, in our country, a social demand that is stronger and more absolute than in any other society (see Constitutional Court 2006. 11. 30. 2005HEONMA739). Accordingly, the Military Service Act provides that all male nationals of the Republic of Korea bear the military service obligation (Article 3). Male nationals of the Republic of Korea become actual persons subject to the military service obligation by being placed in the pre-military service reserve from 18 years of age (Article 8), and become subject to various regulations and controls under the Military Service Act intended to ensure faithful performance of the military service obligation and to prevent evasion thereof. Therefore, multiple-nationality holders such as the Claimant, as long as they are male nationals of the Republic of Korea, must in principle perform the military service obligation and cannot be free from that burden (see Constitutional Court 2004. 8. 26. 2002HEONBA13).\\n\\nC. Under the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act, the period for filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality by a multiple-nationality holder placed in the pre-military service reserve under the Military Service Act is limited. This is intended to prevent a multiple-nationality holder placed in the pre-military service reserve from evading the military service obligation by leaving Korean nationality through the nationality-choice system under the Nationality Act, and to realize the principle of equality in military service burdens embodied in our Constitution.\\n\\nOn the other hand, even under the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act, the freedom to withdraw from nationality is not completely deprived but only partially restricted. A multiple-nationality holder may freely withdraw from nationality if less than 3 months have passed from the time he or she, upon turning 18 and being placed in the pre-military service reserve, may withdraw from nationality, and withdrawal from nationality is prohibited only thereafter until the military service obligation is discharged. Of course, even if 3 months have passed from the time of placement in the pre-military service reserve, the person may also freely withdraw from nationality once the military service obligation has been discharged, such as by performing military service or receiving exemption therefrom. In the case of a male who became a multiple-nationality holder at birth, such as the Claimant, a declaration of withdrawal from nationality may be filed at any time from the date of birth until March 31 of the year in which he attains 18 years of age, which is a period of about 18 years, so it cannot be said that the period provided is short.\\n\\nIf even such a temporal limitation on withdrawal from nationality were not imposed, a person could evade the military service obligation by withdrawing from Korean nationality at any point during the process for performance of military service obligations, even during military service. This would not only create a major incongruity with the current Military Service Act system, but would also be undesirable in relation to the majority of persons who faithfully perform military service obligations. The provisions subject to adjudication of the Act can be seen as the result of the legislature’s adjustment and balancing, with the constitutional value of national defense and equity in military service on one side and the individual fundamental-right value of withdrawal from nationality on the other, without unilaterally sacrificing either (see Constitutional Court 2006. 11. 30. 2005HEONMA739).\\n\\nD. The majority opinion says that the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act are unconstitutional because even where there exists a justifiable reason why a multiple-nationality holder placed in the pre-military service reserve could not file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality within the nationality-choice period, and where it is objectively recognized that fairness in the performance of military service obligations would not be undermined, it still absolutely prevents withdrawal from Korean nationality before the military service obligation is discharged.\\n\\nHowever, under the majority opinion, the justifiable reason for a multiple-nationality holder placed in the pre-military service reserve’s failure to file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality within the nationality-choice period amounts to not knowing the fact that “as a multiple-nationality holder subject to the Korean Nationality Act, one must file a declaration within a limited period in order to withdraw from Korean nationality,” which is ultimately no different from asserting ignorance of the law as a justifiable reason. Even if the reason for not knowing the above fact is that, as a so-called congenital multiple-nationality holder, the person was not even registered by birth in the Republic of Korea and has his or her main base of life in a foreign country, thereby not receiving notice concerning the imposition of military service obligations or individual notice concerning the nationality-choice procedure or the limitation on the nationality-choice period, it is difficult to say that there are circumstances justifying ignorance of the law, considering that one or both parents are, in most cases, or were, nationals of the Republic of Korea, and that Korean overseas missions continuously provide guidance on the withdrawal-from-nationality system through various methods.\\n\\nAs noted above, the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act are intended to realize the principle of equality in military service burdens demanded by the Constitution, and therefore should not lightly be allowed exceptions to their application on grounds such as that individuals may inevitably have special circumstances without a careful standard based on social consensus. If, without clearly establishing limits in light of the constitutional reality we face, one first opens a path for multiple-nationality holders to evade the military service obligation through a declaration of withdrawal from nationality depending on their specific circumstances, the important constitutional value of equal burden of military service obligations may be greatly undermined. Furthermore, the risk of destabilizing even the foundation of the conscription system by causing various new forms of military service evasion cannot be excluded. The majority opinion suggests that fairness in the performance of military service obligations can be maintained through review by the competent authority, but there remains considerable doubt as to how effectively the many and varied opportunistic behaviors that may arise in relation to military service obligations can be blocked.\\n\\nE. The majority opinion states that, in the case of multiple-nationality holders who are not even registered by birth in the Republic of Korea, there is in reality no room for performance of military service obligations, so under the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act only their freedom to withdraw from nationality is restricted while the public interest sought by the above provisions is not substantially achieved. However, if a multiple-nationality holder enters the Republic of Korea and stays or resides there for a long period due to a change in specific circumstances, that person may be required to perform military service obligations, and therefore it should not be concluded in advance that a multiple-nationality holder in such a case has no possibility of performing military service obligations in the Republic of Korea. Moreover, asking for the elimination of the period limitation on declarations of withdrawal from nationality on the ground that military service obligations may not in fact be imposed is merely an argument that reverses means and ends. In addition, even if the multiple-nationality holder ultimately does not actually perform military service obligations, the public confidence in the fair burden of military service obligations that can be preserved by maintaining the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act is by no means negligible.\\n\\nThe majority opinion also points out that the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act may limit a multiple-nationality holder from performing work in public office or work directly related to national security in another country until the military service obligation is discharged; however, it is questionable whether such restrictions exist generally in most countries, and even if they do exist, they are restrictions imposed by the laws or practices of other countries and should be addressed in those countries.\\n\\nF. In our reality, which has adopted conscription for male nationals of the Republic of Korea, public interest in the fair imposition of military service obligations is higher than anything else, and the antipathy toward any undermining of that fairness is also great. Because the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act contain matters directly connected to the military service obligations borne by multiple-nationality holders, a very cautious approach is required in examining their unconstitutionality.\\n\\nThe reason the Constitutional Court has repeatedly decided that Nationality Act provisions containing content substantially identical to the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act do not violate the Constitution is that fairness in bearing the military service burden is, in our society, an important constitutional value that cannot be abandoned. The judgment the Constitutional Court previously articulated remains valid, and we find it difficult to identify any reason to reach a different conclusion in this case. The principle of equality in military service burdens directly embodied in the Constitution must also remain firmly upheld today. Taken together, the provisions subject to adjudication of the Act cannot be said to infringe the Claimant’s freedom to withdraw from nationality.\\n\\n7. Dissenting Opinion of Justice Lee Seok-tae and Justice Moon Hyung-bae regarding the portion on the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule\\n\\nWe believe that the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule violates the principle against excessive restriction and infringes the Claimant’s freedom to withdraw from nationality, and therefore state our opinion as follows.\\n\\nA. In order for the Minister of Justice to accept a declaration of withdrawal from nationality, it is necessary to accurately identify the declarant and to confirm the fact that he or she acquired and possesses Korean nationality as the premise for withdrawal from nationality, and it is understood that receiving standardized Basic Certificates, etc. under the Family Relationship Registration Act from the declarant makes it easier to confirm whether the requirements for withdrawal from nationality are satisfied.\\n\\nB. Under the current Nationality Act, acquisition of nationality by birth does not require birth registration, and therefore it is possible to acquire and possess nationality without birth registration (see Article 2(1) of the Nationality Act).\\n\\nAccording to the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule and its practice, a multiple-nationality holder such as the Claimant, who acquired Korean nationality at birth but has never had a birth registration, must first go through the birth registration procedure and then obtain the Basic Certificates, etc. through relatives in the Republic of Korea or a Korean overseas mission and attach them to the declaration form for withdrawal from nationality in order to withdraw from Korean nationality. If he or she has lived and stayed in a foreign country for most of his or her life, it can be sufficiently anticipated that such a person would face considerable difficulty in understanding and carrying out these procedures.\\n\\nUnder the current Nationality Act, a male multiple-nationality holder who acquired nationality before January 1 of the year in which he attains 18 years of age must file a declaration of withdrawal from nationality by March 31 of that year. If he is a minor and is in a situation where it is difficult to receive assistance from a father or mother who is a national of the Republic of Korea, these difficulties become greater and may be harsh, considering that he has, regardless of his own will, acquired Korean nationality as a matter of course by reason of birth. This does not merely cause procedural inconvenience for multiple-nationality holders, but may, depending on circumstances such as place of residence, ease of visiting a Korean overseas mission, and the degree of understanding of Korean law or the Korean language, lead them to ultimately abandon the filing of a declaration of withdrawal from nationality.\\n\\nFurthermore, from the perspective of a multiple-nationality holder, the process of filing a declaration of withdrawal from nationality leaves a record in the Korean family relationship register of the person’s acquisition and possession of multiple nationality, and a person conscious of the de facto disadvantages arising from holding multiple nationality may, for that reason, be reluctant to file such declaration from the outset.\\n\\nC. It is possible to confirm the relevant matters through other means without receiving the Basic Certificates, etc. under the Family Relationship Registration Act, which can only be issued once the declarant’s own birth registration has first been made. For example, the Minister of Justice, the competent authority for declarations of withdrawal from nationality, can identify the declarant by receiving the multiple-nationality holder’s foreign passport or equivalent foreign public document, and can confirm the fact of Korean nationality acquisition and possession by receiving, together with the Basic Certificates, etc. of the father or mother who acquired Korean nationality, foreign-issued documents that can verify the declarant’s birth and family relationship.\\n\\nIn this way, the Minister of Justice must establish criteria as to what other explanatory documents, rather than the Basic Certificates, etc. under the Family Relationship Registration Act, will be accepted in order to determine whether the declarant satisfies the requirements for withdrawal from nationality, and must examine, in processing the declaration of withdrawal from nationality, whether the documents submitted sufficiently substantiate the matter. This may create an administrative burden for the Minister of Justice, but it is necessary to sufficiently guarantee the freedom to withdraw from nationality for multiple-nationality holders such as the Claimant by opening the path for a declaration of withdrawal from nationality without necessarily undergoing the birth registration procedure.\\n\\nAccordingly, the provision subject to adjudication of the Enforcement Rule fails to satisfy the requirements of minimum restriction and balance of legal interests, and therefore violates the principle against excessive restriction and infringes the Claimant’s freedom to withdraw from nationality."}

question: Which of the following statements concerning the constitutional principle of responsibility is NOT correct? (In case of dispute, according to case law)
A: A provision of the former Ship Safety Act that stipulates that, where a captain employed by a shipowner commits a criminal act in relation to the shipowner’s business, the same fine shall also be imposed on the shipowner violates the principle of responsibility, because it imposes criminal punishment on the shipowner merely on the ground that the captain employed by the shipowner committed a criminal act in relation to his duties, without at all providing for the shipowner’s independent responsibility for the consequences of the act committed by the captain.
B: A provision of the Labor Standards Act that, where a construction subcontractor who has not registered as a construction business fails to pay wages to workers, imposes on the immediate upper-tier contractor an obligation to pay wages jointly and severally with the subcontractor and punishes the immediate upper-tier contractor if it fails to perform that obligation, cannot be regarded as violating the principle of self-responsibility.
C: A provision of the former Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party that requires the head of each central administrative agency to restrict the qualification for participation in bidding, within the extent prescribed by Presidential Decree and not exceeding 2 years, for a person, etc. who is likely to undermine the fair execution of competition or the proper performance of a contract does not violate the principle of self-responsibility, because it enables the disqualified contractor to escape the sanction disposition by proving, among other things, that the act serving as the cause of the sanction disposition cannot be attributed to him or her.
D: A provision of the National Health Insurance Act that allows the National Health Insurance Service to collect all or part of an amount equivalent to the benefit costs from a medical care institution that has received insurance benefit costs by fraud or other wrongful means does not run counter to the principle of responsibility, because, even if the medical care institution has fulfilled its duty of care to manage and supervise its employees, the insurance benefit costs have once accrued to the medical care institution, and once that medical care institution has received insurance benefit costs by fraud or other wrongful means, it has an obligation to return unjust enrichment.
E: A provision of the Act on the Management of Mountainous Districts that directly punishes a corporation, together with employees, etc., for certain criminal acts committed by employees, etc. employed by the corporation cannot readily be regarded as violating the principle of responsibility because it punishes the corporation’s negligence in failing to fulfill its own duty of direction and supervision.
label: E

Case Overview\\n\\n(1) Case 2010HEONGA19\\n\\n(a) In the underlying case, a summary order was sought against the defendant, ○○ Steel Co., Ltd., on the facts charged that “its employee, Seo ○Seok, in relation to the business of the company, while obtaining permission for conversion of mountainous district land and carrying out civil engineering works from around the middle of February 2009 to
